236.rest: — "'And Avraham weighed out the silver (kesef) to Efron' — this is the great yearning (kisufa), which is worlds and yearnings. 'Four hundred shekels of silver' — four hundred worlds of delights and yearnings. 'Current with the merchant' — that it may pass through all the gates of heaven and the heavenly Jerusalem, and none may hinder it."

237.label: Sefer Yetzirah 4:11
237.rest: — "He made the letter Tav king, bound a crown to it, and formed with it [a planet] in the world, the Shabbos day in the year, and the mouth in the soul."

238.label: Kiddushin 40a–41a
238.rest: — "…and a good person is given a taste of the fruit of his deeds [in this world]."

239.label: Berachos 17a
239.rest: — "When the Rabbis took leave of the house of Rabbi Ami — some say, of Rabbi Chanina — they said to him: May you see your world in your lifetime, and may your end be for the life of Olam Haba, and your hope for all generations; may your heart meditate understanding, your mouth speak wisdom, and your eyes shine with the light of Torah."

240.label: Tanchuma, Ki Savo 4
240.rest: — "Rabbi Levi said: The Torah need not have been given to Israel in this world, since all are destined to learn Torah from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, in Olam Haba. Why was it given to them in this world? So that when the Holy One comes to teach them in Olam Haba, all will know which portion He is dealing with."

241.label: Taanis 5b
241.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He was asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He answered: I am expounding a verse, as it says, 'And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov… for behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity' (Yirmeyahu 30:10) — it compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive." Rashi: he lives forever; they embalmed him because they thought he had died.

242.label: Yerushalmi, Pe'ah 2:4
242.rest: — "Many halachos were said to Moshe at Sinai, and all of them are embedded in the Mishnah."

243.label: Kesubos 103b
243.rest: — "On the day of Rebbi's passing a heavenly voice went forth and said: Whoever was present at Rebbi's passing is destined for the life of Olam Haba. A certain launderer used to come before him every day; that day he did not come. When he heard this he went up to a roof, fell to the ground and died. A heavenly voice went forth: That launderer too is destined for the life of Olam Haba."

244.label: Berachos 4b
244.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Who is a ben Olam Haba? One who joins redemption (geulah) to the evening prayer." There too: "Whoever says Tehillah L'David (Tehillim 145) three times each day is assured that he is a ben Olam Haba."

245.label: Berachos 9b
245.rest: — "Rabbi Ila said to Ulla: When you go there, ask after the welfare of my brother Rav Beruna in the presence of the whole group, for he is a great man and rejoices in mitzvos: once he joined redemption to prayer, and laughter did not leave his mouth the whole day."

246.label: Bava Basra 10b
246.rest: — "Rabbi Abahu said: They asked Shlomo: Who is a ben Olam Haba? He said to them: One before whose elders there is honor (Yeshayahu 24:23)." There too, Yosef the son of Rabbi Yehoshua, who had seen the next world in illness: "I saw an upside-down world: the upper ones below and the lower ones above."

247.label: Kiddushin 32b
247.rest: — "Rabbi Yosi HaGlili says: zakein [an elder] is only one who has acquired wisdom, as it says: 'Hashem acquired me [kanani] at the beginning of His way' (Mishlei 8:22)." Rashi: he expounds zakein as zeh shekanah, "this one acquired"; so even a young man who is wise.

248.label: Berachos 17a
248.rest: — "When the Rabbis took leave of the house of Rabbi Ami — some say, of Rabbi Chanina — they said to him: May you see your world in your lifetime, and may your end be for the life of Olam Haba, and your hope for all generations; may your heart meditate understanding, your mouth speak wisdom, and your eyes shine with the light of Torah."

249.label: Zohar II 166b (Terumah)
249.rest: — "The primordial light is ready to bring forth offspring for the World to Come. And if you say, for the World to Come and no more — rather, even on each and every day; for were it not for this light the world could not endure, as it is written, 'I said, the world is built on kindness' (Tehillim 89:3)."

250.label: Sefer Yetzirah 4
250.rest: — "He made the letter tav king… and formed with it… the day of Shabbos in the year, and the mouth in the soul."

251.label: Shabbos 152a
251.rest: — "'For man goes to his eternal home' (Koheles 12:5). Rabbi Yitzchak said: This teaches that each and every tzaddik is given a dwelling according to his honor. A parable: a king entered a city with his servants. When they enter, they all enter by one gate; when they lodge, each is given a dwelling according to his honor."

252.label: Eruvin 54b
252.rest: — "'And those who walk' — these are the masters of Scripture; 'on the way' — the masters of Mishnah; 'converse (sichu)' — these are the masters of Talmud, for all their conversation is words of Torah." Rashi has no comment on this passage.

253.label: Zohar III (Tzav)
253.rest: — "And so Torah scholars, the children of the King and Queen, are called Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim; they have nothing of their own, for they are not craftsmen like other weekday servants; their reward, in this world and the World to Come, is to be delighted with every kind of food and drink and honored with fine garments, like Shabbos."

254.label: Tanchuma, Noach 3
254.rest: — "'According to (al pi) these words' (Shemos 34:27) — this is the Oral Torah, which is hard to learn and involves great suffering, and it is likened to darkness, as it says, 'The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light' (Yeshayahu 9:1): these are the masters of the Talmud, who have seen a great light, for the Holy One, blessed be He, illuminates their eyes in what is forbidden and permitted, impure and pure."

255.label: Zohar I 135b (Midrash HaNe'elam, Toldos)
255.rest: — The righteous who did not merit so much "delight in that radiance," without full grasp; but the righteous who merited more are "nourished" until they reach complete attainment.

256.label: Tanchuma, Tetzaveh 9
256.rest: — "'The wise shall inherit honor' (Mishlei 3:35)… You find thirty-six generations from Adam until Yaavetz, and in none of them is 'honor' written except for Yaavetz, as it says, 'And Yaavetz was more honored than his brothers' (I Divrei HaYamim 4:9). Why? Because he was a Torah scholar who gathered congregations and expounded the reasons of the Torah in public."

257.label: Temurah 16a
257.rest: — “Rav Judah said in the name of Samuel: Three thousand laws were forgotten during the mourning for Moses. They said to Joshua: Ask! He answered them: ‘It is not in heaven.’ ... It was taught: One thousand seven hundred a-fortiori inferences, analogous-word derivations, and details of scribal law were forgotten during the mourning for Moses. Rabbi Avahu said: Nevertheless, Osniel ben Kenaz restored them through his dialectical analysis, as it is said: 'Osniel ben Kenaz, Kalev's brother, captured it, and he gave him Achsah his daughter as a wife.'” The preceding teaching specifies that seventeen hundred inferences, analogies, and fine points of the Scribes were forgotten during the mourning for Moshe. Later the Gemara identifies Osniel with Yaavetz and interprets Yaavetz as one who advised and disseminated Torah in Israel. Rav Tzadok sees the restoration through analysis as a birth of Oral Torah precisely at the time of loss.

258.label: Berachos 7a
258.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosi: From where do we know that the Holy One prays? As it says, 'I will bring them to My holy mountain and gladden them in the house of My prayer' (Yeshayahu 56:7) — it does not say 'their prayer' but 'My prayer.' From here, that the Holy One prays."

259.label: Zohar III, Pinchas (Ra'aya Meheimna)
259.rest: — "The Holy One, blessed be He, is hidden in the secrets of the Torah. How is He known? Through the mitzvos, which are His Shechinah, His image: as He is humble, His Shechinah is humility; He is pious and she is piety…; He is truth (emes) and she is faith (emunah); He is righteous and she is righteousness; He is King and she is kingship."

260.label: Pesachim 56a
260.rest: — “Yaakov sought to reveal the end of days to his sons, but the Shechinah departed from him. He said: Perhaps, Heaven forbid, there is a disqualification among my children, as Avraham had Yishmael and my father Yitzchak had Esav. His sons said to him: ‘Hear, Israel, Hashem is our God, Hashem is One.’ They said: Just as there is only One in your heart, so there is only One in our hearts. At that moment Yaakov our father began and said: ‘Blessed is the name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever.’” The words are addressed to their father Israel. The sons affirm the same exclusive allegiance to the One whom Yaakov knows; Rav Tzadok explains their unity of faith without assuming an identical degree of revelation.

261.label: Taanis 15a
261.rest: — "Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I too say: not all are for light and not all are for gladness. The righteous are for light, and the upright for gladness: the righteous for light, as it is written, 'Light is sown for the righteous' (Tehillim 97:11); and the upright for gladness, as it is written, 'and for the upright of heart, gladness.'"

262.label: Sanhedrin 98a
262.rest: — "Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi found Eliyahu standing at the entrance of the cave of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. He said to him: Will I come to the World to Come? He said: If this Master wills it."

263.label: Sanhedrin 98a
263.rest: — "He went to [Mashiach] and said: Peace upon you, my master and teacher. He said: Peace upon you, son of Levi. He said: When will the master come? He said: Today. He came to Eliyahu, who asked: What did he tell you? — 'Peace upon you, son of Levi.' He said: He has assured you and your father of the World to Come… He said: This is what he told you: 'Today — if you will hearken to His voice' (Tehillim 95:7)." Rashi: had you not been perfect tzaddikim he would not have greeted you and mentioned your father.

264.label: Taanis 5b
264.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He was asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He answered: I am expounding a verse, as it says, 'And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov… for behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity' (Yirmeyahu 30:10) — it compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive." Rashi: he lives forever; they embalmed him because they thought he had died.

265.label: Bava Metzia 114b
265.rest: — Rabbah bar Avuha found Eliyahu standing in a cemetery of idolaters and asked him, "Is the master not a Kohen? Why is the master standing in a cemetery?" — for Eliyahu is identified with Pinchas the Kohen.

266.label: Kesubos 77b
266.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan proclaimed: Beware of the flies of those afflicted with ra'asan… Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi would attach himself to them and occupy himself with Torah. He said: 'A loving hind and a graceful doe' (Mishlei 5:19) — if it bestows grace on those who learn it, will it not protect them?" The Gemara goes on to relate how he entered Gan Eden alive.

267.label: Megillah 15a
267.rest: — "As Ulla said: Wherever a person's name and his father's name are given in prophecy, it is known that he is a prophet the son of a prophet."

268.label: Tanchuma, Metzora 9
268.rest: — "'Like the impurity of a niddah was their way before Me' (Yechezkel 36:17) — like the impurity of a niddah and not like the impurity of a corpse: when a corpse is in the house the Kohen Gadol does not enter there; but with a niddah the Kohen Gadol may enter with her." And: just as a niddah becomes impure and then pure, so the Holy One will purify Israel.

269.label: Shabbos 31b
269.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: She corrupted [the world] in the chambers of her womb; therefore she is stricken in the chambers of her womb."

270.label: Tanchuma, Metzora 9
270.rest: — "Niddah: the Holy One, blessed be He, said: She spilled the blood of Adam, and it is written, 'Whoever spills the blood of man, by man shall his blood be spilled' (Bereishis 9:6); she is liable to have her blood spilled — let her guard her niddah, so that she is atoned for the blood she spilled."

271.label: Niddah 64b
271.rest: — "Rabbi Chiya taught: Just as leaven is good for dough, so is blood good for a woman. It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir: Any woman whose blood is abundant, her children are abundant."

272.label: Berachos 17a
272.rest: — "Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will. And who prevents us? The leaven in the dough and the subjugation to the kingdoms." Rashi: the leaven in the dough is the evil inclination in our hearts, which sours us.

273.label: Berachos 34a
273.rest: — "Our Rabbis taught: Three things — much of them is bad and a little is good: leaven, salt, and refusal."

274.label: Eruvin 100b
274.rest: — "'To the woman He said: I will greatly increase (harbah arbeh)' (Bereishis 3:16) — these are two drops of blood: one the blood of niddah and one the blood of besulim; 'your pain' — the pain of raising children; 'and your conception' — the pain of pregnancy; 'in pain you shall bear children' — as it sounds."

275.label: Shabbos 89b
275.rest: — “If your sins are like these years, which are arranged and come from the six days of creation until now, they will be made white as snow.”

276.label: Nedarim 22b
276.rest: — “Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Yehoshua… as it says, ‘For in much wisdom is much anger’ (Koheles 1:18).”

277.label: Tanchuma, Noach 2
277.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah HaLevi said: When a person departs the world without children, he is distressed and weeps. The Holy One says to him: Why do you weep — because you produced no fruit in the world? You have fruit more beautiful than children. He says: Master of the world, what fruit did I produce? He says: The Torah, in which it is written, 'The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life' (Mishlei 11:30)."

278.label: Niddah 65b
278.rest: — "Rabbi Meir used to say: The appearances of the bloods differ: the blood of niddah is red, the blood of besulim is not red; the blood of niddah is putrid, the blood of besulim is not putrid; the blood of niddah comes from the source, the blood of besulim from the sides."

279.label: Berachos 4b
279.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Why is there no nun in Ashrei? Because it contains the downfall of the enemies of Israel, as it is written, 'She has fallen and will no more rise, the maiden (besulas) of Israel' (Amos 5:2)." In Eretz Yisrael they read it: "She has fallen and will no more fall; rise, maiden of Israel."

280.label: Niddah 31b
280.rest: — "Rabbi Meir used to say: Why did the Torah say that a niddah is for seven days? Because he is used to her and comes to loathe her. The Torah said: let her be impure seven days, so that she will be as beloved to her husband as at the time she entered the chuppah."

281.label: Zohar Chadash, Balak
281.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar opened: 'Since you became precious (yakarta) in My eyes, you are honored, and I have loved you' (Yeshayahu 43:4). It should have said 'since you are precious (yakar)'! What is 'yakarta'? It implies that he became precious through himself: whoever is guilty before the Holy One is at first despised before Him; after he reconsiders and returns from his sin, he becomes precious of himself."

282.label: Berachos 34b
282.rest: — "Rabbi Abahu said: In the place where baalei teshuvah stand, perfect tzaddikim cannot stand, as it says, 'Peace, peace to the far and to the near' (Yeshayahu 57:19) — first to the far, and then to the near."

283.label: Zohar III 16b (Vayikra)
283.rest: — "Therefore we learned: in the place where baalei teshuvah sit, perfect tzaddikim do not sit. Why? Because they are established in a higher place, the place from which the watering of the garden comes, which is Teshuvah; therefore they are called 'masters of teshuvah'; while these are established in another place, called Tzaddik."

284.label: Zohar II 184a (Tetzaveh)
284.rest: — "There is no light except that which comes out of darkness: for when this side is subdued, the Holy One, blessed be He, ascends above and is glorified in His glory. There is no service of the Holy One except from within darkness, and no good except from within evil."

285.label: Zohar II 60a (Beshalach)
285.rest: — "'And they went three days in the wilderness and found no water' (Shemos 15:22) — and water means only Torah, as it says, 'Ho, all who are thirsty, go to the water' (Yeshayahu 55:1). Rabbi Yeisa said: But who gave them Torah here? Until now the Torah had not yet been given to them!"

286.label: Sotah 42b
286.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: [Goliath was] the son of a hundred fathers (papei) and one mother (nanai)." Rashi: many men came to his mother in one night.

287.label: Berachos 35b
287.rest: — “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said: Whoever benefits from this world without a blessing is as though he robs the Holy One, blessed be He, and the congregation of Israel, for it is said: One who robs his father and mother and says there is no transgression is a companion to a destructive man. His father means the Holy One, blessed be He ... and his mother means the congregation of Israel, as it is said: Hear, my son, the instruction of your father, and do not forsake the Torah of your mother.” Rav Tzadok borrows the identification of mother with the collective source. The immediate Talmudic setting is the obligation to bless before benefiting from the world.

288.label: Pesachim 118b
288.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: What is meant by 'He settles the barren woman of the house' (Tehillim 113:9)? Knesses Yisrael said before the Holy One: Master of the world, Your children have made me like a weasel that dwells in the foundations of houses." Rashi: through their many sins in exile.

289.label: Rashi, Devarim 32:8
289.rest: — "'According to the number of the Children of Israel' — corresponding to the number of the seventy souls of the Children of Israel who went down to Egypt, He set the boundaries of the peoples: seventy languages."

290.label: Nedarim 32a
290.rest: — "Another explanation: Great is milah, for were it not for milah, heaven and earth would not endure, as it says, 'If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set the ordinances of heaven and earth' (Yirmeyahu 33:25)."

291.label: Sanhedrin 99b
291.rest: — Menasheh said: "Had Moshe nothing to write but 'And Lotan's sister was Timna' (Bereishis 36:22), 'and Timna was a concubine to Eliphaz,' and 'Reuven went in the days of the wheat harvest and found dudaim in the field' (Bereishis 30:14)? A heavenly voice went forth: 'You sit and speak against your brother' (Tehillim 50:20)."

292.label: Berachos 6a
292.rest: — "Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rav Chiya bar Avin: These tefillin of the Master of the world — what is written in them? He said: 'And who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land' (I Divrei HaYamim 17:21)."

293.label: Zohar II 204a (Vayakhel)
293.rest: — “Shabbos: shin–bas. The shin is the secret of the three Avos, who unite with the only daughter, and she is crowned with them.”

294.label: Zohar III 257a (Ra'aya Meheimna)
294.rest: — "'And the Children of Israel shall keep the Shabbos' (Shemos 31:16). The Shechinah is called Shabbos on account of three supernal levels, which are the Shin: three crowns, Kesser, Chochmah and Binah; and she is the Bas (daughter), a fourth to them. In the six days, from Chesed to Yesod, work is done…; but from Binah upward it is rest, delight and cessation of all work."

295.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
295.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

296.label: Megillah 19b
296.rest: — "Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: What is meant by 'and upon them, according to all the words that Hashem spoke with you on the mountain' (Devarim 9:10)? This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Moshe the fine points of the Torah, the fine points of the Sofrim, and what the Sofrim would in the future innovate."

297.label: Shabbos 101b
297.rest: — "Rav Safra said to him: Moshe, you have spoken well!" — addressing Rav Moshe, the great scholar of his generation, by the name of Moshe.

298.label: Zohar III 11b (Vayikra)
298.rest: — "Come and see: ten utterances for the work of Creation, as we learned, 'With ten utterances the world was created'; ten utterances for the giving of the Torah — the Ten Commandments. It is written, 'I am Hashem your God' (Shemos 20:2), and in the work of Creation, 'Let there be light, and there was light' (Bereishis 1:3) — this is the faith of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called 'light.'"

299.label: Rosh Hashanah 32a
299.rest: — "[The ten verses of each blessing correspond to what?]… Rav Yosef said: Corresponding to the Ten Commandments that were said to Moshe at Sinai. Rabbi Yochanan said: Corresponding to the ten utterances with which the world was created."

300.label: Sotah 44a
300.rest: — "The Torah taught proper conduct: that a person should build a house, plant a vineyard, and afterwards marry a wife. And Shlomo said in his wisdom, 'Prepare your work outside, make it ready for yourself in the field, and afterwards build your house' (Mishlei 24:27): 'prepare your work outside' — a house; 'make it ready in the field' — a vineyard; 'afterwards build your house' — a wife."

301.label: Tanchuma, Noach 3
301.rest: — "In the second portion it is written, 'with all your heart and with all your soul' (Devarim 11:13), and it does not say 'with all your might,' to teach you that whoever loves wealth and pleasure cannot learn the Oral Torah, for it involves great suffering and loss of sleep; therefore its reward is in the World to Come, as it says, 'The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light' (Yeshayahu 9:1)."

302.label: Tanchuma, Noach 3
302.rest: — Israel accepted the Written Torah willingly, but not the Oral Torah, which requires toil and suffering; and for it the Holy One held the mountain over them like a barrel. The Oral Torah is not found with one who seeks the pleasures of the world.

303.label: Berachos 17a
303.rest: — "Rava used to say: The goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, so that a person should not read and learn and then kick at his father, mother, teacher… as it says, 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem; good understanding to all who do them.'" Rashi: the essence of Torah is that repentance and good deeds accompany it.

304.label: Avodah Zarah 3a
304.rest: — "Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: What is meant by 'which I command you today to do them' (Devarim 7:11)? Today to do them, and not tomorrow to do them; today to do them, and not today to receive reward." Rashi: today — in this world; not tomorrow — for they cannot be done in the World to Come.

305.label: Berachos 17a
305.rest: — "When the Rabbis took leave of the house of Rabbi Ami — some say, of Rabbi Chanina — they said to him: May you see your world in your lifetime, and may your end be for the life of Olam Haba, and your hope for all generations; may your heart meditate understanding, your mouth speak wisdom, and your eyes shine with the light of Torah."

306.label: Kiddushin 40a–41a
306.rest: — "…and a good person is given a taste of the fruit of his deeds [in this world]."

307.label: Berachos 5a
307.rest: — "Whoever is able to occupy himself with Torah and does not, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings upon him ugly sufferings that disturb him, as it says, 'I was mute with silence, I was still from good, and my pain was stirred' (Tehillim 39:3) — and 'good' means only Torah, as it says, 'For I have given you good teaching; do not forsake My Torah' (Mishlei 4:2)."

308.label: Pesachim 50b
308.rest: — "Rava contrasted: It is written, 'For Your kindness is great unto the heavens' (Tehillim 57:11), and it is written, 'great above the heavens' (Tehillim 108:5). Here, for those who do it lishmah; there, for those who do it not lishmah — as Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: A person should always occupy himself with Torah and mitzvos even not lishmah, for from not lishmah he comes to lishmah."

309.label: Eruvin 100b
309.rest: — "'To the woman He said: I will greatly increase (harbah arbeh)' (Bereishis 3:16) — these are two drops of blood: one the blood of niddah and one the blood of besulim; 'your pain' — the pain of raising children; 'and your conception' — the pain of pregnancy; 'in pain you shall bear children' — as it sounds."

310.label: Sanhedrin 38b
310.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: [Adam] drew his foreskin forward, as it is written here, 'But they, like Adam, transgressed the covenant' (Hoshea 6:7), and it is written there, 'he has broken My covenant' (Bereishis 17:14)."

311.label: Eruvin 18b
311.rest: — “Rabbi Yirmiyah ben Elazar said: During all the years that Adam was under a ban he begot spirits, demons and lilin, as it says, ‘Adam lived one hundred and thirty years and begot in his likeness, after his image’—implying that until then he had not begotten after his image. Rabbi Meir said: Adam was greatly pious. When he saw that death had been decreed through him, he fasted for one hundred and thirty years, separated from his wife for one hundred and thirty years, and wore a belt of fig branches for one hundred and thirty years.” The Gemara reconciles the accounts by explaining that the former refers to involuntary emission. Its description of the 130 years is the background here; the connection with the sale of Yosef is Rav Tzadok’s further interpretation.

312.label: Zohar II 23a (Vaera)
312.rest: — "Whoever is circumcised is called a tzaddik, as it is written, 'Your people are all tzaddikim; they shall inherit the land forever' (Yeshayahu 60:21). Whoever is circumcised and guards this sign of the covenant is called a tzaddik."

313.label: Niddah 13b
313.rest: — "[Those who 'sport with children'] — shall we say this means relations with males? They are liable to stoning! Rather, it means by way of limbs: they are like the generation of the Flood." Rashi: that is, wasting seed.

314.label: Niddah 73a
314.rest: — "The school of Eliyahu taught: Whoever studies halachos every day is assured that he is a ben Olam Haba, as it says, 'The ways (halichos) of the world are His' (Chavakuk 3:6) — read not halichos but halachos."

315.label: Berachos 17a
315.rest: — "When the Rabbis took leave of the house of Rabbi Ami — some say, of Rabbi Chanina — they said to him: May you see your world in your lifetime, and may your end be for the life of Olam Haba, and your hope for all generations; may your heart meditate understanding, your mouth speak wisdom, and your eyes shine with the light of Torah."

316.label: Bava Basra 16b–17a
316.rest: — "Three the Holy One gave a taste in this world of the World to Come: Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov. Avraham, as it is written of him, 'with everything (bakol)' (Bereishis 24:1); Yitzchak, 'from everything (mikol)' (27:33); Yaakov, 'everything (kol)' (33:11)."

317.label: Zohar I 129a (Chayei Sarah)
317.rest: — "When he grew old and entered the supernal levels as is fitting, as it is written, 'And Avraham was old,' then he 'came into days' — into those supernal days, the days known in the secret of faith; 'and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything (bakol)' — from where all blessings and all good issue."

318.label: Megillah 28b
318.rest: — "We learned there: 'And one who makes use of the crown (taga) passes away.' Reish Lakish taught: This is one who makes use of one who studies halachos, the crown of the Torah."

319.label: Rashi, Shemos 31:3
319.rest: — "'With wisdom' — what a person hears from others and learns; 'and with understanding' — that he understands a matter from his own heart, from what he has learned; 'and with knowledge' — ruach hakodesh."

320.label: Bava Basra 12a
320.rest: — "From the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed, prophecy was taken from the prophets and given to the Sages… Abaye said: Know that this is so, for a great man says something, and the same is then reported in the name of another great man." The Ramban there infers that the Sages' teaching comes through a form of ruach hakodesh.

321.label: Menachos 29b
321.rest: — "When Moshe ascended on high, he found the Holy One, blessed is He, tying crowns to the letters. He said: Master of the world, who holds back Your hand? He said: There is one man at the end of many generations, Akiva ben Yosef is his name, who will expound upon every crownlet heaps upon heaps of halachos." Rashi: crowns — the tagin of a Sefer Torah.

322.label: Zohar III, Pinchas (Ra'aya Meheimna)
322.rest: — "Shlomo said: Binah is Moshe's; I will ask for the supernal Chochmah, which is above his level. What is written? 'I said, I will become wise, but it is far from me' (Koheles 7:23). But is it not written, 'And Hashem gave wisdom to Shlomo' (I Melachim 5:26)? A small wisdom… for even to Binah no man in the world can ascend except Moshe — all the more so above it."

323.label: Zohar I 207a (Vayigash)
323.rest: — "What is 'heavens'? The secret of the Patriarchs, and the secret of the Patriarchs is Yaakov, who includes them all, for Yaakov is the choicest of the Patriarchs... And because he ascended into the World to Come, one beautiful branch went out from him, from which all lights go out: Yosef the tzaddik, who gives sustenance to the whole world."

324.label: Taanis 5b
324.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He was asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He answered: I am expounding a verse, as it says, 'And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov… for behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity' (Yirmeyahu 30:10) — it compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive." Rashi: he lives forever; they embalmed him because they thought he had died.

325.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13, 29a
325.rest: — "When the sukkah is complete, it is said of Yaakov, 'And Yaakov came whole' (Bereishis 33:18); and Yaakov is certainly the image of the middle pillar from the outside. But was not Moshe there? Rather, he was there from the inside: this one from the body, and that one from the soul."

326.label: Sotah 12a
326.rest: — “When Moshe was born, the whole house was filled with light.”

327.label: Rosh Hashanah 21b
327.rest: — "'Koheles sought to find words of delight' (Koheles 12:10) — Koheles sought to be like Moshe. A heavenly voice went forth and said to him: 'And written uprightly, words of truth' — 'And there arose no more a prophet in Israel like Moshe' (Devarim 34:10)."

328.label: Zohar III, Pinchas (Ra'aya Meheimna)
328.rest: — "'For the conductor, upon the eighth' (Tehillim 12:1) — that Netzach should not move from Hod, which is the eighth sefirah. The Holy Luminary said: If so, Binah is your level; why then did they explain, 'and He gave the Hod to Moshe,' as it says, 'You shall put of your majesty (hod) upon him' (Bamidbar 27:20)?"

329.label: Yoma 28b
329.rest: — "Rav said: Avraham Avinu fulfilled the entire Torah, as it says, 'Because Avraham listened to My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes and My Torahs' (Bereishis 26:5). Rav Shimi bar Chiya said to Rav: Perhaps only the seven mitzvos? — There was milah too! — Perhaps seven and milah? — If so, why 'My commandments and My Torahs'?"

330.label: Zohar III 80b–81a (Kedoshim)
330.rest: — "He said to him: 'The fear of Hashem' is written, not Torah! He answered: So it is indeed, for the Torah comes from the side of Gevurah… as it is written, 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem' (Tehillim 111:10)." Yitzchak, the "Fear of Yitzchak," is the chariot of Gevurah.

331.label: Berachos 5b
331.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Granted Torah and kindness, as it is written, 'Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned' (Mishlei 16:6): 'kindness' is acts of kindness… and 'truth' is Torah, as it is said, 'Buy truth and do not sell it' (Mishlei 23:23)."

332.label: Nedarim 38a
332.rest: — "Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Chanina said: The Torah was given only to Moshe and his seed, as it says, 'Write for yourself' (Shemos 34:27), 'Carve for yourself' (34:1) — just as the chips are yours, so is the writing yours; but Moshe dealt generously with it and gave it to Israel… Rather, it was only the pilpul [the dialectic] that was given to him."

333.label: Zohar III 53b (Metzora)
333.rest: — "What is between Moshe and Aharon — which is higher? Moshe: Moshe is the groomsman of the King, Aharon the groomsman of the Matronita. A parable: a king gave his noble consort a groomsman to adorn her and look after the house; when that groomsman enters before the King, he enters only with the Matronita, as it is written, 'With this (zos) shall Aharon come' (Vayikra 16:3)."

334.label: Zohar III 152b (Ra'aya Meheimna)
334.rest: — "The Shechinah is the first Pesach from the right and the second Pesach from the left: the first Pesach from the right, where Chochmah is; the second Pesach from the left, where Binah is. And because in Gevurah all foreign fires, which are like straw and chaff before the fire of Gevurah, are consumed, the impure are deferred to the second Pesach."

335.label: Berachos 26b
335.rest: — "Avraham instituted the morning prayer, as it says, 'And Avraham rose early in the morning to the place where he had stood' (Bereishis 19:27), and 'standing' means only prayer, as it says, 'And Pinchas stood and prayed' (Tehillim 106:30)."

336.label: Sanhedrin 99b
336.rest: — “Reish Lakish said: Whoever teaches his fellow's son Torah is regarded by Scripture as though he made him, as it is said: 'The souls they made in Charan.' Rabbi Elazar says: As though he made the words of Torah, as it is said: 'You shall keep the words of this covenant and do them.' Rava said: As though he made himself, as it is said: 'And do them'—do not read 'them,' but 'you.'” The verse quoted for Rabbi Elazar's statement is Deuteronomy 29:8. Rav Tzadok explains the making of Torah as bringing its understanding into a heart in which it was not previously present.

337.label: Zohar III 110b, Behar
337.rest: — “Come and see: 'Trust in Hashem and do good.' What is 'do good'? We have learned that through an act below, an act above is aroused. They have explained 'and you shall do them': as it were, you make them, because through the awakening that you produce below, an awakening is produced above. Therefore it is written, 'do good.' Good refers to the righteous one, as it is written: 'Say of the righteous one that he is good.'” The Zohar describes an effective awakening above produced by observance below. Rav Tzadok applies this pattern to the making of words of Torah. The traditional folio is tracked by the retrieved text's Vilna-page markers.

338.label: Zohar II, Beshalach 64b
338.rest: — “Rabbi Abba said: What is meant by ‘Is the Lord in our midst, or nothing?’ Were Israel fools who did not know this matter? Had they not seen the Divine Presence before them and the clouds of glory surrounding them? ... Rather, Rabbi Shimon said this: They wished to know the difference between the Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, who is called Nothing, and Zeir Anpin, who is called the Lord. ... Why, then, were they punished? Because they made a separation and put it to a test. They said: If it is this One, we will ask in one manner; if it is this One, we will ask in another manner. Therefore, immediately, ‘Amalek came.’” The Zohar interprets Israel's question at Massah as a question about the degree from which Divine governance was being revealed. It explicitly names the concealed Atika as Ayin.

339.label: Shabbos 88a
339.rest: — “Rabbi Simai expounded: When Israel placed 'We will do' before 'We will hear,' six hundred thousand ministering angels came, and tied two crowns to each individual of Israel, one corresponding to 'We will do' and one to 'We will hear.' When Israel sinned, twelve hundred thousand destructive angels descended and removed them, as it says: 'The children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Chorev.' Rabbi Yochanan said: Moshe merited them all and took them. Reish Lakish said: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will return them to us, as it says: 'Those redeemed by Hashem will return and come to Zion with song, with everlasting joy upon their heads'—the joy that had been upon their heads from of old. Rabbi Elazar said: When Israel placed 'We will do' before 'We will hear,' a heavenly voice went forth: 'Who revealed to My children this secret used by the ministering angels?' For it is written: 'Bless Hashem, His angels, mighty in strength, who perform His word, to hear the voice of His word'—first performing, and afterward hearing.” This is the source both for the two crowns and for the angelic precedence of doing over hearing. Its account of Moshe receiving the lost crowns and their eventual restoration also underlies the ensuing discussion.

340.label: Sukkah 25b
340.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak says: If they were the bearers of Yosef's coffin, they could have purified themselves in time; if Mishael and Eltzafan, they could have purified themselves. Rather, they were occupied with a meis mitzvah whose seventh day fell on Erev Pesach."

341.label: Zohar III 152b (Ra'aya Meheimna)
341.rest: — "Every impurity — niddah, metzora, zav, zavah and a woman after childbirth — is burned in the fire of Gevurah. For the soul is a vessel of the Holy One, blessed be He, and He does not dwell in it until it is whitened in the fire of Gevurah, as it is written, 'Is not My word like fire, says Hashem?' (Yirmeyahu 23:29): in this fire, if it is iron it shatters, and if stone it melts."

342.label: Zohar III 105b (Emor)
342.rest: — "In the days of Rabbi Shimon a person would say to his fellow, 'Open your mouth and let your words shine'; after he passed away they said, 'Do not let your mouth bring sin' (Koheles 5:5). In his days — 'to eat to satiety'; after he passed away — 'and for covering the Ancient' (Yeshayahu 23:18), for the companions stammered and could not stand on the matters."

343.label: Bava Metzia 115a
343.rest: — "Shall we say that Rabbi Yehudah does not expound the reason of the verse and Rabbi Shimon expounds the reason of the verse?" — Rabbi Shimon's known method is to expound the reasons behind the Torah's commandments.

344.label: Pesachim 119a
344.rest: — "What is 'and for covering the Ancient (mechaseh atik)' (Yeshayahu 23:18)? This is one who covers the things that the Ancient of Days covered — and what are they? The secrets of the Torah. And some say: this is one who reveals the things that the Ancient of Days covered — and what are they? The reasons of the Torah." Rashi: the secrets are Maaseh Merkavah and Maaseh Bereishis.

345.label: Zohar III, Pinchas (Ra'aya Meheimna)
345.rest: — "When he [David] reached the three upper sefiros, he opened and said: 'Hashem, my heart was not haughty, nor were my eyes raised, nor did I pursue matters too great and too wondrous for me' (Tehillim 131:1)."

346.label: Berachos 17a
346.rest: — “May you see your world in your lifetime, and may your end be life in the World to Come, your hope for every generation. May your heart meditate understanding, your mouth speak wisdom, and your tongue utter songs. ... May your eyes shine with the light of Torah and your face radiate like the brightness of the firmament; may your lips express knowledge, your innermost parts rejoice in uprightness, and your steps run to hear the words of the Ancient of Days.” This blessing distinguishes seeing one's world during life from one's final life in the World to Come. Its conjunction of understanding, speech, song, and the Ancient of Days particularly illuminates Rav Tzadok's present interpretation.

347.label: Zohar III 81a (Kedoshim)
347.rest: — "He said to him: There is no Torah without Chochmah, and no Chochmah without Torah, and all is on one level and all is one; but the Torah is found in supernal Chochmah, and in it it stands, and in it its roots are planted on every side."

348.label: Chagigah 11b
348.rest: — "One might think a person may ask what was before the world was created; the verse teaches, 'from the day that God created man upon the earth' (Devarim 4:32)."

349.label: Zohar I, Vayigash
349.rest: — "Because he [Yaakov] is of the male side more than all people of the world, he endured in his existence more and did not die like the rest of the world; for he is entirely from the Tree of Life and not from the dust, and therefore he ascended above."

350.label: Zohar III, Pinchas (Ra'aya Meheimna)
350.rest: — "Hei rises with Yud five times ten, to the fifty gates of Binah… Afterwards Tzaddik came and took all fifty gates by himself, to be equal to all five, and is called Kol, for he took all fifty gates; and likewise the Kallah took them all."

351.label: Zohar III 61a (Acharei Mos)
351.rest: — "When this 'zos' is blessed from the supernal place, which is called kodesh and called Chochmah, it is called ruach hakodesh — that is, a spirit (ruach) from that kodesh above. And when the secrets of Torah go forth and are aroused from it, it is called lashon hakodesh."

352.label: Yevamos 49b
352.rest: — "As it was taught: All the prophets gazed through a lens that does not shine; Moshe Rabbeinu gazed through a lens that shines."

353.label: Zohar III, Acharei Mos
353.rest: — "Come and see: Yud is first, the totality of all, hidden on every side… The crownlet of the Yud above alludes to Ayin. Afterwards Yud brought forth that river that flows and issues from it, so that Hei should conceive from it, as it is written, 'And a river goes out of Eden' (Bereishis 2:10)."

354.label: Zohar III 65b (Acharei Mos)
354.rest: — "The Yud at first is the totality of all, hidden on every side... The upper tip of the Yud alludes to Ayin (Nothingness)." Zohar III 10b (Vayikra): "The Yud of the holy Name is tied with three knots: one tip above, one below and one in the middle. The tip above is Kesser Elyon, highest of all the highest, head of all heads."

355.label: Berachos 29a
355.rest: — "But we learned: Do not trust yourself until the day of your death, for Yochanan the Kohen Gadol served in the High Priesthood eighty years and in the end became a Tzeduki."

356.label: Avos D'Rabbi Nosson 5
356.rest: — The students of Antignos's students reasoned, "Is it possible that a laborer should work all day and not take his wage in the evening? Had our fathers known that there is another world and a resurrection of the dead, they would not have said so"; they separated from the Torah, and from them came Tzadok and Baisos.

357.label: Berachos 54a (Mishnah)
357.rest: — "All the closings of blessings in the Beis HaMikdash would say 'until the world'; when the Tzedukim corrupted and said there is only one world, they instituted that they say 'from the world and until the world.'"

358.label: Sanhedrin 90a (Mishnah)
358.rest: — "All Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it says, 'And your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands to be glorified' (Yeshayahu 60:21). And these have no share in the World to Come: one who says there is no resurrection of the dead from the Torah, that the Torah is not from Heaven, and an apikoros."

359.label: Sanhedrin 21b
359.rest: — "Rabbi Yosi says: Ezra was fit for the Torah to be given through him to Israel, had Moshe not preceded him. Of Moshe it says, 'And Moshe went up to God' (Shemos 19:3); of Ezra it says, 'He, Ezra, went up from Bavel' (Ezra 7:6): just as the going up there was for Torah, so the going up here was for Torah."

360.label: Sanhedrin 21b
360.rest: — "Rabbi Yosi says: Ezra was worthy that the Torah be given to Israel through him, had Moshe not preceded him. Of Moshe it says, 'And Moshe went up to God' (Shemos 19:3), and of Ezra, 'He, Ezra, went up from Bavel' (Ezra 7:6): just as the going up there was for Torah, so the going up here was for Torah."

361.label: Sukkah 52a
361.rest: — "Abaye said: If it were someone who hates me, he could not have restrained himself. He went and leaned against the doorpost in distress. An old man came and taught him: Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than he." Rashi: he was speaking of himself.

362.label: Kiddushin 81a
362.rest: — "Rabbi Akiva would mock transgressors. One day the Satan appeared to him as a woman at the top of a palm tree. He grabbed the palm and began to climb. When he reached halfway, [the Satan] let him go and said: Were it not that they proclaim in heaven, 'Beware of Rabbi Akiva and his Torah,' I would have valued your life at two ma'ah."

363.label: Bava Basra 17a
363.rest: — "Three over whom the evil inclination had no power: Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, as it is written of them 'with everything' (bakol), 'from everything' (mikol), 'everything' (kol). And some say: David too, as it is written, 'and my heart is slain within me' (Tehillim 109:22)." Rashi: they lacked no good at all.

364.label: Sotah 21a
364.rest: — “‘When you lie down it shall guard you’—this is death; ‘and when you awake it shall speak with you’—in the World to Come.”

365.label: Sanhedrin 99b
365.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: Every person was created for toil, as it says, 'For man is born to toil' (Iyov 5:7). I do not know whether for toil of the mouth or of labor; when it says, 'for his mouth urges him on' (Mishlei 16:26), it is toil of the mouth. And I still do not know whether toil of Torah or of conversation; when it says, 'This book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth' (Yehoshua 1:8), he was created for the toil of Torah."

366.label: Berachos 35b
366.rest: — "'And you shall gather your grain' (Devarim 11:14) — why is this said? Because it says, 'This book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth' (Yehoshua 1:8), one might think the words are as written; the verse teaches, 'and you shall gather your grain': conduct yourself with them in the way of the world — the words of Rabbi Yishmael."

367.label: Berachos 21a
367.rest: — "And Rabbi Yochanan said: If only a person would pray the entire day."

368.label: Shabbos 11a
368.rest: — "Companions who were occupied with Torah interrupt for Krias Shema but do not interrupt for prayer. Rabbi Yochanan said: This was taught only of such as Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his companions, whose Torah is their occupation; but such as we interrupt for Krias Shema and for prayer."

369.label: Rosh Hashanah 35a
369.rest: — "Rav Yehudah would pray only once in thirty days." Rashi: he would review his learning throughout the thirty days, and since his Torah was his occupation he was exempt from prayer in the interval.

370.label: Bava Basra 75b
370.rest: — "Rabbah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: The righteous are destined to be called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, 'Everyone who is called by My Name, and for My glory I created him, formed him, even made him' (Yeshayahu 43:7)."

371.label: Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer 11
371.rest: — When the creatures saw Adam, they feared him, thinking he was their Creator, and came to bow down to him. He said to them: "Why do you bow to me? Come, you and I, let us clothe in majesty and might the One who created us," and he proclaimed, "Hashem reigns; He is clothed in majesty" (Tehillim 93:1).

372.label: Kesubos 5a
372.rest: — "Bar Kappara expounded: The deeds of the righteous are greater than the making of heaven and earth. Of heaven and earth it is written, 'Also My hand founded the earth' (Yeshayahu 48:13), while of the work of the hands of the righteous it is written, 'The Sanctuary, my Lord, that Your hands established' (Shemos 15:17)." Rashi: one hand there; here two hands — the Sanctuary is the handiwork of the righteous.

373.label: Zohar I 27a
373.rest: — The Holy One places one who repents and toils in Torah "in His garden, which is the Shechinah, 'to work it' — with positive mitzvos, 'and to guard it' — with negative mitzvos." Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 21 (62a), says the same of Adam: "'to work it' — with positive commandments, 'and to guard it' — with negative commandments."

374.label: Shabbos 119a–b
374.rest: — "Rabbi Zeira would go around after the Rabbis [who were learning on Shabbos] and say to them: Please, I beg you, do not desecrate it." Rashi: when he saw them in pairs speaking words of Torah, he would say: go and occupy yourselves with the delight of Shabbos, and do not desecrate it by neglecting its delights.

375.label: Yerushalmi, Shabbos 15:3
375.rest: — "Rabbi Chaggai said in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman: Shabbasos and Yamim Tovim were given only for eating and drinking; because the mouth is burdened, they permitted it to occupy itself with words of Torah. Rabbi Berechyah said in the name of Rabbi Chiya bar Ba: Shabbasos and Yamim Tovim were given only to occupy oneself in them with words of Torah."

376.label: Shabbos 119b
376.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: From where do we know that speech is like action? For it says, 'By the word of Hashem the heavens were made' (Tehillim 33:6)."

377.label: Berachos 63b
377.rest: — "'The pressing of anger brings forth strife' (Mishlei 30:33)… In whom do you find the butter of Torah? In one who spits out over it the milk he nursed from his mother's breasts."

378.label: Berachos 17a
378.rest: — "Rava used to say: The goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, so that a person should not read and learn and then kick at his father, mother, teacher… as it says, 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem; good understanding to all who do them.'" Rashi: the essence of Torah is that repentance and good deeds accompany it.

379.label: Kiddushin 40b
379.rest: — "Rabbi Tarfon and the elders were once reclining in the upper chamber of the house of Nitzah in Lod, and this question was asked before them: Is study greater, or is action greater? Rabbi Tarfon answered: Action is greater. Rabbi Akiva answered: Study is greater. All answered and said: Study is greater, for study leads to action." Rashi: so both are in his hand.

380.label: Sanhedrin 106b
380.rest: — "And Rav Yehudah would take off one shoe and the rain would come, while we cry out and no one pays attention to us. But the Holy One, blessed be He, wants the heart, as it is written, 'and Hashem sees into the heart' (I Shmuel 16:7)."

381.label: Sanhedrin 106b
381.rest: — "The Holy One (other texts: the Merciful One) wants the heart, as it says, 'And Hashem sees into the heart' (I Shmuel 16:7)."

382.label: Berachos 61a
382.rest: — "Rav said: The evil inclination resembles a fly and sits between the two openings of the heart, as it says, 'Dead flies make the perfumer's oil putrid' (Koheles 10:1). Shmuel said: It resembles a kind of wheat (chitah), as it says, 'Sin (chatas) crouches at the door' (Bereishis 4:7)."

383.label: Kiddushin 30b
383.rest: — "I created the evil inclination; I created Torah as its antidote… The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: My son, if this repulsive one accosts you, drag him to the beis midrash: if he is stone, he will melt; if he is iron, he will shatter, as it says, 'Is not My word like fire, says Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?' (Yirmeyahu 23:29)." Rashi: "this repulsive one" is the evil inclination provoking you.

384.label: Yerushalmi, Berachos 2:4
384.rest: — "Rabbi Chiya Rabbah said: In all my days I never concentrated [in prayer]; once I wished to concentrate, and I thought in my heart: who goes in first before the king, the arkafta or the reish galusa? Shmuel said: I counted birds. Rabbi Bun bar Chiya said: I counted the rows of the building. Rabbi Masnia said: I am grateful to my head, for when it reaches Modim it bows by itself."

385.label: Kiddushin 40a
385.rest: — "Whoever is confronted with a forbidden relation and is saved from it, a miracle is done for him… 'Mighty in strength, who do His word, to hearken to the voice of His word' (Tehillim 103:20) — such as Rabbi Tzadok and his companions." Rashi: he clothed himself in strength to subdue his inclination to the will of his Maker.

386.label: Chullin 89a
386.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: What is meant by 'Do you indeed speak righteousness in silence?' (Tehillim 58:2) What should a person's occupation be in this world? Let him make himself like a mute. One might think even regarding words of Torah — the verse teaches, 'speak righteousness.' One might think he may become proud — the verse teaches, 'judge uprightly, sons of men.'"

387.label: Avodah Zarah 18b
387.rest: — "Lest a person say: Since I did not go to theaters and circuses and did not stand at the arena, I will go and indulge in sleep — the verse teaches, 'and in His Torah he meditates day and night' (Tehillim 1:2)."

388.label: Berachos 33a
388.rest: — Havdalah is said in the blessing "Who graciously grants knowledge": "since it is a matter of wisdom, they instituted it in the blessing of wisdom." And: "Great is knowledge, for it was placed between two Names, as it says, 'For a God of knowledge is Hashem' (Shmuel I 2:3)."

389.label: Shabbos 55b
389.rest: — "Was she the daughter of Nachash? Was she not the daughter of Yishai, as it is written, 'and their sisters were Tzeruyah and Avigail' (I Divrei HaYamim 2:16)? Rather, she was the daughter of one who died only through the counsel of the serpent." Rashi: through the serpent's counsel to Chavah, not through any sin of his own.

390.label: Zohar I 137b (Toldos)
390.rest: — "'And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh' (Yechezkel 36:26). What is a heart of flesh? Rabbi Yehudah said: A heart to bring forth flesh."

391.label: Taanis 5b
391.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He was asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He answered: I am expounding a verse, as it says, 'And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov… for behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity' (Yirmeyahu 30:10) — it compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive." Rashi: he lives forever; they embalmed him because they thought he had died.

392.label: Berachos 32a
392.rest: — "Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: Were it not for three verses, the feet of Israel's enemies would have slipped: one, 'and whom I have harmed' (Michah 4:6); one, 'Behold, like clay in the hand of the potter, so are you in My hand, house of Israel' (Yirmeyahu 18:6); and one, 'I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh' (Yechezkel 36:26)."

393.label: Kiddushin 30b
393.rest: — "I created the evil inclination; I created Torah as its antidote… The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: My son, if this repulsive one accosts you, drag him to the beis midrash: if he is stone, he will melt; if he is iron, he will shatter, as it says, 'Is not My word like fire, says Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?' (Yirmeyahu 23:29)." Rashi: "this repulsive one" is the evil inclination provoking you.

394.label: Yoma 75b
394.rest: — "'Man ate the bread of the mighty (abirim)' (Tehillim 78:25) — bread that the ministering angels eat; the words of Rabbi Akiva. When this was said before Rabbi Yishmael, he said: Go and tell Akiva: Akiva, you erred! Do the ministering angels eat bread? Is it not said, 'I did not eat bread or drink water' (Devarim 9:9)? Rather, 'abirim' means bread absorbed in the 248 limbs (evarim)."

395.label: Berachos 32a
395.rest: — "Rav Acha son of Rav Huna said in the name of Rav Sheshes: This is what people say: A full belly breeds wicked deeds, as it says, 'As they were fed they became sated; they were sated and their heart grew haughty; therefore they forgot Me' (Hoshea 13:6)."

396.label: Yoma 75b
396.rest: — "Rather, how do I uphold 'And you shall have a spade among your gear' (Devarim 23:14)? It refers to the things that the merchants of the nations sold them" — for the manna itself was entirely absorbed in the body.

397.label: Kesubos 111b
397.rest: — "'For Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth shall cast out the dead' (Yeshayahu 26:19): whoever makes use of the light of Torah, the light of Torah revives him."

398.label: Shabbos 88b
398.rest: — "Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: At each utterance that came from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the souls of Israel left them, as it says, 'My soul went out when He spoke' (Shir HaShirim 5:6). If their souls left at the first utterance, how did they receive the second? He brought down the dew with which He will revive the dead in the future and revived them, as it says, 'A generous rain You shed, O God' (Tehillim 68:10)."

399.label: Sukkah 52a
399.rest: — "Abaye said: If it were someone who hates me, he could not have restrained himself. He went and leaned against the doorpost in distress. An old man came and taught him: Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than he." Rashi: he was speaking of himself.

400.label: Shabbos 105b
400.rest: — "One who tears his garments in his anger, breaks his vessels in his anger, or scatters his money in his anger should be in your eyes like an idolater; for such is the craft of the evil inclination: today it tells him 'do this,' tomorrow 'do that,' until it tells him 'go worship idols,' and he goes and worships."

401.label: Niddah 13b
401.rest: — "Rabbi Ami said: He is called a transgressor, for such is the craft of the evil inclination: today it tells him 'do this,' tomorrow 'do that,' and the next day 'go worship idols,' and he goes and worships."

402.label: Sanhedrin 63b
402.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: Israel knew that idolatry has no substance, and they worshipped idols only to permit themselves forbidden relations openly." Rashi: their inclination overpowered them for forbidden relations, not for idolatry.

403.label: Megillah 17b
403.rest: — "And why did they see fit to place healing as the eighth blessing? Rabbi Acha said: Because circumcision, which requires healing, was given on the eighth day, therefore they set it as the eighth."

404.label: Sanhedrin 38b
404.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: [Adam] drew his foreskin forward, as it is written here, 'But they, like Adam, transgressed the covenant' (Hoshea 6:7), and it is written there, 'he has broken My covenant' (Bereishis 17:14)."

405.label: Taanis 7a
405.rest: — "Rabbi Chanina bar Idi said: Why are the words of Torah likened to water, as it is written, 'Ho, all who are thirsty, go to the water' (Yeshayahu 55:1)? To tell you: just as water leaves a high place and goes to a low place, so the words of Torah endure only in one whose mind is humble."

406.label: Shabbos 31b
406.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: The Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world but the fear of Heaven alone, as it says, 'And now, Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you but to fear' (Devarim 10:12); and it is written, 'And He said to man: Behold (hen), the fear of Hashem is wisdom' (Iyov 28:28) — for in Greek they call 'one' hen."

407.label: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah 3
407.rest: — "David the King further said: I feared out of my joy, and I rejoiced out of my fear, and my love rose above them all."

408.label: Berachos 2b
408.rest: — "From when does one recite the Shema in the evening? From when the poor man comes in to eat his bread with salt, until he rises to leave his meal."

409.label: Nedarim 31a
409.rest: — "But there is Yishmael! — 'For through Yitzchak offspring shall be called yours' (Bereishis 21:12). But there is Esav! — 'through Yitzchak,' and not all of Yitzchak."

410.label: Berachos 5a
410.rest: — "R. Shimon bar Yochai says: The Holy One gave Israel three good gifts, and gave all of them only through suffering: Torah, Eretz Yisrael and the World to Come." Rashi (on "Fortunate is the man whom You chasten… and teach from Your Torah"): through suffering a person must come to Torah study.

411.label: Bava Basra 100a
411.rest: — "With what did the public acquire it according to Rabbi Eliezer? By walking, as it was taught: one who walked in it along its length and its breadth acquires the place of his walking — the words of Rabbi Eliezer."

412.label: Zohar II 170b (Terumah)
412.rest: — When Israel came to the sea, Rahav, the prince appointed over Egypt, came and sought judgment: "Master of the world, why do You judge Egypt and split the sea for Israel? All of them are guilty before You: these worship stars and constellations and those worship stars and constellations; these are immoral and those are immoral; these shed blood and those shed blood."

413.label: Chullin 89a
413.rest: — "'Not because you are more numerous than all the peoples did Hashem desire you' (Devarim 7:7): The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: I desire you, for even when I bestow greatness upon you, you diminish yourselves before Me."

414.label: Taanis 8b
414.rest: — "Rabbah bar Shila said: A day of rain is as harsh as a day of judgment. Ameimar said: Were it not that the world needs it, we would pray for mercy and have it annulled." Rashi: for travelers are distressed by it.

415.label: Zohar III 273a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Eikev)
415.rest: — "The third: to eat three meals on Shabbos, as the masters of the Mishnah established — one of them said, 'May my portion be with those who complete three meals on Shabbos'… The secret of the delight is 'And a river goes out of Eden to water the garden' (Bereishis 2:10)… 'Then you shall delight in Hashem' (Yeshayahu 58:14)."

416.label: Shabbos 119a
416.rest: — "The emperor said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya: Why does the Shabbos dish have a fragrant aroma? He said: We have a certain spice called Shabbos that we put into it, and its aroma spreads. He said: Give us some of it. He said: For whoever keeps the Shabbos it helps; for one who does not keep the Shabbos it does not help."

417.label: Tamid 32b
417.rest: — "As he went on, he sat by a certain spring and ate bread. He had salted fish with him; when they were washed in it, a fragrance came upon them. He said: Learn from this that this spring comes from Gan Eden."

418.label: Sanhedrin 58b
418.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: An idolater who rested [on Shabbos] is liable to death, as it says, 'And day and night they shall not cease' (Bereishis 8:22)… Ravina said: Even on a Monday."

419.label: Sanhedrin 71b (Mishnah)
419.rest: — "Dispersal for the wicked is pleasant for them and pleasant for the world; for the righteous, bad for them and bad for the world… Quiet for the wicked is bad for them and bad for the world; for the righteous, pleasant for them and pleasant for the world."

420.label: Yevamos 63a
420.rest: — "Rabbi Yosi found Eliyahu and said to him: It is written, 'I will make him a helper' (Bereishis 2:18) — how does a woman help a man? He said: A man brings wheat — does he chew wheat? Flax — does he wear flax? Is she not found to light up his eyes and set him on his feet?"

421.label: Shabbos 118b
421.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: Whoever gives delight to the Shabbos is granted the wishes of his heart, as it says, 'Delight in Hashem, and He will give you the wishes of your heart' (Tehillim 37:4). This delight — I do not know what it is; when it says, 'And you shall call the Shabbos a delight' (Yeshayahu 58:13), it is the delight of Shabbos." Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: he is saved from the subjugation of the exiles.

422.label: Shabbos 118b
422.rest: — "Rabbi Yosi said: In all my days I never called my wife 'my wife' or my ox 'my ox,' but my wife 'my home' and my ox 'my field.'" Rashi: she is the essence of the home, and the ox the essence of the field.

423.label: Sanhedrin 90a
423.rest: — “All Israel has a share in the World to Come, as it is said: Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to glory. These are the ones who have no share in the World to Come: one who says that resurrection of the dead is not taught in the Torah, that Torah is not from Heaven, and an apostate.” The Mishnah states both the general promise and specified exclusions. Rav Tzadok's subsequent discussion concerns the ultimate repair of those whom the cited sources treat as excluded; it does not erase the Mishnah's distinctions.

424.label: Eruvin 21b
424.rest: — "'Good figs' (Yirmeyahu 24) — these are the completely righteous; 'bad figs' — the completely wicked. And lest you say their hope is lost, the verse teaches, 'The dudaim give forth fragrance' (Shir HaShirim 7:14): both these and those are destined to give forth fragrance."

425.label: Rambam, Hilchos Gerushin 2:20
425.rest: — One whom the law requires to divorce and who refuses is struck by the beis din until he says "I want to," and the divorce is valid: for every Jew wants to be part of Israel, to do all the mitzvos and keep away from transgressions, and only his inclination overpowered him; once he is struck until his inclination weakens and he says "I want to," he has divorced of his own will.

426.label: Sukkah 52b
426.rest: — "Rava said: At first the evil inclination is called a traveler, then a guest, and finally a man (master of the house), as it says, 'And a traveler came to the rich man… [to prepare] for the guest who had come to him… and he prepared it for the man who had come to him' (Shmuel II 12:4)."

427.label: Shabbos 119a
427.rest: — "Rabbi Chanina would wrap himself and stand at nightfall on Erev Shabbos and say: Come, let us go out to greet Shabbos the Queen. Rabbi Yannai would put on his garments on Erev Shabbos and say: Come, O bride; come, O bride."

428.label: Yoma 72b
428.rest: — "Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What is meant by 'Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?' (Mishlei 17:16)? Woe to Torah scholars who occupy themselves with Torah but have no fear of Heaven."

429.label: Zohar III 221b (Pinchas; cf. Shelach III 161b)
429.rest: — "The Holy One made Israel the heart of the whole world; and Israel among the other nations are like the heart among the limbs… and likewise Jerusalem among the other lands is like the heart among the limbs, and therefore it is in the middle of the whole world."

430.label: Zohar III 273a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Eikev)
430.rest: — "The third: to eat three meals on Shabbos, as the masters of the Mishnah established — one of them said, 'May my portion be with those who complete three meals on Shabbos'… The secret of the delight is 'And a river goes out of Eden to water the garden' (Bereishis 2:10)… 'Then you shall delight in Hashem' (Yeshayahu 58:14)."

431.label: Berachos 26b
431.rest: — "The prayers were instituted corresponding to the daily offerings… The evening prayer has no fixed time, for the limbs and fats that were not consumed by evening are offered all night long."

432.label: Zohar III 110b, Behar
432.rest: — “Come and see: 'Trust in Hashem and do good.' What is 'do good'? We have learned that through an act below, an act above is aroused. They have explained 'and you shall do them': as it were, you make them, because through the awakening that you produce below, an awakening is produced above. Therefore it is written, 'do good.' Good refers to the righteous one, as it is written: 'Say of the righteous one that he is good.'” The Zohar describes an effective awakening above produced by observance below. Rav Tzadok applies this pattern to the making of words of Torah. The traditional folio is tracked by the retrieved text's Vilna-page markers.

433.label: Berachos 55a
433.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: Betzalel knew how to combine the letters with which heaven and earth were created. It is written here, 'And He filled him with the spirit of God, with wisdom, with understanding and with knowledge' (Shemos 35:31), and there, 'Hashem with wisdom founded the earth, established the heavens with understanding' (Mishlei 3:19), and 'by His knowledge the depths were split.'"

434.label: Zohar II 88a (Yisro)
434.rest: — "Corresponding to them one must complete his meals, delight in all of them and rejoice in each, for this is complete faith. Therefore Shabbos is honored above all other times and festivals, for everything is found in it, which is not so in all the other times and festivals."

435.label: Zohar II 88a (Yisro)
435.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon said: Whoever completes three meals on Shabbos, a voice goes forth and proclaims of him: 'Then you shall delight in Hashem' — this is one meal, corresponding to the Holy Ancient One; 'and I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth' — the second meal, corresponding to the Field of holy Apples; 'and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father' — the completion in Zeir Anpin."

436.label: Kiddushin 18a
436.rest: — "Rav Chiya bar Avin said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: An idolater inherits his father by Torah law, as it is written, 'For I have given Mount Seir to Esav as an inheritance' (Devarim 2:5). But perhaps an apostate Jew is different! Rather, from here: 'For I have given Ar to the children of Lot as an inheritance' (Devarim 2:9)."

437.label: Taanis 29b
437.rest: — "'See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field which Hashem has blessed' (Bereishis 27:27). Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilas said in the name of Rav: Like the fragrance of a field of apples."

438.label: Zohar II 88b (Yisro)
438.rest: — "Woe to the person who does not complete the joy of the holy King. And what is His joy? These three meals of faith, in which the meals of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov are included, all of them joy upon joy, complete faith from every side."

439.label: Sanhedrin 93b
439.rest: — "Bar Koziva reigned two and a half years. He said to the Rabbis: I am Mashiach. They said to him: Of Mashiach it is written that he smells and judges; let us see whether he smells and judges. When they saw that he could not smell and judge, they killed him."

440.label: Sotah 5a
440.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Adam — efer, dam, marah (dust, blood, gall); basar — bushah, seruchah, rimah (shame, stench, worm)."

441.label: Avos D'Rabbi Nasan 9
441.rest: — "Nittai HaArbeli says: Distance yourself from a bad neighbor, do not join with the wicked, and do not despair of retribution."

442.label: Sotah 21a
442.rest: — "A transgression extinguishes a mitzvah, but a transgression does not extinguish Torah." Rashi: it extinguishes the reward of a mitzvah, but not the reward of one who has already toiled in Torah.

443.label: Zohar III 84a (Kedoshim)
443.rest: — "'See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field which Hashem has blessed' (Bereishis 27:27) — this implies that the Garden of Eden, the field of holy apples, entered with Yaakov. But how could the Garden of Eden enter with him, when it is so vast in breadth and length?"

444.label: Berachos 61a
444.rest: — "Two kidneys are in a person: one advises him for good and one advises him for bad. It stands to reason that the good one is at his right and the bad one at his left, as it is written, 'A wise man's heart is at his right, and a fool's heart at his left.'" Rashi (later on the amud): the kidneys advise the heart.

445.label: Megillah 6b
445.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: If a person tells you, 'I toiled and did not find,' do not believe him; 'I did not toil and I found,' do not believe him; 'I toiled and I found,' believe him."

446.label: Sotah 49a
446.rest: — "Rav Huna found a palm branch of chinunisa dates, took it and wrapped it in his scarf. His son Rabbah came and said: I smell the fragrance of chinunisa. He said: My son, there is purity in you — and he gave it to him."

447.label: Eruvin 21b
447.rest: — "Rava expounded: What is meant by 'The dudaim give forth fragrance' (Shir HaShirim 7:14)? These are the young men of Israel who have not tasted the taste of sin."

448.label: Yoma 72b
448.rest: — "'The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever' (Tehillim 19:10). Rabbi Chanina said: This is one who learns Torah in purity. What is that? He marries a wife and afterwards learns Torah." Rashi: he is saved from sinful thoughts.

449.label: Berachos 61b
449.rest: — "The lung draws in all kinds of liquids; the liver becomes angry; the gall casts a drop into it and calms it; the spleen laughs; the gizzard grinds; the stomach sleeps; the nose awakens."

450.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48, 85a
450.rest: — "Fortunate is one who guards a dwelling for Shabbos, which is the heart, so that there does not approach it the sadness of the spleen and the anger of the gall, which is the fire of Gehinnom, of which it is said, 'You shall not kindle fire in all your dwellings on the Shabbos day' (Shemos 35:3)."

451.label: Sanhedrin 70b
451.rest: — "Rabbi Meir says: The tree from which Adam ate was a vine, for there is nothing that brings wailing to a person except wine."

452.label: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah 3
452.rest: — "David the King further said: I feared out of my joy, and I rejoiced out of my fear, and my love rose above them all."

453.label: Rashi, Bereishis 21:6
453.rest: — "'Whoever hears will laugh with me' — will rejoice for me. Many barren women were remembered with her, many sick were healed on that day, many prayers were answered with hers, and there was much laughter in the world."

454.label: Zohar I (Midrash HaNe'elam, Chayei Sarah)
454.rest: — "Rabbi Abahu said: Come and see, 'And he took Rivkah and she became his wife, and he loved her, and Yitzchak was comforted after his mother'… and that is a time of laughter and joy in the world."

455.label: Zohar III 192b (Balak)
455.rest: — "Why is it written of Samael 'He rose (zarach)' and of Rahav 'He shone forth (hofia)'? Because He took the light He stripped from Samael — the sword and killing, to kill in judgment; and from Rahav He took a little of their blessing, like one who shines a little; therefore 'He shone forth from Mount Paran' (Devarim 33:2), and not 'rose.'"

456.label: Pesikta d'Rav Kahana 12:12
456.rest: — "Ben Azzai said: [The Torah should be to you] not like an old edict, nor even like one two or three days old, but like an edict of that very day. Know that this is so, for it is written, 'In the third month… on this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai' (Shemos 19:1) — it does not say 'on that day' but 'on this day.'"

457.label: Berachos 63b
457.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah further opened in honor of the Torah: 'Be attentive and hear, Israel: this day you have become a people' (Devarim 27:9) — was the Torah given to Israel on that day? Was that day not at the end of forty years? Rather, to teach you that the Torah is as beloved to those who learn it every day as on the day it was given from Mount Sinai."

458.label: Shabbos 86b
458.rest: — "On the sixth of the month the Ten Commandments were given to Israel; Rabbi Yosi says: on the seventh. Rava said: All agree that they came to the wilderness of Sinai on Rosh Chodesh, for it is written, 'on this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai' (Shemos 19:1), and there, 'This month (chodesh) shall be for you' (Shemos 12:2)… Rabbi Yosi holds the month was fixed on Sunday, and on Sunday he said nothing to them because of the weariness of the journey."

459.label: Zohar II 78b (Yisro)
459.rest: — "Because Yaakov is Twins (te'omim), the Torah was given to his children in the month of Twins — the Torah in the secret of Twins: the Written Torah and the Oral Torah; in the third month, to a threefold people, in threefold levels; a threefold Torah — Torah, Prophets and Writings — and all is one."

460.label: Nedarim 22b
460.rest: — "Rav Ada son of Rabbi Chanina said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the Five Books of the Torah and the Book of Yehoshua, since it holds the layout of Eretz Yisrael. Why? 'For in much wisdom is much anger' (Koheles 1:18)." Rashi: Yehoshua records each tribe's portion; because they sinned, much wisdom (the other books) was added.

461.label: Zohar II 60a (Beshalach)
461.rest: — "'And he cried out to Hashem, and Hashem showed him a tree (etz)' (Shemos 15:25) — and 'tree' means only Torah, as it is written, 'It is a tree of life to those who grasp it' (Mishlei 3:18); and Torah is none other than the Holy One, blessed be He."

462.label: Tanchuma, Bereishis 2
462.rest: — "When the Holy One, blessed be He, created His world, He created it in six days and rested on the day of Shabbos, blessed it and sanctified it, like one who builds a house, finishes his work and makes a festive day… And the Merciful One said: Rest on the day of Shabbos, just as I rested on it, as it is written, 'and He rested on the seventh day; therefore Hashem blessed…' (Shemos 20:11)."

463.label: Rosh Hashanah 24a (Mishnah)
463.rest: — "The head of the beis din says, 'Mekudash (It is sanctified),' and all the people answer after him, 'Mekudash, mekudash.'"

464.label: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah 22
464.rest: — "While I was standing and speaking with the elder, a student who was not versed in halachah came to me and said: I occupy myself with the faith, I desire it, yearn for it and wait for Torah to come to me — and Torah does not come to me."

465.label: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Zuta 14
465.rest: — "Once I was walking from place to place, and I met a man who had neither Scripture nor Mishnah, who was scoffing. I said to him: My son, what will you answer your Father in Heaven on the day of judgment? He said to me: Rabbi, I have words with which to answer Him — understanding and knowledge were not given to me from Heaven."

466.label: Berachos 24b
466.rest: — "Rabbi Zeira said: This matter was absorbed into me in the house of Rav Hamnuna, and it outweighs for me all my learning: one who sneezes in his prayer, it is a good sign for him — just as they give him satisfaction below, so they give him satisfaction above."

467.label: Zohar II 54a (Beshalach)
467.rest: — "When the light of the Alef joined and reached the Zayin — what is Zayin? 'A sword for Hashem, filled with blood' (Yeshayahu 34:6) — then He did miracles and mighty deeds."

468.label: Zohar III 192b (Balak)
468.rest: — When the Torah was to be given, the heavenly prince of Esav was told that Israel must be given a gift to receive it; he stripped off the radiance that covered him and gave it to be given to Israel. This is "And He shone forth from Seir to them" (Devarim 33:2).

469.label: Midrash Tanchuma, Toldot 8
469.rest: — “When Esav came from outside, he told his father: Father, is salt liable to the tithe? Yitzchak marveled and said: See how particular my son is in commandments. His father asked him: My son, where were you today? He answered: In the house of study. Is this not the law of such and such? Is this not its prohibition? Is this not its permission? Through these words he hunted him with his mouth, and therefore he loved him.
