929.rest: — The Gemara reckons that the spies were sent at the end of Sivan and returned on the eighth of Av: "'And the people wept that night' (Bamidbar 14:1) — that night was the night of Tisha B'Av. The Holy One said to them: You wept a weeping for nothing; I will establish for you a weeping for generations."

930.label: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah 1
930.rest: — "'To guard the way of the Tree of Life' (Bereishis 3:24): 'the way' — this is derech eretz; 'the Tree of Life' — this teaches that derech eretz preceded the Tree of Life; and the Tree of Life is nothing but Torah, as it says, 'It is a tree of life to those who grasp it' (Mishlei 3:18)."

931.label: Zohar III 155b (Behaaloscha)
931.rest: — "'Kill me, I pray' (Bamidbar 11:15): he spoke toward the place where death dwells, and that place is the feminine; and this is the Tree of Death — for, as we have established, in the Tree of Life death does not dwell."

932.label: Rashi, Genesis 1:1, s.v. Bereishis Bara
932.rest: — “As our Sages expounded: For the sake of the Torah, which is called 'the beginning of His way,' and for the sake of Israel, who are called 'the beginning of His produce.'” Rashi's two readings of bereishis underlie the claim that Creation's purpose is bound to Torah and Israel. The Sinai condition discussed in Shabbos 88a then gives that purpose its explicit covenantal form.

933.label: Yoma 76b
933.rest: — “Rava raised a contradiction: it is written yeshammach and read yesammach. If he merits, wine gladdens him; if he does not merit, it devastates him. This is what Rava said: Wine and spices have made me perceptive.” The wordplay distinguishes beneficial joy from wine's ruinous effect. Rav Tzadok applies the requirement of merit to the spiritual wine of Oral Torah.

934.label: Sotah 7a
934.rest: — "And he says to her: My daughter, wine does much, frivolity does much, youth does much, bad neighbors do much."

935.label: Zohar I 202a, Mikeitz
935.rest: — “A person should recall the day of death, for this breaks the human heart. The evil inclination dwells only where there is the joy of wine and arrogance of spirit. Where a broken spirit is found, it departs and does not dwell with him. ... Come and see: the good inclination seeks the joy of Torah; the evil inclination seeks the joy of wine, adultery, and arrogance of spirit. Therefore a person should continually confront it with that great day, the day of judgment and accounting.” The source itself distinguishes two kinds of joy. Rav Tzadok therefore does not identify all joy with the spleen's unstable laughter.

936.label: Zohar II 148b (Terumah)
936.rest: — "We have learned that everywhere this serpent goes after the secret of the 'woman of valor,' and the 'woman of harlotry' seeks to fashion herself like her, but cannot. The mark and letter of the woman of valor is hei… and the letter of the woman of harlotry is kuf, like an ape among men, which imitates people."

937.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
937.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

938.label: Chagigah 12b
938.rest: — "Aravos — in which are righteousness, justice and charity, the treasuries of life, the treasuries of peace and the treasuries of blessing… and the dew with which the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to revive the dead, as it says, 'A bountiful rain You shed, O God' (Tehillim 68:10)."

939.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 19 (38b)
939.rest: — "Therefore the union of Torah scholars is from Shabbos to Shabbos, to bequeath that drop which is Chochmah, the dew (tal = 39) of Torah, to their children; and not for nothing did the Sages explain: whoever occupies himself with the dew of Torah, the dew of Torah revives him."

940.label: Kesubos 111b
940.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said to him: I expound from another verse, as it is written, 'For Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth shall cast forth the dead' (Yeshayahu 26:19): whoever makes use of the light of Torah, the light of Torah revives him; and whoever does not make use of the light of Torah, the light of Torah does not revive him."

941.label: Zohar III (Pinchas, Ra'aya Meheimna)
941.rest: — "Elder, elder: the Shechinah is called 'the land of the Holy One,' as it is written, 'And the earth is My footstool' (Yeshayahu 66:1). From the side of Chesed it is called water, from the side of Gevurah fire, from the side of the middle pillar air; and it is earth, the ground for them all."

942.label: Menachos 29b
942.rest: — "[The scribes] make a bump (chotrei) on the roof of the Ches, as if to say: He lives (chai) in the heights of the world." Rashi: the roof of the Ches is made with a raised point above, meaning that the Holy One, blessed is He, Who lives forever, dwells in the heights of the world.

943.label: Zohar III 158b (Shelach)
943.rest: — "'Is there a tree in it or not' (Bamidbar 13:20) — this is what you asked to know at first: 'Is Hashem among us or not' (Shemos 17:7). There you will see: if its fruit is like that of other lands, the Tree of Life is not there; and if its fruit is greater and different from every place in the world…"

944.label: Zohar II, Beshalach 64b
944.rest: — “Rabbi Abba said: What is meant by ‘Is the Lord in our midst, or nothing?’ Were Israel fools who did not know this matter? Had they not seen the Divine Presence before them and the clouds of glory surrounding them? ... Rather, Rabbi Shimon said this: They wished to know the difference between the Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, who is called Nothing, and Zeir Anpin, who is called the Lord. ... Why, then, were they punished? Because they made a separation and put it to a test. They said: If it is this One, we will ask in one manner; if it is this One, we will ask in another manner. Therefore, immediately, ‘Amalek came.’” The Zohar interprets Israel's question at Massah as a question about the degree from which Divine governance was being revealed. It explicitly names the concealed Atika as Ayin.

945.label: Nedarim 22b
945.rest: — “Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Yehoshua.”

946.label: Sanhedrin 70a
946.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: What is meant by 'Do not look upon wine when it reddens' (Mishlei 23:31)? Do not look upon wine, which reddens the faces of the wicked in this world and whitens [shames] their faces in the World to Come. Rava said: … Do not look upon wine, for its end is blood." Rashi: in the end he will be killed over it.

947.label: Bava Basra 84a
947.rest: — "Rav Pappa said: Since it teaches 'white,' learn from this that the sun is red. Know it, for it is red in the morning and in the evening; and that we do not see it so all day is because our eyesight is not strong enough."

948.label: Bava Metzia 84a
948.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: I have remained of the beautiful men of Yerushalayim. Whoever wishes to see the beauty of Rabbi Yochanan should bring a silver goblet fresh from the smith, fill it with seeds of red pomegranate, set a garland of red roses about its rim, and place it between sun and shade: that radiance is a glimpse of Rabbi Yochanan's beauty."

949.label: Sukkah 52a
949.rest: — "R. Avira expounded: The evil inclination has seven names. The Holy One called it 'evil'… Moshe called it 'uncircumcised (arel),' as it says, 'Circumcise the foreskin of your heart'; David called it 'impure'…." Rashi has no comment on this line.

950.label: Rosh Hashanah 16b–17a
950.rest: — Beis Shammai say: There are three groups on the Day of Judgment… the completely wicked are written and sealed at once for Gehinnom, as it says, "And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, these to eternal life, and these to shame and everlasting abhorrence" (Daniel 12:2).

951.label: Avodah Zarah 5a
951.rest: — "As this Tanna taught: Rabbi Yosi says: Israel accepted the Torah only so that the Angel of Death would not rule over them, as it says, 'I said: you are angels, all of you children of the Most High' — you corrupted your deeds — 'therefore like men you shall die' (Tehillim 82:6–7)."

952.label: Bava Basra 16a
952.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: He is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the Angel of Death."

953.label: Nedarim 22b
953.rest: — "Rav Ada son of Rabbi Chanina said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Yehoshua alone, which contains the apportioning of Eretz Yisrael. What is the reason? 'For in much wisdom is much anger' (Koheles 1:18)." Rashi: because they rebelled, much wisdom — the other books — was added, to burden them further.

954.label: Zohar II 82b (Yisro)
954.rest: — "For we learned: six hundred and thirteen kinds of counsel the Torah gave to a person, to be whole with his Master, for his Master wishes to do good to him in this world and in the World to Come."

955.label: Avodah Zarah 9a
955.rest: — "The school of Eliyahu taught: The world exists six thousand years: two thousand of tohu, two thousand of Torah, two thousand the days of Mashiach… And the two thousand of Torah — from when? From 'and the souls they had made in Charan' (Bereishis 12:5); and it is a tradition that Avraham was then fifty-two years old."

956.label: Yoma 28b
956.rest: — "Rav said: Avraham Avinu fulfilled the entire Torah, as it says, 'Because Avraham listened to My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes and My Torahs' (Bereishis 26:5). Rav Shimi bar Chiya said to Rav: Perhaps only the seven mitzvos? — There was milah too! — Perhaps seven and milah? — If so, why 'My commandments and My Torahs'?"

957.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
957.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

958.label: Taanis 26a–b (Mishnah)
958.rest: — "Five things happened to our fathers on the seventeenth of Tammuz…: the Tablets were broken, the daily offering ceased, the city was breached, Apostomos burned the Torah, and an idol was set up in the Sanctuary."

959.label: Zohar II 184a (Tetzaveh)
959.rest: — "There is no light except that which comes out of darkness: for when this side is subdued, the Holy One, blessed be He, ascends above and is glorified in His glory. There is no service of the Holy One except from within darkness, and no good except from within evil."

960.label: Rema, Orach Chaim 1:1
960.rest: — "When a person takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed be He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, as it says, 'Can a man hide in secret places that I shall not see him? says Hashem' (Yirmeyahu 23:24) — immediately awe and submission will come upon him, in dread of Hashem Yisbarach, and he will be ashamed before Him constantly."

961.label: Berachos 28b
961.rest: — "They said to him: Our master, bless us. He said to them: May it be His will that the fear of Heaven be upon you like the fear of flesh and blood. His students said: Only so far? He said to them: Would that it were so! Know that when a person commits a transgression, he says: Let no person see me."

962.label: Zohar I 5b (Introduction)
962.rest: — "'You shall fear My Sanctuary' (Vayikra 19:30) — this is the Shabbos of Friday night, which is fear, and fear dwells in it."

963.label: Eruvin 54b
963.rest: — "'And those who walk' — these are the masters of Scripture; 'on the way' — the masters of Mishnah; 'converse (sichu)' — these are the masters of Talmud, for all their conversation is words of Torah." Rashi has no comment on this passage.

964.label: Berachos 26b
964.rest: — "Yitzchak instituted the afternoon prayer, as it says, 'Yitzchak went out lasuach (to converse) in the field toward evening,' and 'sichah' means nothing other than prayer, as it says, 'A prayer of the afflicted… he pours out his sichah before Hashem.'" Rashi: the Patriarchs instituted the prayers, as this Baraisa teaches.

965.label: Zohar III 2a (beginning of Vayikra)
965.rest: — "And so with Rachav, what is written? 'Give me a true sign (os emes)' (Yehoshua 2:12) — this is the letter vav, which is called the sign of truth. And if you say the other letters are not truth — they are, but this letter is called 'the sign of truth.'"

966.label: Berachos 5b
966.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Granted Torah and kindness, as it is written, 'Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned' (Mishlei 16:6): 'kindness' is acts of kindness… and 'truth' is Torah, as it is said, 'Buy truth and do not sell it' (Mishlei 23:23)."

967.label: Berachos 61b
967.rest: — "The lung draws in all kinds of liquids; the liver becomes angry; the gall casts a drop into it and calms it; the spleen laughs; the gizzard grinds; the stomach sleeps; the nose awakens."

968.label: Avodah Zarah 9a
968.rest: — "The school of Eliyahu taught: The world exists six thousand years: two thousand of tohu, two thousand of Torah, two thousand the days of Mashiach… And the two thousand of Torah — from when? From 'and the souls they had made in Charan' (Bereishis 12:5); and it is a tradition that Avraham was then fifty-two years old."

969.label: Sanhedrin 38b
969.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: [Adam] drew his foreskin forward, as it is written here, 'But they, like Adam, transgressed the covenant' (Hoshea 6:7), and it is written there, 'he has broken My covenant' (Bereishis 17:14)."

970.label: Tanchuma, Vayeshev 4
970.rest: — "When the Holy One created the world, on the first day He created the Angel of Death. From where? Rabbi Berechyah said: Because it says, 'and darkness upon the face of the deep' (Bereishis 1:2) — this is the Angel of Death, who darkens the faces of the creatures."

971.label: Shabbos 104a
971.rest: — "The Rabbis said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: Children came to the study hall today and said things the like of which were not said even in the days of Yehoshua bin Nun: Alef-beis — learn understanding (alef binah); gimmel-dalet — be kind to the poor (gemol dalim)." Rashi: "learn understanding" — the study of Torah.

972.label: Temurah 16a
972.rest: — "'Rich and poor meet; Hashem makes them both' (Mishlei 22:2): when a student goes to his teacher and says 'Teach me Torah' — if he teaches him, well; if not, He Who made this one wise makes him foolish, and the foolish one wise." Rashi: He now begins to make them anew, this one wise and this one foolish.

973.label: Temurah 16a
973.rest: — “When a student goes to his teacher and says, Teach me Torah, if he teaches him, Hashem enlightens the eyes of them both. If not, The rich and the poor meet; Hashem makes them all: He who made this one wise makes him ignorant, and the one who made this one ignorant makes him wise. This is Rabbi Nasan's teaching.”

974.label: Tanchuma, Noach 3
974.rest: — "'According to (al pi) these words' (Shemos 34:27) — this is the Oral Torah, which is hard to learn and involves great suffering, and it is likened to darkness, as it says, 'The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light' (Yeshayahu 9:1): these are the masters of the Talmud, who have seen a great light, for the Holy One, blessed be He, illuminates their eyes in what is forbidden and permitted, impure and pure."

975.label: Yoma 72b
975.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: There are three crowns: of the Altar, of the Ark and of the Table. That of the Altar — Aharon merited it and took it; that of the Table — David merited it and took it; that of the Ark still lies there: whoever wishes to take it, let him come and take it. Lest you say it is lesser, the verse says, 'Through me kings reign' (Mishlei 8:15)."

976.label: Sanhedrin 44a
976.rest: — "'Yisrael has sinned' (Yehoshua 7:11) — Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is Yisrael."

977.label: Berachos 7a
977.rest: — "Rabbi Meir said: Two were given to him and one was not given to him, as it says, 'And I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious' (Shemos 33:19) — even though he is not worthy; 'and I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy' — even though he is not worthy."

978.label: Menachos 29b
978.rest: — "[The scribes] make a bump (chotrei) on the roof of the Ches, as if to say: He lives (chai) in the heights of the world." Rashi: the roof of the Ches is made with a raised point above, meaning that the Holy One, blessed is He, Who lives forever, dwells in the heights of the world.

979.label: Shabbos 88b
979.rest: — "Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: At each utterance that came from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the souls of Israel left them, as it says, 'My soul went out when He spoke' (Shir HaShirim 5:6). If their souls left at the first utterance, how did they receive the second? He brought down the dew with which He will revive the dead in the future and revived them, as it says, 'A generous rain You shed, O God' (Tehillim 68:10)."

980.label: Pesachim 77a
980.rest: — Rosh Chodesh is called a mo'ed, "in line with Abaye, for Abaye said: Tammuz of that year they made full, as it is written, 'He proclaimed a mo'ed against me to crush my young men' (Eichah 1:15)." Rashi: because Tammuz was made full, the forty days of the spies ended on Tisha B'Av, and weeping was fixed for them on it for generations; so the day of the new month is called a mo'ed.

981.label: Pesachim 77a
981.rest: — "Our Rabbis taught: 'And Moshe declared the appointed times (mo'adei) of Hashem' (Vayikra 23:44) — why is this said? Because we learned only of the daily offering and the Pesach, of which 'in its appointed time' is said: 'in its appointed time' — even on Shabbos; 'in its appointed time' — even in impurity." The verse extends this to the other communal offerings, the Rosh Chodesh goats among them.

982.label: Yoma 56b
982.rest: — "'Who dwells with them amid their impurity' (Vayikra 16:16) — even at a time that they are impure, the Shechinah is with them."

983.label: Rosh Hashanah 24a (Mishnah)
983.rest: — "The head of the beis din says 'Mekudash,' and all the people answer after him, 'Mekudash, mekudash.' Whether it was seen in its time or not seen in its time, they sanctify it."

984.label: Bava Kamma 55a
984.rest: — "Rather, because Scripture opened with it for good at first: from 'Bereishis' until 'And God saw the light, that it was good (tov)' (Bereishis 1:4), no tes is written." Rashi: the first tes written in the Torah was said for good.

985.label: Bava Basra 4a
985.rest: — Hordos asked Bava ben Buta how to atone for killing the Sages: "He said: He extinguished the light of the world, as it is written, 'For a mitzvah is a lamp and Torah is light' (Mishlei 6:23); let him go and occupy himself with the light of the world, as it is written, 'And all the nations shall stream to it' (Yeshayahu 2:2)."

986.label: Zohar I 2b (Introduction)
986.rest: — "The letter tes came before Him and said: 'Create the world with me, for through me You are called good (tov) and upright.' He said to it: 'I will not create the world with you, for your goodness is hidden and concealed within you, as it says, "How great is Your goodness which You have hidden for those who fear You" (Tehillim 31:20). Since it is hidden within you, it has no portion in this world that I wish to create, but in the World to Come.'"

987.label: Zohar II 152a, Terumah
987.rest: — “Come and see: Tes is the illumination of life in every place. Therefore the verse begins with it in 'that it was good,' as it is written: 'God saw the light, that it was good.' From this letter the destroying angel flees—or rather, he is not given permission to enter there. This letter differs from kuf: kuf is not established in any settled place in the world; its sign is 'A man of evil speech shall not be established in the land.' Tes is established in every place and is properly fitted to settle there; wherever tes is, kuf has no settled place. ... Just as this letter rules in this place, so another letter rules in the place of Gehinnom. Which is it? Qof.” The source contrasts tes with kuf in the account of a place protected from death. The retrieved text also preserves a variant reading of ches for kuf. Rav Tzadok's argument follows the kuf reading quoted in his manuscript.

988.label: Arachin 10b
988.rest: — "Rosh Chodesh, which is called a mo'ed — let one say [Hallel]! It is not sanctified by a prohibition of labor, as it is written, 'The song shall be for you as in the night when a festival is sanctified' (Yeshayahu 30:29): a night sanctified as a festival requires song, and one not sanctified as a festival does not require song."

989.label: Taanis 28b
989.rest: — "Rav came to Bavel and saw them reciting Hallel on Rosh Chodesh. He thought to stop them; when he saw that they skipped portions, he said: Learn from this: the custom of their fathers is in their hands."

990.label: Zohar III 11b (Vayikra)
990.rest: — "Come and see: ten utterances for the work of Creation, as we learned, 'With ten utterances the world was created'; ten utterances for the giving of the Torah — the Ten Commandments. It is written, 'I am Hashem your God' (Shemos 20:2), and in the work of Creation, 'Let there be light, and there was light' (Bereishis 1:3) — this is the faith of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called 'light.'"

991.label: Rosh Hashanah 32a
991.rest: — "The 'And He said's of the Creation account are nine! — 'Bereishis' is also an utterance, as it is written, 'By the word of Hashem the heavens were made' (Tehillim 33:6)." Rashi: although "and He said" is not written there, it is as though it were, for heaven too was created by speech and not by hand.

992.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 26
992.rest: — When Yirmiyahu turned back from the exiles at the rivers of Babylon, they cried out, "Our father Yirmiyahu, are you leaving us?" — as it is written, "By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat, and we also wept" (Tehillim 137:1). Yirmiyahu answered: "I call heaven and earth to witness: had you wept a single weeping while you were still in Zion, you would not have been exiled."

993.label: Sanhedrin 98a
993.rest: — "He went to [Mashiach] and said: Peace upon you, my master and teacher. He said: Peace upon you, son of Levi. He said: When will the master come? He said: Today. He came to Eliyahu, who asked: What did he tell you? — 'Peace upon you, son of Levi.' He said: He has assured you and your father of the World to Come… He said: This is what he told you: 'Today — if you will hearken to His voice' (Tehillim 95:7)." Rashi: had you not been perfect tzaddikim he would not have greeted you and mentioned your father.

994.label: Yoma 86b
994.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Great is teshuvah, for it overrides a prohibition of the Torah, as it says, 'If a man sends away his wife and she goes from him and becomes another man's, shall he return to her again?… Yet you have strayed with many lovers — and return to Me, says Hashem' (Yirmeyahu 3:1)."

995.label: Shabbos 89b
995.rest: — “The Holy One said to Israel: If your sins are like these years, which are arranged and come in order from the six days of Creation until now, they shall be made white as snow.”

996.label: Bava Kamma 17a
996.rest: — "And water means only Torah, as it says, 'Ho, all who are thirsty, go to the water' (Yeshayahu 55:1)."

997.label: Pesikta D'Rav Kahana 13:15
997.rest: — "The lion (Nevuchadnetzar) came up in the month whose sign is the lion (Av) and destroyed Ariel (the Beis HaMikdash); so the Lion (the Holy One) will come in the month whose sign is the lion and build Ariel."

998.label: Rashi, Sukkah 41a (s.v. i nami)
998.rest: — the Mikdash of the future that we await will be revealed and come down from Heaven built and perfected, as it says, "The Sanctuary, Hashem, which Your hands have established" (Shemos 15:17); therefore it may be built at any moment, even at night or on Yom Tov.

999.label: Taanis 26b, 29a
999.rest: — "From when Av enters, we diminish in joy." "Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilas said in the name of Rav: Just as from when Av enters we diminish in joy, so from when Adar enters we increase in joy."

1000.label: Arachin 10b
1000.rest: — "Rosh Chodesh, which is called a mo'ed — let one say [Hallel]! It is not sanctified by a prohibition of labor, as it is written, 'The song shall be for you as in the night when a festival is sanctified' (Yeshayahu 30:29): a night sanctified as a festival requires song, and one not sanctified as a festival does not require song."

1001.label: Sefer Yetzirah 6
1001.rest: — "The heart in the soul is like a king in war."

1002.label: Pri Etz Chaim, Shaar Rosh Chodesh 3
1002.rest: — The Name Havayah brings all being into existence, and nothing in the world lacks light from this Name; it has twelve permutations, divided among the twelve months of the year, and the four letters of Havayah — one letter per month — return each year.

1003.label: Kiddushin 5a
1003.rest: — "'And she departs from his house and goes and becomes (vehaysah) another man's' (Devarim 24:2) — it compares becoming [married] to departing: just as departure is by a document, so becoming [married] can be by a document."

1004.label: Kiddushin 68a
1004.rest: — "Chizkiyah said: The verse says, 'And her niddah shall be upon him' (Vayikra 15:24) — even at the time of her niddah, there can be havayah [kiddushin] with her."

1005.label: Berachos 34b
1005.rest: — "R. Abahu said: In the place where ba'alei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous cannot stand, as it says, 'Peace, peace, to the far and to the near' — the far first, then the near." This disputes R. Yochanan, who holds the completely righteous are greater. Rashi: "the near" is one who was far from sin all his days, a tzaddik from the start.

1006.label: Berachos 34b
1006.rest: — "Rabbi Abahu said: In the place where baalei teshuvah stand, perfect tzaddikim cannot stand, as it says, 'Peace, peace to the far and to the near' (Yeshayahu 57:19) — first to the far, and then to the near."

1007.label: Zevachim 91a
1007.rest: — "Come and hear: the mussafin of Shabbos precede the mussafin of Rosh Chodesh. — Is it so that [the sanctity of] Rosh Chodesh is effective for its own mussafin, but not effective for the mussafin of Shabbos?" The Gemara thus weighs the view that the Rosh Chodesh mussafin are more sanctified than those of Shabbos.

1008.label: Zevachim 91a
1008.rest: — "Even though the Mussafin are holier — does Shabbos avail for the Mussafin and not avail for the Temidin?" And: "Does Rosh Chodesh avail for its own Mussafin and not avail for the Mussafin of Shabbos?" Rashi: the Mussafin bear the name of Shabbos; but since the Temidin are offered today, the name of Shabbos is on them too.

1009.label: Pesachim 117b
1009.rest: — "Shabbos is fixed and established [and so we say] 'Who sanctifies the Shabbos'; a Yom Tov — it is Israel who fix it, for they intercalate the months and fix the years — [so we say] 'Who sanctifies Israel and the festivals.'"

1010.label: Rosh Hashanah 24a
1010.rest: — “The head of the court says: Sanctified! All the people answer after him: Sanctified, sanctified! ... From where is it learned that all the people answer after him? Rav Pappa said: Scripture says, Which you shall proclaim them; read it as you. ... Why twice, Sanctified, sanctified? Because it is written, Holy convocations. Whether it was seen at its expected time or was not seen at its expected time, they sanctify it.” The Mishnah and Gemara include the people in the proclamation. Rav Tzadok reads their response as participation in the holiness conferred by the court.

1011.label: Bava Metzia 38a
1011.rest: — "But it says, 'A person prefers one kav of his own to nine kavin of his fellow's'! — That is mere hyperbole."

1012.label: Kesubos 52a
1012.rest: — "Our Rabbis taught: If she was taken captive and they demanded of him up to ten times her value, the first time he redeems her; from then on, if he wishes he redeems her, and if he wishes he does not." Rashi: the Sages enacted only one redemption.

1013.label: Shabbos 31a
1013.rest: — Hillel said to the convert: "What is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow; this is the whole Torah, and the rest is its explanation — go and learn." Rashi (s.v. da'alach): "Your friend and your father's friend do not forsake" (Mishlei 27:10) — this is the Holy One, blessed be He: do not transgress His words, just as it is hateful to you that your friend should transgress yours.

1014.label: Pesachim 77a
1014.rest: — Rosh Chodesh is called a mo'ed, "in line with Abaye, for Abaye said: Tammuz of that year they made full, as it is written, 'He proclaimed a mo'ed against me to crush my young men' (Eichah 1:15)." Rashi: because Tammuz was made full, the forty days of the spies ended on Tisha B'Av, and weeping was fixed for them on it for generations; so the day of the new month is called a mo'ed.

1015.label: Zevachim 91a
1015.rest: — "Come and hear: the mussafin of Shabbos precede the mussafin of Rosh Chodesh. — Is it so that [the sanctity of] Rosh Chodesh is effective for its own mussafin, but not effective for the mussafin of Shabbos?" The Gemara thus weighs the view that the Rosh Chodesh mussafin are more sanctified than those of Shabbos.

1016.label: Shabbos 10b
1016.rest: — “The Holy One said to Moshe: I have a good gift in My treasure house, and Shabbos is its name, and I wish to give it to Yisrael.”

1017.label: Zohar II 152a, Terumah
1017.rest: — “Come and see: Tes is the illumination of life in every place. Therefore the verse begins with it in 'that it was good,' as it is written: 'God saw the light, that it was good.' From this letter the destroying angel flees—or rather, he is not given permission to enter there. This letter differs from kuf: kuf is not established in any settled place in the world; its sign is 'A man of evil speech shall not be established in the land.' Tes is established in every place and is properly fitted to settle there; wherever tes is, kuf has no settled place. ... Just as this letter rules in this place, so another letter rules in the place of Gehinnom. Which is it? Qof.” The source contrasts tes with kuf in the account of a place protected from death. The retrieved text also preserves a variant reading of ches for kuf. Rav Tzadok's argument follows the kuf reading quoted in his manuscript.

1018.label: Zohar II 230a (Pekudei)
1018.rest: — "The letter tes is hidden and concealed, and it shines the light of them all, for this letter is the light of them all, and there is no light except from this letter, as it is written, 'And God saw the light, that it was good (tov)'; and it is the shining of that light which is hidden and concealed."

1019.label: Zohar II 184a
1019.rest: — “There is no light except that which comes forth from within darkness.”

1020.label: Berachos 61a
1020.rest: — "A person has two kidneys: one counsels him for good and one counsels him for evil. It stands to reason that the good one is at his right and the evil one at his left, as it is written, 'The heart of a wise man is at his right, and the heart of a fool at his left' (Koheles 10:2)."

1021.label: Zohar III 193b (Balak)
1021.rest: — "'Counsels from afar' (Yeshayahu 25:1) — what are they? The two willow branches, for all the counsel of the prophets comes from there; they are called 'counsels from afar.'"

1022.label: Yerushalmi Sanhedrin 10:2
1022.rest: — "What would Achitofel do? When a person came to take counsel with him on a matter, he would say to him: Go and do so-and-so; and if you do not believe me, go and ask of the Urim VeTumim. And he would go and ask and find it so."

1023.label: Zohar III 194a (Balak)
1023.rest: — "'And knows the knowledge of the Most High' (Bamidbar 24:16) — he knew the hour when judgment hangs over the world, and he would aim for that hour with his sorceries."

1024.label: Zohar II 152a, Terumah
1024.rest: — “Come and see: Tes is the illumination of life in every place. Therefore the verse begins with it in 'that it was good,' as it is written: 'God saw the light, that it was good.' From this letter the destroying angel flees—or rather, he is not given permission to enter there. This letter differs from kuf: kuf is not established in any settled place in the world; its sign is 'A man of evil speech shall not be established in the land.' Tes is established in every place and is properly fitted to settle there; wherever tes is, kuf has no settled place. ... Just as this letter rules in this place, so another letter rules in the place of Gehinnom. Which is it? Qof.” The source contrasts tes with kuf in the account of a place protected from death. The retrieved text also preserves a variant reading of ches for kuf. Rav Tzadok's argument follows the kuf reading quoted in his manuscript.

1025.label: Bava Kamma 55a
1025.rest: — "Rather, because Scripture opened with it for good at first: from 'Bereishis' until 'And God saw the light, that it was good (tov)' (Bereishis 1:4), no tes is written." Rashi: the first tes written in the Torah was said for good.

1026.label: Taanis 15a
1026.rest: — “Tzaddikim for light and the upright for gladness, as it is written: ‘Light is sown for the tzaddik, and for the upright of heart, gladness.’”

1027.label: Chagigah 12a
1027.rest: — "And for whom did He store it away? For the righteous in the time to come, as it says, 'And God saw the light, that it was good' (Bereishis 1:4), and 'good' means only the righteous, as it says, 'Say of the righteous that he is good' (Yeshayahu 3:10)."

1028.label: Zohar III, Pinchas (Ra'aya Meheimna)
1028.rest: — "'Men of valor, God-fearing, men of truth' (Shemos 18:21): 'men of valor' — from the side of the right of Avraham, where there is the seeing of Torah; 'God-fearing' — from the side of Yitzchak, where there is hearing, as Chavakuk the prophet said, 'Hashem, I have heard Your report and I was afraid' (Chavakuk 3:2); 'men of truth' — from the side of Yaakov, where there is smell."

1029.label: Yoma 72b: “Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, when he has no heart? Woe to those Torah scholars who engage in Torah and have no fear of Heaven”: on Proverbs 17:16 (“a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, and he has no heart”)
1029.rest: — the “heart” lacking is fear of Heaven.

1030.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
1030.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

1031.label: Zohar II 14b (Shemos)
1031.rest: — "When He wished to establish the world, He made Avraham in the secret of Chochmah, Yitzchak in the secret of Tevunah, Yaakov in the secret of Daas, and with this it is called, 'And with knowledge the chambers are filled' (Mishlei 24:4)."

1032.label: Zohar II 152a (Terumah)
1032.rest: — "Come and see: tes is the light of life in every place, and therefore Scripture opened with it in 'ki tov,' as it is written, 'And God saw the light, that it was good (tov)' (Bereishis 1:4)… From this place the destroying angel flees — do not say flees, but that he is not given permission to enter there."

1033.label: Shabbos 118a
1033.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosi: Whoever delights the Shabbos is given an inheritance without boundaries, as it says, 'Then you shall delight in Hashem, and I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth, and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father' (Yeshayahu 58:14)." Rashi: without boundaries — that has no end.

1034.label: Zohar III 215b (Pinchas)
1034.rest: — "The secret of the holy covenant is the letter yud, crowned with the supernal mark… Here this letter in Pinchas [is a small yud]: the small yud is the yud of the covenant, which certainly emerges from within the upper yud."

1035.label: Shabbos 117b
1035.rest: — "From where do we know three meals [on Shabbos]? Rabbi Chidka said: 'And Moshe said: Eat it today, for today is a Shabbos to Hashem; today you will not find it in the field' (Shemos 16:25) — three times 'today.'"

1036.label: Midrash Tehillim 95
1036.rest: — "'Today, if you will listen to His voice' (Tehillim 95:7): Rabbi Levi said: If Israel kept even one Shabbos properly, they would be redeemed immediately, as it says, 'Today, if you will listen to His voice,' and it is written, 'Keep the Shabbos day to sanctify it' (Devarim 5:12)."

1037.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
1037.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

1038.label: Zohar III 2a (beginning of Vayikra)
1038.rest: — "And so with Rachav, what is written? 'Give me a true sign (os emes)' (Yehoshua 2:12) — this is the letter vav, which is called the sign of truth. And if you say the other letters are not truth — they are, but this letter is called 'the sign of truth.'"

1039.label: Berachos 5b
1039.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Granted Torah and kindness, as it is written, 'Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned' (Mishlei 16:6): 'kindness' is acts of kindness… and 'truth' is Torah, as it is said, 'Buy truth and do not sell it' (Mishlei 23:23)."

1040.label: Megillah 14b
1040.rest: — "'And Esther donned royalty (malchus)' (Esther 5:1) — it should have said 'royal garments'! Rather, ruach hakodesh clothed her: it is written here 'donned,' and there, 'And the spirit clothed Amasai' (I Divrei HaYamim 12:19)."

1041.label: Zohar III 61a, Acharei Mos
1041.rest: — “It is called the holy spirit (ruach hakodesh), that is, a spirit from that supernal holiness.”

1042.label: Zohar I 47b (Bereishis)
1042.rest: — “‘And God finished on the seventh day’: this is Torah she'b'al peh, which is the seventh day.”

1043.label: Zohar I 32a (Bereishis)
1043.rest: — "And this speech is called Shabbos; and because Shabbos is called speech, mundane speech is forbidden on Shabbos. And so Rabbi Shimon would do: when he saw his mother talking [on Shabbos], he would say to her: Mother, be silent; it is Shabbos and it is forbidden — for this speech must rule, and no other."

1044.label: Shabbos 138b on Amos 8:11–12
1044.rest: — “'They will wander to seek the word of Hashem, but will not find it.' 'The word of Hashem' means halachah; 'the word of Hashem' means the end; 'the word of Hashem' means prophecy.” The quoted prophecy is Amos 8:11–12. Rav Tzadok selects the Gemara’s first interpretation: halachah itself is called the word of Hashem.

1045.label: Taanis 4a
1045.rest: — “Rava said: A young Torah scholar who becomes heated—it is the Torah that makes him heated, as it is said, ‘Is not My word like fire, says Hashem?’ Rav Ashi said: Any Torah scholar who is not hard as iron is not a Torah scholar, as it is said, ‘Like a hammer that shatters rock.’ ... Ravina said: Even so, a person must train himself in gentleness, as it is said, ‘Remove anger from your heart.’” The fire describes Torah’s force. The Gemara’s concluding qualification requires gentleness; its teaching does not make ordinary anger a virtue.

1046.label: Sanhedrin 86b
1046.rest: — the rebellious elder is tried before "the Great [Sanhedrin] in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, from which Torah goes forth to all Israel, as it says, 'from that place which Hashem shall choose' (Devarim 17:10)."

1047.label: Sukkah 20a
1047.rest: — "At first, when the Torah was forgotten from Israel, Ezra came up from Bavel and established it; it was again forgotten, and Hillel the Babylonian came up and established it; it was again forgotten, and Rabbi Chiya and his sons came up and established it."

1048.label: Pirkei Avot 1:1
1048.rest: — “Moses received Torah from Sinai and transmitted it to Joshua; Joshua to the elders; the elders to the prophets; and the prophets transmitted it to the Men of the Great Assembly. They said three things: Be deliberate in judgment, raise up many students, and make a fence for Torah.” The transmission culminates in the assembly whose program Rav Tzadok invokes: the expansion of students and the protection of Torah through a fence.

1049.label: Zohar III 35a (Tzav)
1049.rest: — "'And I have put My words in your mouth, and in the shadow of My hand I covered you' (Yeshayahu 51:16): we learned, whoever toils in words of Torah and whose lips murmur Torah, the Holy One covers him and the Shechinah spreads her wings over him… And not only that, but he sustains the world, and the Holy One rejoices with him as though on that day he had planted heaven and earth, as it is written, 'to plant the heavens and found the earth, and to say to Tziyon: You are My people.'"

1050.label: Zohar III 29b (Tzav)
1050.rest: — "So Torah scholars, the children of the King and the Queen, are called Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim. They have nothing of their own, for they are not craftsmen like other servants… their reward is in this world and in the World to Come, to delight them with every kind of food and drink and to honor them with fine garments, like Shabbos, of which it is said, 'Honor it with clean clothing'; whatever a person does for Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim he should do for them."

1051.label: Avodah Zarah 5a
1051.rest: — "As this Tanna taught: Rabbi Yosi says: Israel accepted the Torah only so that the Angel of Death would not rule over them, as it says, 'I said: you are angels, all of you children of the Most High' — you corrupted your deeds — 'therefore like men you shall die' (Tehillim 82:6–7)."

1052.label: Zohar I 202a (Miketz)
1052.rest: — “There is nothing that breaks the evil inclination except Torah.”

1053.label: Berachos 61a
1053.rest: — "Two kidneys are in a person: one advises him for good and one advises him for bad. It stands to reason that the good one is at his right and the bad one at his left, as it is written, 'A wise man's heart is at his right, and a fool's heart at his left.'" Rashi (later on the amud): the kidneys advise the heart.

1054.label: Tanchuma, Bereishis 7
1054.rest: — "'This alone I have found: that God made man upright' (Koheles 7:29) — the Holy One, who is called righteous and upright, created man in His image only so that he be righteous and upright like Him. And if you say, why did He create the evil inclination, of which it is written, 'For the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth' (Bereishis 8:21)? You say it is evil — who can make it good? The Holy One said: You are the one who makes it evil."

1055.label: Kiddushin 30b
1055.rest: — “The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: 'My children, I created the evil inclination and I created Torah as its remedy. If you occupy yourselves with Torah, you will not be delivered into its hand, as it says, If you do well, shall it not be lifted up? But if you do not occupy yourselves with Torah, you are delivered into its hand, as it says, Sin crouches at the door. Moreover, all its occupation is with you, as it says, Its desire is toward you. If you wish, you can rule over it, as it says, You shall rule over it.'” The source couples the reality of the inclination with a divinely provided means of resistance. Rav Tzadok further explains the energy of desire as capable of being directed toward yearning for Torah.

1056.label: Avos 6:1
1056.rest: — "Rabbi Meir says: Whoever occupies himself with Torah for its own sake merits many things… and people benefit from him counsel and sound wisdom (tushiyah), understanding and strength, as it says, 'Mine are counsel and sound wisdom; I am understanding, mine is strength' (Mishlei 8:14)."

1057.label: Sanhedrin 26b
1057.rest: — "Rabbi Chanan said: Why is it called tushiyah? Because it weakens (mesheshes) a person's strength. Another explanation: tushiyah, for it was given in secret (chashai) because of the Satan. Another explanation: tushiyah — words of tohu, upon which the world is founded."

1058.label: Tanchuma, Noach 3
1058.rest: — "'Nor is it found in the land of the living' (Iyov 28:13) — the Oral Torah is not found with one who seeks the pleasure of the world, desire, honor and greatness in this world, but with one who kills himself over it, as it says, 'This is the Torah: a man who dies in a tent' (Bamidbar 19:14). And such is the way of Torah: bread with salt you shall eat, water in measure you shall drink, on the ground you shall sleep, a life of hardship you shall live, and in Torah you shall toil."

1059.label: Berachos 63b
1059.rest: — "Another explanation: 'Haskeis ushma Yisrael' (Devarim 27:9) — be silent (has), and afterward analyze (kateis), in line with Rava, for Rava said: A person should always learn Torah and afterward reflect on it."

1060.label: Shabbos 155b (Mishnah)
1060.rest: — "One may not stuff a camel or cram it, but one may put food into its mouth (mal'itin)."

1061.label: Zohar III 271b, Eikev (Ra’aya Mehemna)
1061.rest: — “‘Come, eat of my bread’ — this is the Written Torah; ‘and drink of the wine I mixed’ — this is the wine of the Oral Torah.”

1062.label: Berachos 61a
1062.rest: — "Two kidneys are in a person: one advises him for good and one advises him for bad. It stands to reason that the good one is at his right and the bad one at his left, as it is written, 'A wise man's heart is at his right, and a fool's heart at his left.'" Rashi (later on the amud): the kidneys advise the heart.

1063.label: Sanhedrin 26b
1063.rest: — "Rabbi Chanan said: Why is it called tushiyah? Because it weakens (mesheshes) a person's strength. Another explanation: tushiyah, for it was given in secret (chashai) because of the Satan. Another explanation: tushiyah — words of tohu, upon which the world is founded."

1064.label: Avodah Zarah 5a
1064.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: Let us be grateful to our forefathers, for had they not sinned we would not have come into the world, as it says, 'I said: you are angels (elohim), all of you children of the Most High' — you corrupted your deeds — 'therefore like men you shall die' (Tehillim 82:6–7)."

1065.label: Taanis 26b (Mishnah)
1065.rest: — "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no festive days for Israel like the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur, on which the daughters of Yerushalayim would go out in borrowed white garments, so as not to shame one who had none… And so it says, 'Go forth and gaze, O daughters of Tziyon, upon King Shlomo, upon the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart' (Shir HaShirim 3:11): 'on the day of his wedding' — this is the giving of the Torah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash, may it be rebuilt speedily in our days."

1066.label: Taanis 30b
1066.rest: — "Granted Yom Kippur, because it has pardon and forgiveness, and it is the day on which the second Tablets were given; but the fifteenth of Av — what is it? Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel: It is the day on which the tribes were permitted to marry into one another."

1067.label: Chagigah 10b
1067.rest: — "Perhaps the Merciful One said 'chogu chaga' (celebrate a festival)!" Rashi: chogu chaga — to increase rejoicing.

1068.label: Taanis 26b (Mishnah)
1068.rest: — "From when Av enters, we diminish in joy. In the week in which Tisha B'Av falls it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder, but on Thursday it is permitted in honor of Shabbos. On the eve of Tisha B'Av a person may not eat two cooked dishes, may not eat meat and may not drink wine."

1069.label: Taanis 29b
1069.rest: — "It was taught: … it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder from Rosh Chodesh until the fast — the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehudah says: The entire month is forbidden. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: It is forbidden only during that week."

1070.label: Arachin 10b
1070.rest: — "Rosh Chodesh, which is called a mo'ed — let one say [Hallel]! It is not sanctified by a prohibition of labor, as it is written, 'The song shall be for you as in the night when a festival is sanctified' (Yeshayahu 30:29): a night sanctified as a festival requires song, and one not sanctified as a festival does not require song."

1071.label: Taanis 29a
1071.rest: — "'And the whole congregation raised their voice, and the people wept that night' (Bamidbar 14:1). Rabbah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: That day was the eve of Tisha B'Av. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: You wept a weeping for nothing, and I will establish for you a weeping for generations."

1072.label: Moed Katan 20a
1072.rest: — "From where do we derive seven days of mourning? As it is written, 'And I will turn your festivals into mourning' (Amos 8:10): just as a festival is seven days, so mourning is seven days."

1073.label: Yerushalmi, Moed Katan 3:5
1073.rest: — On the derivation of seven days of mourning from "I will turn your festivals into mourning," the Yerushalmi asks: say rather eight, like the eight days of the festival [of Sukkos and Shemini Atzeres].

1074.label: Taanis 30b
1074.rest: — "Rabbah bar bar Chanah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: It is the day on which the dead of the wilderness came to an end, for the master said: Until the dead of the wilderness came to an end there was no Divine speech with Moshe, as it says, 'And it was, when all the men of war had finished dying… that Hashem spoke to me' (Devarim 2:16–17) — to me was the speech."

1075.label: Bava Basra 121a
1075.rest: — The same teaching is brought there: "There were no festive days for Israel like the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur… Granted Yom Kippur, a day of pardon and forgiveness, the day on which the last Tablets were given; but the fifteenth of Av — what is it?"

1076.label: Makkos 11a
1076.rest: — "Why was the passage of the cities of refuge said in harsh language, as it is written, 'And Hashem spoke (vaydaber) to Yehoshua, saying: Speak to the Children of Israel, saying: Assign for yourselves the cities of refuge' (Yehoshua 20:1–2)? Because they are of the Torah." Rashi: everywhere in Yehoshua it says "vayomer," but here "vaydaber," and dibbur is a harsh expression.

1077.label: Rashi, Devarim 2:17 (from the Mechilta)
1077.rest: — "From the sending of the spies until here, this section does not say vayedaber but vayomer, to teach you that all thirty-eight years that Israel were under rebuke, the utterance was not addressed to him in a language of affection — face to face and with settled mind — to teach you that the Shechinah rests upon the prophets only for the sake of Israel."

1078.label: Zohar II 88b (Yisro)
1078.rest: — If one rejoices on Shabbos, even though he gives nothing to another, he is not punished as at other times and festivals; for it is written, "the dung of your festivals" (Malachi 2:3) — "your festivals," not "your Shabbosos"; and "Your new moons and your appointed times My soul hates" (Yeshayahu 1:14) — but Shabbos it does not mention.

1079.label: Shabbos 145b
1079.rest: — "Why are the festivals in Bavel joyous? Because they were not included in that curse, as it is written, 'And I will cause to cease all her joy, her festival, her new moon and her Shabbos, and all her appointed times' (Hoshea 2:13)."

1080.label: Taanis 31a
1080.rest: — "Ulla of Bira said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle dance for the righteous, and He will sit among them in Gan Eden, and each one will point with his finger, as it says, 'And it shall be said on that day: Behold, this is our God; we hoped to Him and He saved us… let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation' (Yeshayahu 25:9)."

1081.label: Berachos 6a
1081.rest: — "Rabbi Avin bar Rav Ada said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak: From where do we know that the Holy One puts on tefillin? As it says, 'Hashem has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His strength' (Yeshayahu 62:8)… And what is written in the tefillin of the Master of the world? 'And who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth' (I Divrei HaYamim 17:21)… The Holy One said to Israel: You have made Me one entity in the world, and I shall make you one entity in the world."

1082.label: Shir HaShirim 3:11 as expounded by Chazal (Taanis 26b; Eichah Rabbah, Pesichta 33)
1082.rest: — "'On the day of his wedding' — this is the giving of the Torah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash, may it be built speedily in our days." Yom Kippur is a day of forgiveness, on which the last Tablets were given.

1083.label: Sanhedrin 99a
1083.rest: — "What is meant by 'For a day of vengeance is in My heart' (Yeshayahu 63:4)? Rabbi Yochanan said: To My heart I revealed it; to My limbs I did not reveal it. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: To My heart I revealed it; to the ministering angels I did not reveal it."

1084.label: Mechilta, Beshalach, Shirah 3
1084.rest: — "'This is my God and I will glorify Him' (Shemos 15:2): a maidservant saw at the Sea what Yeshayahu and Yechezkel did not see."

1085.label: Gittin 55b
1085.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: What is meant by 'Fortunate is the man who fears always, but he who hardens his heart shall fall into evil' (Mishlei 28:14)? Because of Kamtza and Bar Kamtza Yerushalayim was destroyed; because of a rooster and a hen Tur Malka was destroyed; because of the shaft of a litter Beitar was destroyed."

1086.label: Yoma 9b
1086.rest: — “The second Temple: they occupied themselves with Torah, commandments, and acts of kindness. Why was it destroyed? Because it contained baseless hatred. This teaches that baseless hatred is equivalent to the three transgressions of idolatry, forbidden relations, and bloodshed. ... Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar both said: The earlier ones, whose sin was revealed, had the end of their exile revealed; the later ones, whose sin was not revealed, did not have their end revealed.” The Gemara contrasts visible religious achievement with destructive hatred and the differing revelation of the exile's end. Rav Tzadok links this inward failure with the concealed opposition of Edom.

1087.label: Gittin 57a
1087.rest: — "'Hashem has swallowed up and not pitied all the dwellings of Yaakov' (Eichah 2:2): when Ravin came, he said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: These are the six hundred thousand towns that King Yannai had in the King's Mountain, and in each one there were as many as those who left Egypt."

1088.label: Berachos 22a
1088.rest: — On Ezra's enactment of immersion for a ba'al keri: "The one who teaches 'hatred' — because of neglect of Torah and neglect of procreation; and the one who teaches 'whisper' — so that Torah scholars should not be found with their wives like roosters."

1089.label: Shabbos 139a
1089.rest: — "If the haughty cease, the magi will cease, as it is written, 'And I will smelt away your dross as with lye, and remove all your alloy' (Yeshayahu 1:25)." Rashi: if Israel cease their haughtiness, the inciters who make us hated will cease.

1090.label: Rashi, Devarim 25:18 (from the Midrash)
1090.rest: — "'Who chilled you (karcha)' — an expression of cold and heat: he cooled you and made you lukewarm from your boiling heat, for all the nations were afraid to fight you, and this one came and began and showed the way to others."

1091.label: Temurah 16a
1091.rest: — "'If You will bless me' — with Torah; 'and enlarge my border' — with students; 'and Your hand be with me' — that my learning be not forgotten from my heart; 'and keep me from evil' — that I find companions like me; 'that it not grieve me (atzbi)' — that the evil inclination not overpower me from learning (I Divrei HaYamim 4:10)."

1092.label: Sanhedrin 46b
1092.rest: — The Gemara asks whether burial is on account of disgrace or on account of atonement, and brings, "They shall not be eulogized nor buried; they shall be as dung upon the face of the ground" (Yirmeyahu 16:4). Rashi: if burial were for atonement, let them be buried and be atoned; rather, the Holy One did not wish them to have atonement.

1093.label: Pesachim 50a
1093.rest: — "Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said: The World to Come is not like this world. In this world, over good tidings one says 'Blessed is He Who is good and does good,' and over bad tidings one says 'Blessed is the true Judge'; in the World to Come it is all 'Who is good and does good.'" Rashi: for there are no bad tidings there.

1094.label: Sanhedrin 93b
1094.rest: — "Bar Koziva reigned two and a half years. He said to the Sages: I am Mashiach. They said to him: Of Mashiach it is written that he discerns by smell and judges; let us see whether he discerns by smell and judges. When they saw that he did not, they killed him."

1095.label: Rambam, Hilchos Melachim 11:3
1095.rest: — "Rabbi Akiva was a great sage among the Sages of the Mishnah, and he was the arms-bearer of Ben Koziva the king, and he said of him that he was King Mashiach; he and all the Sages of his generation imagined that he was King Mashiach, until he was killed in his iniquities."

1096.label: Zohar III 260b (Vaeschanan)
1096.rest: — "Therefore Moshe was the beginning in the world. And if you ask who was the conclusion — since Moshe was the beginning, the conclusion is King Mashiach, for then completeness will be found in the world such as has not been in all generations; at that time there will be completeness above and below, and all the worlds will be in one union, and then it is written, 'On that day Hashem will be One and His Name One' (Zechariah 14:9)."

1097.label: Bava Basra 12a
1097.rest: — "Amemar said: And a sage is greater than a prophet, as it says, 'And a prophet (nevi) has a heart of wisdom' (Tehillim 90:12) — who depends on whom? The lesser on the greater." The Ramban there explains that the Sages' wisdom is a form of ruach hakodesh.

1098.label: Shemos Rabbah 47:3
1098.rest: — "'Write for yourself these words, for according to these words I have made a covenant with you' (Shemos 34:27): Rabbi Yochanan said: … the Written Torah and the Oral Torah — with them I have made a covenant with you."

1099.label: Gittin 60b
1099.rest: — “Rabbi Yochanan said: The Holy One, blessed be He, made a covenant with Israel only on account of the oral teachings, as it says: 'For on the basis of these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.'” The cited verse is Shemos 34:27. The exposition reads al pi as indicating what is transmitted by mouth, explaining why the covenant is identified here particularly with the Oral Torah.

1100.label: Menachos 29b
1100.rest: — “Moshe returned before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said: Master of the world, You have such a person, and You give the Torah through me? He said: Be silent; so it arose in thought before Me. Moshe said: You have shown me his Torah; show me his reward. He said: Turn around. Moshe turned and saw Rabbi Akiva’s flesh being weighed in the market. He said: Master of the world, this is Torah and this its reward? He said: Be silent; so it arose in thought before Me.” The passage follows Moshe’s vision of Rabbi Akiva expounding the crowns of letters. Rav Tzadok’s reading of “before Me” as a level beyond thought is the maamar’s mystical interpretation of the divine response.

1101.label: Yevamos 62b
1101.rest: — Rabbi Akiva's twelve thousand pairs of students died, "and the world was desolate until Rabbi Akiva came to our Rabbis in the South and taught it to them: Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehudah, Rabbi Yosi, Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua; and they are the ones who upheld the Torah at that time."

1102.label: Berachos 5a
1102.rest: — “Rabbi Yochanan said: ... Whoever can occupy himself with Torah but does not do so, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings ugly sufferings upon him and troubles him, as it is said, I became mute in silence; I was silent from good, and my pain was stirred up. Good means nothing other than Torah, as it is said, For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.” Rav Tzadok draws on the identification of good with Torah when reading a good heart as a heart shaped by Torah.

1103.label: Sukkah 49b
1103.rest: — "'And a Torah of kindness is on her tongue' (Mishlei 31:26): is there a Torah of kindness and a Torah not of kindness? … Some say: Torah studied in order to teach it is a Torah of kindness; not in order to teach, a Torah not of kindness." (Rashi has no comment on this line.)

1104.label: Taanis 31a
1104.rest: — "Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: From the fifteenth of Av onward the strength of the sun weakens, and they would no longer cut wood for the altar, because it would not dry… From here on, one who adds will have added to him, and one who does not add will be taken away." Rashi: one who adds nights to his learning will have years added to his life.

1105.label: Eruvin 65a
1105.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said: The night was created only for sleep. Reish Lakish said: The moon was created only for review (girsa). They said to Rabbi Zeira: Your teachings are sharp! He said to them: They are from the daytime."

1106.label: Megillah 32a
1106.rest: — "Rabbi Shefatyah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Whoever reads [Scripture] without melody and learns [Mishnah] without song, of him the verse says, 'And I also gave them statutes that were not good' (Yechezkel 20:25)."

1107.label: Tosafos, Megillah 32a (s.v. v'hashoneh b'lo zimrah)
1107.rest: — "For they were accustomed to learn the Mishnayos with melody, since they learned them by heart, and through this they remembered them better."

1108.label: Rambam, Hilchos Talmud Torah 3:13
1108.rest: — "Even though it is a mitzvah to learn by day and by night, a person learns most of his wisdom only at night. Therefore whoever wishes to merit the crown of Torah should be careful with all his nights and not lose even one of them to sleep, eating, drinking, conversation and the like, but [give them] to Torah study and words of wisdom. The Sages said: The song of Torah is only at night, as it says, 'Arise, cry out at night' (Eichah 2:19); and whoever occupies himself with Torah at night, a thread of kindness is drawn over him by day."

1109.label: Shulchan Aruch, Yoreh De'ah 246:23
1109.rest: — "One who wishes to merit the crown of Torah should be careful with all his nights, and not lose even one of them to sleep, eating, drinking, conversation and the like, but [give them] to Torah study and words of wisdom."

1110.label: Taanis 31a
1110.rest: — "Our Rabbis taught: What would the beautiful ones among them say? Set your eyes on beauty, for a woman is only for beauty. What would the well-born among them say? Set your eyes on family, for a woman is only for children. What would the unattractive among them say? Take your acquisition for the sake of Heaven — only crown us with gold coins."

1111.label: Taanis 26b (Mishnah)
1111.rest: — "And the daughters of Yerushalayim would go out and dance in the vineyards. And what would they say? Young man, lift up your eyes and see what you choose for yourself; do not set your eyes on beauty, set your eyes on family: 'Grace is false and beauty is vain; a woman who fears Hashem, she shall be praised' (Mishlei 31:30)."

1112.label: Bereishis Rabbah 63:3
1112.rest: — Avraham is called Yisrael, and Yitzchak too is called Yisrael, as it says, "And these are the names of the Children of Israel who came to Egypt: Yaakov…" — and Yitzchak is called Avraham, as it says, "These are the generations of Yitzchak son of Avraham — Avraham."

1113.label: Bava Basra 25b
1113.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: One who wishes to become wise should face south, and one who wishes to become rich should face north; and your sign: the Table is in the north and the Menorah in the south." There also: "Out of the north comes gold" (Iyov 37:22).

1114.label: Nedarim 41a
1114.rest: — "Abaye said: We have a tradition: there is no poor man except in knowledge. In the West they say: One who has this has everything in him; one who lacks this — what has he? One who has acquired this — what does he lack? One who has not acquired this — what has he acquired?"

1115.label: Sanhedrin 44a
1115.rest: — "'Yisrael has sinned' (Yehoshua 7:11) — Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is Yisrael."

1116.label: Nedarim 66a
1116.rest: — "At that time Rabbi Yishmael wept and said: The daughters of Israel are beautiful, but poverty makes them unsightly."

1117.label: Berachos 17a
1117.rest: — "Rabbi Alexandri, after his prayer, would say: Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will; and who holds us back? The leaven in the dough and the subjugation to the kingdoms." Rashi: the leaven in the dough — the evil inclination in our hearts, which sours us.

1118.label: Taanis 26b (Mishnah)
1118.rest: — "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no festive days for Israel like the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur, on which the daughters of Yerushalayim would go out in borrowed white garments, so as not to shame one who had none… And so it says, 'Go forth and gaze, O daughters of Tziyon, upon King Shlomo, upon the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart' (Shir HaShirim 3:11): 'on the day of his wedding' — this is the giving of the Torah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash, may it be rebuilt speedily in our days."

1119.label: Taanis 26b (Mishnah 4:8)
1119.rest: — "'On the day of his wedding' (Shir HaShirim 3:11) — this is the giving of the Torah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash, may it be built speedily in our days." Rashi: "his mother" is Knesses Yisrael; "the giving of the Torah" is Yom Kippur, when the second Luchos were given.

1120.label: Tosfos Yom Tov, Taanis 4:8
1120.rest: — "'This is the building of the Beis HaMikdash': the Bartenura explains that it was dedicated on Yom Kippur — that is, Yom Kippur fell within the days of the dedication, as is evident in Melachim I 8… One cannot say that the Second Temple is meant here, for of it Ezra 6 states that it was completed on the third of Adar."

1121.label: Pesikta D'Rav Kahana 13:15
1121.rest: — "The lion (Nevuchadnetzar) came up in the month whose sign is the lion (Av) and destroyed Ariel (the Beis HaMikdash); so the Lion (the Holy One) will come in the month whose sign is the lion and build Ariel."

1122.label: Nedarim 22b
1122.rest: — “Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Yehoshua… as it says, ‘For in much wisdom is much anger’ (Koheles 1:18).”

1123.label: Pesikta D'Rav Kahana 13:15
1123.rest: — "The lion (Nevuchadnetzar) came up in the month whose sign is the lion (Av) and destroyed Ariel (the Beis HaMikdash); so the Lion (the Holy One) will come in the month whose sign is the lion and build Ariel."

1124.label: Taanis 31a
1124.rest: — "Rav Menashya said: And they called it 'the day of the breaking of the axe.' From here on, one who adds will have added to him, and one who does not add will be gathered. Rav Yosef taught: What is 'will be gathered'? His mother will bury him."

1125.label: Tanchuma, Noach 3
1125.rest: — "'A great light' (Yeshayahu 9:1) — the light that was created on the first day, which the Holy One, blessed be He, hid away for those who toil in the Oral Torah by day and by night, in whose merit the world stands, as it says, 'If not for My covenant day and night…' (Yirmeyahu 33:25). Which covenant is practiced by day and by night? This is Talmud."

1126.label: Sanhedrin 99b
1126.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: Every person was created for toil, as it says, 'For man is born to toil' (Iyov 5:7). I do not know whether for toil of the mouth or of labor; when it says, 'for his mouth urges him on' (Mishlei 16:26), it is toil of the mouth. And I still do not know whether toil of Torah or of conversation; when it says, 'This book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth' (Yehoshua 1:8), he was created for the toil of Torah."

1127.label: Sanhedrin 24a
1127.rest: — "What is Bavel? Rabbi Yochanan said: Mixed (belulah) with Scripture, mixed with Mishnah, mixed with Talmud. 'He has set me in dark places, like the long dead' (Eichah 3:6) — Rabbi Yirmeyah said: This is the Talmud of Bavel."

1128.label: Nedarim 22b
1128.rest: — "Rav Ada son of Rabbi Chanina said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Yehoshua alone, which contains the apportioning of Eretz Yisrael. What is the reason? 'For in much wisdom is much anger' (Koheles 1:18)." Rashi: because they rebelled, much wisdom — the other books — was added, to burden them further.

1129.label: Pesachim 109a
1129.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira says: when the Temple stood, there was no rejoicing except with meat, as it says: 'You shall slaughter peace offerings and eat there and rejoice'; now that it does not stand, there is no rejoicing except with wine, as it says: 'And wine gladdens the heart of man.'" (Rashbam's chapter; no Rashi.)

1130.label: Taanis 30b
1130.rest: — "Granted Yom Kippur, because it has pardon and forgiveness, and it is the day on which the second Tablets were given; but the fifteenth of Av — what is it? Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel: It is the day on which the tribes were permitted to marry into one another."

1131.label: Pirkei Avot 4:21
1131.rest: — “Rabbi Elazar HaKappar says: Jealousy, desire, and honor remove a person from the world.” Rav Tzadok maps these three root traits onto the three forms of impurity and the purifying work of the readings.

1132.label: Gittin 55b
1132.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: What is meant by 'Fortunate is the man who fears always, but he who hardens his heart shall fall into evil' (Mishlei 28:14)? Because of Kamtza and Bar Kamtza Yerushalayim was destroyed; because of a rooster and a hen Tur Malka was destroyed; because of the shaft of a litter Beitar was destroyed."

1133.label: Bava Basra 122a
1133.rest: — Elazar would direct himself with ruach hakodesh "and say: Naftali comes up, and the border of Ginosar comes up with it. He drew from the urn of the tribes, and Naftali came up in his hand; he drew from the urn of the borders, and the border of Ginosar came up in his hand; and so with each and every tribe."

1134.label: Rashi, Bamidbar 26:54
1134.rest: — The land was divided by lot, through the holy spirit: Elazar wore the Urim and Tumim and would say, "If such-and-such tribe comes up, such-and-such border comes up with it"; and the lot itself would cry out, "I, the lot, have come up for such-and-such border, for such-and-such tribe."

1135.label: Gittin 57a
1135.rest: — "It was the custom in Beitar: when a boy was born they would plant a cedar, and when a girl was born they would plant a pine; and when they married, they would cut them down and make a wedding canopy."

1136.label: Rambam, Hilchos Melachim 11:3
1136.rest: — "Rabbi Akiva was a great sage among the Sages of the Mishnah, and he was the arms-bearer of Ben Koziva the king, and he said of him that he was King Mashiach; he and all the Sages of his generation imagined that he was King Mashiach, until he was killed in his iniquities."

1137.label: Sanhedrin 86a
1137.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: An anonymous Mishnah is Rabbi Meir; an anonymous Tosefta is Rabbi Nechemiah; an anonymous Sifra is Rabbi Yehudah; an anonymous Sifrei is Rabbi Shimon — and all of them follow Rabbi Akiva."

1138.label: Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6
1138.rest: — "Things that were not revealed to Moshe were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues: 'And every precious thing his eye beheld' (Iyov 28:10) — this is Rabbi Akiva."

1139.label: Gittin 57a
1139.rest: — "'He cut off in fierce anger every horn of Israel' (Eichah 2:3): Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rabbi Abahu in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: These are the eighty thousand war horns that entered the city of Beitar when it was captured, and they killed in it men, women and children until their blood flowed into the Great Sea."

1140.label: Taanis 7a
1140.rest: — "Rabbi Chanina bar Idi said: Why are the words of Torah likened to water, as it is written, 'Ho, all who are thirsty, go to the water' (Yeshayahu 55:1)? To tell you: just as water leaves a high place and goes to a low place, so the words of Torah endure only in one whose mind is humble."

1141.label: Berachos 48b
1141.rest: — "'Who is good and does good' was instituted in Yavneh on account of the slain of Beitar"; the Gemara there also derives it from "which He has given you" (Devarim 8:10).

1142.label: Berachos 5a
1142.rest: — “Rabbi Yochanan said: ... Whoever can occupy himself with Torah but does not do so, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings ugly sufferings upon him and troubles him, as it is said, I became mute in silence; I was silent from good, and my pain was stirred up. Good means nothing other than Torah, as it is said, For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.” Rav Tzadok draws on the identification of good with Torah when reading a good heart as a heart shaped by Torah.

1143.label: Sotah 4b
1143.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: Any person who has haughtiness of spirit is as though he worships idols; it is written here, 'Every haughty heart is an abomination to Hashem' (Mishlei 16:5), and it is written there, 'And you shall not bring an abomination into your house' (Devarim 7:26)."

1144.label: Arachin 15b
1144.rest: — "The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: Whoever speaks lashon hara increases his sins to the measure of three transgressions: idolatry, forbidden relations and bloodshed."

1145.label: Taanis 29a
1145.rest: — "'And the whole congregation raised their voice, and the people wept that night' (Bamidbar 14:1). Rabbah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: That day was the eve of Tisha B'Av. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: You wept a weeping for nothing, and I will establish for you a weeping for generations."

1146.label: Shabbos 56b
1146.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: At the time David said to Mefiboshes, 'You and Tziva shall divide the field' (II Shmuel 19:30), a heavenly voice went forth and said to him: Rechavam and Yeravam shall divide the kingdom." And: "Had David not accepted lashon hara, the kingdom of the house of David would not have been divided."

1147.label: Taanis 31a
1147.rest: — "Rabbah and Rav Yosef both said: It is the day on which they stopped cutting wood for the altar pyre. It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: From the fifteenth of Av onward the strength of the sun weakens, and they would no longer cut wood for the pyre, because it would not dry."

1148.label: Sotah 17a: “Rabbi Akiva expounded: Man and woman
1148.rest: — if they are worthy, the Shechinah is between them; if they are not worthy, fire consumes them”; and Rashi there: “The Shechinah is between them — for He divided His Name and placed it between them, the yud in ish (man) and the heh in ishah (woman).” Take the yud from ish and the heh from ishah and each is left esh, “fire”; together the yud and heh make the Name Y-H, numerically fifteen.

1149.label: Kiddushin 81a
1149.rest: — Rabbi Amram the Pious: "When he reached halfway up the ladder he braced himself and cried aloud: Fire in the house of Amram! … He adjured [the inclination] to leave him, and it left him like a pillar of fire. He said to it: See, you are fire and I am flesh, yet I am better than you."

1150.label: Yoma 69b
1150.rest: — "They sat in fasting three days and three nights, and it was handed over to them. There came forth something like a fiery lion cub from the Holy of Holies. The prophet said to Israel: This is the inclination for idolatry, as it says, 'And he said: This is the wickedness' (Zechariah 5:8)."

1151.label: Taanis 31a
1151.rest: — "Rav Menashya said: And they called it 'the day of the breaking of the axe.' From here on, one who adds will have added to him, and one who does not add will be gathered. Rav Yosef taught: What is 'will be gathered'? His mother will bury him."

1152.label: Taanis 26b (Mishnah)
1152.rest: — "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no festive days for Israel like the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur, on which the daughters of Yerushalayim would go out in borrowed white garments, so as not to shame one who had none… And so it says, 'Go forth and gaze, O daughters of Tziyon, upon King Shlomo, upon the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart' (Shir HaShirim 3:11): 'on the day of his wedding' — this is the giving of the Torah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash, may it be rebuilt speedily in our days."

1153.label: Taanis 30b
1153.rest: — "Granted Yom Kippur, because it has pardon and forgiveness, and it is the day on which the second Tablets were given; but the fifteenth of Av — what is it? Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel: It is the day on which the tribes were permitted to marry into one another."

1154.label: Berachos 55a
1154.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: Betzalel knew how to combine the letters with which heaven and earth were created. It is written here, 'And He filled him with the spirit of God, with wisdom, with understanding and with knowledge' (Shemos 35:31), and there, 'Hashem with wisdom founded the earth, established the heavens with understanding' (Mishlei 3:19), and 'by His knowledge the depths were split.'"

1155.label: Berachos 33a
1155.rest: — “Any person who has da’as, it is as if the Beis HaMikdash were built in his days.”

1156.label: Moed Katan 25b
1156.rest: — From a eulogy: "He was angered at His world and took souls from it, and rejoiced in them as in a new bride; the Rider of the heavens exults and rejoices when a pure and righteous soul comes to Him."

1157.label: Horayos 5a (Mishnah)
1157.rest: — "If the beis din ruled and seven tribes, or a majority of them, acted on their ruling, they bring a bull… Rabbi Yehudah says: The seven tribes that sinned bring seven bulls… Rabbi Shimon says: Eight bulls" — each tribe is reckoned a congregation (kahal) of its own.

1158.label: Taanis 30b
1158.rest: — "Granted Yom Kippur, because it has pardon and forgiveness, and it is the day on which the second Tablets were given; but the fifteenth of Av — what is it? Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel: It is the day on which the tribes were permitted to marry into one another."

1159.label: Zohar II 152a, Terumah
1159.rest: — “Come and see: Tes is the illumination of life in every place. Therefore the verse begins with it in 'that it was good,' as it is written: 'God saw the light, that it was good.' From this letter the destroying angel flees—or rather, he is not given permission to enter there. This letter differs from kuf: kuf is not established in any settled place in the world; its sign is 'A man of evil speech shall not be established in the land.'
