Tes is established in every place and is properly fitted to settle there; wherever tes is, kuf has no settled place. ... Just as this letter rules in this place, so another letter rules in the place of Gehinnom. Which is it? Qof.” The source contrasts tes with kuf in the account of a place protected from death. The retrieved text also preserves a variant reading of ches for kuf. Rav Tzadok's argument follows the kuf reading quoted in his manuscript.

1160.label: Zohar I 2b (Introduction)
1160.rest: — "The letter tes came before Him and said: 'Create the world with me, for through me You are called good (tov) and upright.' He said to it: 'I will not create the world with you, for your goodness is hidden and concealed within you, as it says, "How great is Your goodness which You have hidden for those who fear You" (Tehillim 31:20). Since it is hidden within you, it has no portion in this world that I wish to create, but in the World to Come.'"

1161.label: Pesikta D'Rav Kahana 13:15
1161.rest: — "The lion (Nevuchadnetzar) came up in the month whose sign is the lion (Av) and destroyed Ariel (the Beis HaMikdash); so the Lion (the Holy One) will come in the month whose sign is the lion and build Ariel."

1162.label: Taanis 31a
1162.rest: — "Ulla of Bira said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle dance for the righteous, and He will sit among them in Gan Eden, and each one will point with his finger, as it says, 'And it shall be said on that day: Behold, this is our God; we hoped to Him and He saved us… let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation' (Yeshayahu 25:9)."

1163.label: Shabbos 106b
1163.rest: — "Abaye said to him: 'The halachah' — implying they disagree? He said: What difference does it make to you? He said to him: Learn the received teaching — let it be like a song?" Rashi: saying the teaching as a mere song, to no purpose.

1164.label: Sefer Yetzirah 5
1164.rest: — "He made the letter ches king over sight… and formed with it Sartan (Cancer) in the world, Tammuz in the year."

1165.label: Menachos 29b
1165.rest: — "[The scribes] make a bump (chotrei) on the roof of the Ches, as if to say: He lives (chai) in the heights of the world." Rashi: the roof of the Ches is made with a raised point above, meaning that the Holy One, blessed is He, Who lives forever, dwells in the heights of the world.

1166.label: Kiddushin 39b
1166.rest: — "'That it may go well with you' (Devarim 22:7) — in the world that is entirely good; 'and that your days may be lengthened' — in the world that is entirely long."

1167.label: Zohar II 52b (Beshalach)
1167.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: Then, when everything was illuminated as one, the sea performed supernal laws, and upper and lower were delivered into its hand; therefore all is as hard before the Holy One as the splitting of the Red Sea. Why? Because the splitting of the Red Sea depends on Atika."

1168.label: Mechilta, Beshalach, Shirah 3
1168.rest: — "'This is my God and I will glorify Him' (Shemos 15:2). Rabbi Eliezer says: From where do you say that a maidservant saw at the Sea what Yeshayahu and Yechezkel did not see? For it says, 'and through the prophets I was imaged' (Hoshea 12:11)… When the Holy One, blessed be He, was revealed at the Sea, no one needed to ask, 'Which is the King?'"

1169.label: Bava Basra 115b
1169.rest: — "Abaye said: It is a tradition that a tribe will not be wiped out."

1170.label: Sefer Yetzirah 5
1170.rest: — "Twelve simple letters… He engraved them, hewed them, weighed them, refined them and exchanged them, and formed with them twelve constellations in the world… and these are the twelve months in the year: Nissan, Iyar, Sivan, Tammuz, Av, Elul…; and these are the twelve guides in the soul." Of Av it says: He made the letter tes king and formed with it Aryeh (Leo) in the world and Av in the year.

1171.label: Taanis 30b
1171.rest: — "Rav Yosef said in the name of Rav Nachman: It is the day on which the tribe of Binyamin was permitted to enter the congregation, as it says, 'And the men of Israel had sworn at Mitzpah, saying: None of us shall give his daughter to Binyamin as a wife' (Shoftim 21:1). What did they expound? Rav said: 'None of us' — and not of our children."

1172.label: Taanis 26b (Mishnah)
1172.rest: — "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no festive days for Israel like the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur, on which the daughters of Yerushalayim would go out in borrowed white garments, so as not to shame one who had none… And so it says, 'Go forth and gaze, O daughters of Tziyon, upon King Shlomo, upon the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart' (Shir HaShirim 3:11): 'on the day of his wedding' — this is the giving of the Torah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash, may it be rebuilt speedily in our days."

1173.label: Pesikta D'Rav Kahana 13:15
1173.rest: — "The lion (Nevuchadnetzar) came up in the month whose sign is the lion (Av) and destroyed Ariel (the Beis HaMikdash); so the Lion (the Holy One) will come in the month whose sign is the lion and build Ariel."

1174.label: Sanhedrin 99a
1174.rest: — "What is meant by 'For a day of vengeance is in My heart' (Yeshayahu 63:4)? Rabbi Yochanan said: To My heart I revealed it; to My limbs I did not reveal it. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: To My heart I revealed it; to the ministering angels I did not reveal it."

1175.label: Zohar II 166b
1175.rest: — "This light the Holy One, blessed is He, sowed in His Garden of Eden, and made it into rows upon rows through this Tzaddik, who is the gardener of the Garden. He took this light and sowed it as a seed of truth… and it brought forth and sprouted and produced fruit, from which the world is nourished. This is 'Light is sown for the righteous.'"

1176.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
1176.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

1177.label: Taanis 31a
1177.rest: — "Rav Masna said: It is the day on which the slain of Beitar were given over for burial. And Rav Masna said: On the day the slain of Beitar were given over for burial they instituted in Yavneh 'Who is good and does good': 'Who is good' — that they did not decay; 'and does good' — that they were given over for burial."

1178.label: Taanis 31a
1178.rest: — "The king's daughter borrows from the Kohen Gadol's daughter, the Kohen Gadol's daughter from the deputy's daughter, the deputy's daughter from the daughter of the anointed for war, and the daughter of the anointed for war from the daughter of an ordinary Kohen; and all Israel borrow from one another, so as not to shame one who has none."

1179.label: Sanhedrin 93b
1179.rest: — "Bar Koziva reigned two and a half years. He said to the Sages: I am Mashiach. They said to him: Of Mashiach it is written that he discerns by smell and judges; let us see whether he discerns by smell and judges. When they saw that he did not, they killed him."

1180.label: Rambam, Hilchos Melachim 11:3
1180.rest: — "Rabbi Akiva was a great sage among the Sages of the Mishnah, and he was the arms-bearer of Ben Koziva the king, and he said of him that he was King Mashiach; he and all the Sages of his generation imagined that he was King Mashiach, until he was killed in his iniquities."

1181.label: Gittin 57a
1181.rest: — "His mouth made Bar Daroma stumble, and he said: 'Have You not, O God, forsaken us, and You do not go forth, O God, with our hosts?' (Tehillim 60:12). — But David too said this! — David was saying it in wonder."

1182.label: Kesubos 111a
1182.rest: — The three oaths: that Israel not go up [en masse] as a wall; that Israel not rebel against the nations of the world; and that the nations not subjugate Israel excessively. "And Rabbi Zeira — that one is that Israel should not go up as a wall."

1183.label: Pesachim 87a
1183.rest: — "'I am a wall, and my breasts like towers' (Shir HaShirim 8:10): Rabbi Yochanan said: 'I am a wall' — this is Torah; 'and my breasts like towers' — these are Torah scholars. And Rava said: 'I am a wall' — this is the Congregation of Israel; 'and my breasts like towers' — these are the synagogues and study halls."

1184.label: Sanhedrin 98b
1184.rest: — "Rav Nachman said: If he is among the living, he is someone like me… Rav said: If he is among the living, he is like Rabbeinu HaKadosh; if he is among the dead, he is like Daniel, the man of delights." Rashi: if Mashiach is among those alive now, surely it is Rabbeinu HaKadosh, who bore suffering and was completely pious.

1185.label: Berachos 48b
1185.rest: — "'Who is good and does good' was instituted in Yavneh on account of the slain of Beitar"; the Gemara there also derives it from "which He has given you" (Devarim 8:10).

1186.label: Berachos 5a
1186.rest: — “Rabbi Yochanan said: ... Whoever can occupy himself with Torah but does not do so, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings ugly sufferings upon him and troubles him, as it is said, I became mute in silence; I was silent from good, and my pain was stirred up. Good means nothing other than Torah, as it is said, For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.” Rav Tzadok draws on the identification of good with Torah when reading a good heart as a heart shaped by Torah.

1187.label: Sukkah 49b
1187.rest: — "'And a Torah of kindness is on her tongue' (Mishlei 31:26): is there a Torah of kindness and a Torah not of kindness? … Some say: Torah studied in order to teach it is a Torah of kindness; not in order to teach, a Torah not of kindness." (Rashi has no comment on this line.)

1188.label: Tosafos, Taanis 31a (s.v. tiknu b'Yavneh)
1188.rest: — "'They instituted in Yavneh HaTov veHaMeitiv' — in Birkas HaMazon; and therefore they instituted HaTov veHaMeitiv over wine more than over other things, because [the slain of Beitar] were like a fence in a vineyard, and did not decay."

1189.label: Zohar III 271b, Eikev (Raya Mehemna)
1189.rest: — the wine of the Oral Torah, “Drink of the wine I have mixed.”

1190.label: Taanis 31a
1190.rest: — "Rav Menashya said: And they called it 'the day of the breaking of the axe.' From here on, one who adds will have added to him, and one who does not add will be gathered. Rav Yosef taught: What is 'will be gathered'? His mother will bury him."

1191.label: Tanchuma, Ki Sisa 36
1191.rest: — "'And he was there with Hashem forty days and forty nights' (Shemos 34:28) — how did Moshe know when it was day? When the Holy One, blessed be He, taught him the Written Torah, he knew it was day; and when He taught him orally, Mishnah and Talmud, he knew it was night."

1192.label: Eruvin 65a
1192.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said: The night was created only for sleep. Reish Lakish said: The moon was created only for review (girsa). They said to Rabbi Zeira: Your teachings are sharp! He said to them: They are from the daytime."

1193.label: Megillah 32a
1193.rest: — "Rabbi Shefatyah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Whoever reads [Scripture] without melody and learns [Mishnah] without song, of him the verse says, 'And I also gave them statutes that were not good' (Yechezkel 20:25)."

1194.label: Shabbos 106b
1194.rest: — "Abaye said to him: 'The halachah' — implying they disagree? He said: What difference does it make to you? He said to him: Learn the received teaching — let it be like a song?" Rashi: saying the teaching as a mere song, to no purpose.

1195.label: Taanis 31a
1195.rest: — "Ulla of Bira said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle dance for the righteous, and He will sit among them in Gan Eden, and each one will point with his finger, as it says, 'And it shall be said on that day: Behold, this is our God; we hoped to Him and He saved us… let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation' (Yeshayahu 25:9)."

1196.label: Taanis 26b (Mishnah)
1196.rest: — "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no festive days for Israel like the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur, on which the daughters of Yerushalayim would go out in borrowed white garments, so as not to shame one who had none… And so it says, 'Go forth and gaze, O daughters of Tziyon, upon King Shlomo, upon the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart' (Shir HaShirim 3:11): 'on the day of his wedding' — this is the giving of the Torah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash, may it be rebuilt speedily in our days."

1197.label: Zohar II 135a (Terumah)
1197.rest: — "Gold, silver and copper…: gold — in the secret of the day of Rosh Hashanah, which is a day of gold, a day of judgment, when that side rules, as you say, 'Out of the north comes gold' (Iyov 37:22); and silver — this is Yom Kippur, on which the sins of Israel are whitened like snow, as you say, 'Though your sins be like scarlet, they shall be white as snow' (Yeshayahu 1:18)."

1198.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 41, 81a
1198.rest: — In "Bereishis" are the letters of Tishrei, and this is the second arm, the second day; "He made (yashes) darkness His hiding place" (Tehillim 18:12): remove yashes from bereishis and reish remains — Rosh Hashanah.

1199.label: Shemos Rabbah 52:5 (so too Bamidbar Rabbah 12:8)
1199.rest: — "The Holy One loved Israel; He called them 'My sister, My beloved, My dove, My perfect one' (Shir HaShirim 5:2), and He did not cease loving them until He called them 'My mother,' as it says, 'Listen to Me, My people, and give ear to Me, My nation (le'umi)' (Yeshayahu 51:4) — written 'le'imi,' 'My mother.' Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai stood and kissed him on his head."

1200.label: Shir HaShirim 3:11 as expounded by Chazal (Taanis 26b; Eichah Rabbah, Pesichta 33)
1200.rest: — "'On the day of his wedding' — this is the giving of the Torah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash, may it be built speedily in our days." Yom Kippur is a day of forgiveness, on which the last Tablets were given.

1201.label: Pesikta D'Rav Kahana 13:15
1201.rest: — "The lion (Nevuchadnetzar) came up in the month whose sign is the lion (Av) and destroyed Ariel (the Beis HaMikdash); so the Lion (the Holy One) will come in the month whose sign is the lion and build Ariel."

1202.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 27
1202.rest: — "When he came to destroy it in the fifth [month], none could appease, for the fifth is called Aryeh (lion), as it says, 'A lion has gone up from his thicket' (Yirmeyahu 4:7); and he destroyed the House that is called Ariel, as it says, 'Woe, Ariel, Ariel' (Yeshayahu 29:1)… in the month that is called Ariel."

1203.label: Kerisos 6b
1203.rest: — "Any fast in which the sinners of Israel do not take part is not a fast, for chelbenah has a foul odor, yet Scripture counted it among the spices of the incense."

1204.label: Zohar III 160a, Shelach
1204.rest: — “Furthermore, ‘Amalek dwells in the land of the Negev.’ If a person says that despite all this he will attain it: ‘Amalek dwells in the land of the Negev’—this is the evil inclination, the accuser, who accuses a person and is constantly found in the body. ‘The Hittite and the Amorite’—how many accusers are found there, so that a person cannot enter that world at all. Who will merit it, and who will enter it? With these words ‘they disheartened the children of Israel,’ for they brought out an evil report about it.” The Zohar first portrays the discouraging accusation, then answers it with sincere will and guarding the covenant. This exact context supports Rav Tzadok's identification of Amalek as the accusing root of the inclination.

1205.label: Rashi, Devarim 25:18
1205.rest: — "'Who happened upon you (karcha)' — a term of coldness (kerirus) and heat: he cooled you and made you lukewarm from your boiling heat; for all the nations feared to fight you, and this one came, began, and showed the way to others."

1206.label: Bechoros 5b
1206.rest: — "What is the meaning of Rephidim?… It is a dispute of Tannaim: Rabbi Eliezer says, Rephidim is its name; Rabbi Yehoshua says, that they slackened (rifu) themselves from words of Torah, and so it says, 'Fathers did not turn back to their children for slackness (rifyon) of hands' (Yirmeyahu 47:3)."

1207.label: Kiddushin 81a
1207.rest: — Rav Amram the Pious, overcome by his desire, adjured the evil inclination to leave him: "It went out of him like a pillar of fire. He said to it: See, you are fire and I am flesh, yet I am stronger than you." Rashi has no comment on this line.

1208.label: Yoma 69b
1208.rest: — "They sat in fasting three days and three nights, and it was handed over to them. There came forth something like a fiery lion cub from the Holy of Holies. The prophet said to Israel: This is the inclination for idolatry, as it says, 'And he said: This is the wickedness' (Zechariah 5:8)."

1209.label: Berachos 8a
1209.rest: — "It was taught likewise: Nine hundred and three kinds of death were created in the world, as it says, 'And to God the Lord are the issues (totza'os) of death' (Tehillim 68:21) — totza'os in gematria is that number. The hardest of all is askara; the gentlest of all is the kiss."

1210.label: Shabbos 104a
1210.rest: — "The Rabbis said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: Children came to the study hall today and said things the like of which were not said even in the days of Yehoshua bin Nun: Alef-beis — learn understanding (alef binah); gimmel-dalet — be kind to the poor (gemol dalim)." Rashi: "learn understanding" — the study of Torah.

1211.label: Zohar III 256b (Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas)
1211.rest: — "The first commandment, Anochi, is called so from the side of Kesser, which is Ayin: 'Anochi' — in it is kaf, Kesser, and in it is Ayin."

1212.label: Shabbos 89b
1212.rest: — "'Like scarlet' (kashanim) — it should have said kasheni! R. Yitzchak said: The Holy One, blessed is He, said to Israel: If your sins are like these years (shanim), which stand ordered and come from the six days of Creation until now, they shall become white as snow." Rashi: it should have said kasheni, like "kasheleg," which is not in the plural.

1213.label: Sefer Yetzirah 5
1213.rest: — "Twelve simple letters… He engraved them, hewed them, weighed them, refined them and exchanged them, and formed with them twelve constellations in the world… and these are the twelve months in the year: Nissan, Iyar, Sivan, Tammuz, Av, Elul…; and these are the twelve guides in the soul." Of Av it says: He made the letter tes king and formed with it Aryeh (Leo) in the world and Av in the year.

1214.label: Zohar II 152a (Terumah)
1214.rest: — "Come and see: tes is the light of life in every place, and therefore Scripture opened with it in 'ki tov,' as it is written, 'And God saw the light, that it was good (tov)' (Bereishis 1:4)… From this place the destroying angel flees — do not say flees, but that he is not given permission to enter there."

1215.label: Chagigah 12a
1215.rest: — The light of the first day was hidden away "for the righteous in the future, as it says, 'And God saw the light, that it was good' (Bereishis 1:4), and 'good' means only the tzaddik, as it says, 'Say of the tzaddik that he is good' (Yeshayahu 3:10)."

1216.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48, 85a
1216.rest: — "Fortunate is he who makes them a dwelling on Shabbos in the two chambers of the heart, so that the evil inclination, which is the desecration of Shabbos, is cleared out from there."

1217.label: Rosh Hashanah 10b–11a
1217.rest: — "Rabbi Eliezer says: In Tishrei the world was created; in Tishrei the Patriarchs were born; in Tishrei the Patriarchs died; on Pesach Yitzchak was born; on Rosh Hashanah Sarah, Rachel and Chanah were remembered; on Rosh Hashanah Yosef went out of prison… In Nissan they were redeemed, and in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed. Rabbi Yehoshua says: In Nissan the world was created…; in Nissan they were redeemed, and in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed."

1218.label: Rosh Hashanah 27a
1218.rest: — "Like whom do we pray today, 'This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day'? Like Rabbi Eliezer, who said the world was created in Tishrei." Tosafos there (s.v. kemaan) explain that both views are the words of the living God: in Tishrei it arose in thought to create, and it was not created until Nissan.

1219.label: Taanis 31a
1219.rest: — "Rabbah and Rav Yosef both said: It is the day on which they stopped cutting wood for the altar pyre. It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: From the fifteenth of Av onward the strength of the sun weakens, and they would no longer cut wood for the pyre, because it would not dry."

1220.label: Zohar I 26a (Bereishis)
1220.rest: — "At that time it will be said of Moshe and Israel, 'Then you shall delight (tisaneg) upon Hashem' (Yeshayahu 58:14) — with oneg, which is ayin, Eden; nun, nahar (river); gimel, gan (garden)… and it will be turned for the Erev Rav, from oneg (delight) to nega (plague)."

1221.label: Taanis 31a
1221.rest: — "Ulla of Bira said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle dance for the righteous, and He will sit among them in Gan Eden, and each one will point with his finger, as it says, 'And it shall be said on that day: Behold, this is our God; we hoped to Him and He saved us… let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation' (Yeshayahu 25:9)."

1222.label: Zohar II 52b (Beshalach)
1222.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: Then, when everything was illuminated as one, the sea performed supernal laws, and upper and lower were delivered into its hand; therefore all is as hard before the Holy One as the splitting of the Red Sea. Why? Because the splitting of the Red Sea depends on Atika."

1223.label: Mechilta, Beshalach, Shirah 3
1223.rest: — "'This is my God and I will glorify Him' (Shemos 15:2): a maidservant saw at the Sea what Yeshayahu and Yechezkel did not see."

1224.label: Zohar III 141a (Idra Rabba)
1224.rest: — "'The glory of young men is their strength' (Mishlei 20:29) — and He appeared at the Sea as a fine young man, as it is written, 'Young as the cedars' (Shir HaShirim 5:15), like a mighty warrior performing mighty deeds; and this is the glory of power, might and mercy."

1225.label: Rosh Hashanah 24a (Mishnah)
1225.rest: — "The head of the beis din says 'Mekudash,' and all the people answer after him, 'Mekudash, mekudash.' Whether it was seen in its time or not seen in its time, they sanctify it."

1226.label: Zevachim 91a
1226.rest: — "Come and hear: the mussafin of Shabbos precede the mussafin of Rosh Chodesh. — Is it so that [the sanctity of] Rosh Chodesh is effective for its own mussafin, but not effective for the mussafin of Shabbos?" The Gemara thus weighs the view that the Rosh Chodesh mussafin are more sanctified than those of Shabbos.

1227.label: R. Yosef Chaim of Baghdad, Ben Yehoyada, Rosh Hashanah 11a
1227.rest: — “Those born in Nissan were not complete in their birth, to be counted among the born, until after thirty days, which fall in Iyar. Therefore the Avos, who are the radiance of the world — since their thirty days were completed in Iyar, this radiance is ascribed to Iyar, and so Iyar is called ‘the month of Ziv,’ for their birth was completed in it. And according to the one who says it is called Ziv ‘because it has radiance for the trees’: the blossom comes out in Nissan and covers the body of the fruit, which is the tree's radiance; in Iyar the blossom falls and the body of the fruit is seen.” Connection: He too asks why the Avos' radiance belongs to Iyar rather than Nissan, and answers that what begins in Nissan is completed and revealed only in Iyar.

1228.label: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Iyar 1:2
1228.rest: — “In Sefer Yetzirah: ‘He made the letter vav king over contemplation (hirhur), bound a crown to it… and formed with it Shor in the world, Iyar in the year, and the right kidney in the soul.’ According to what was said above, since the permutation of the Name that shines in Iyar comes from ‘Let him who glories glory in this: that he understands and knows Me’ (Yirmeyahu 9:23), the month is suited to understanding and knowledge, like the tefillin of the head. Therefore the creation of hirhur, which is in the brain of understanding, belongs to this month.” Connection: Both read the Sefer Yetzirah of Iyar as the month for refining contemplation; Bnei Yissaschar ties it to Iyar's permutation of the Name and to Da'as.

1229.label: Radak, Melachim I 6:1
1229.rest: — “‘In the month of Ziv’: this is the month of Iyar, which is the second of the months, for Nissan is the first of the months. It is called Ziv as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained: ‘because it has radiance for the trees,’ meaning the brilliance of the blossoms and buds. And so Yonasan translated ‘in the month of Ziv’ as ‘in the month of blossoms.’” Connection: Radak gives the plain meaning of the one month-name Tanach itself uses, which Rav Tzadok sets beside the names brought from Bavel.

1230.label: R. Avraham Yehoshua Heschel of Apta, Ohev Yisrael, Shabbos after Pesach
1230.rest: — “The permutation of the month of Iyar comes out of the pasuk ‘Let him who glories glory in this: that he understands and knows Me’ (Yirmeyahu 9:23). To understand what connection this pasuk has to this permutation and this month: from the first day of the counting of the Omer until Rosh Chodesh Iyar are two weeks; the first week is in the secret of the mochin of Chochmah, the second in the secret of the mochin of Binah; and from Rosh Chodesh Iyar begins the third week, corresponding to the secret of Da'as. And the essence of the unions of the holy worlds is through the supernal Da'as, as it says, ‘Through knowledge the chambers are filled’ (Mishlei 24:4).” Connection: The same permutation of Havayah for Iyar, explained through the Omer weeks reaching Da'as on Rosh Chodesh Iyar.

1231.label: R. Avraham Azulai, Ohr HaChammah on Zohar III 152b
1231.rest: — “It is a known rule in Sefer Bris Menuchah that a Name of greater level acts even without purity and cleanliness. So too this second Pesach, which is [brought] among the kelipos, must be in the second month, which is of a higher level; and therefore he says it cannot be below, since the lower is grasped only through Malchus. And this is: Israel, the holy seed, who stood in their holiness and were not grasped by the kelipos, who made the Pesach in its time — they took the moon and the sun together.” Connection: A Kabbalistic commentary on the very Zohar Rav Tzadok opens with, explaining why the second month carries a higher light for those who were far.

1232.label: Maharsha, Chidushei Aggados, Niddah 73a
1232.rest: — “For this reason the teaching of Tanna D'vei Eliyahu, ‘Whoever studies halachos…,’ is brought at the end of Megillah: it refers to the laws of niddah, which are the essential body of halachah (gufei halachos). And for the same reason it is brought at the conclusion of this tractate: whoever studies the halachos of this tractate, and does not rely on the stringency of Rabbi Zeira as if every error were thereby corrected, but studies the essential laws of Niddah themselves, will merit the life of the World to Come.” Connection: Maharsha answers Rav Tzadok's question of why this aggadah closes Niddah by tying it to the laws of niddah themselves; Rav Tzadok ties it to the root of tumah that Torah she'b'al peh repairs.

1233.label: Maharal, Tiferes Yisrael 13
1233.rest: — “‘The school of Eliyahu taught: whoever studies halachos every day is assured that he is a ben Olam Haba, as it says, “The ways (halichos) of the world are His” (Chavakuk 3:6) — do not read halichos but halachos.’ The explanation is that halachah is the clarification and refining of the law; therefore it is fitting that halachah should refine the person as well, until he is a ben Olam Haba.” Connection: Maharal explains the promise of “ben Olam Haba” through the nature of halachah as clarification; Rav Tzadok reaches the same promise through the Oral Torah that clarifies the person.

1234.label: Abarbanel, Yechezkel 36:16, citing the Midrash
1234.rest: — “‘Like the tumah of a niddah’ (Yechezkel 36:17), and not like the tumah of a corpse. When a corpse is in the house, the Kohen Gadol does not enter there; but a niddah — he enters the house with her and sits with her. So Israel: had they been likened to the tumah of a corpse, you would say the Shechinah never returns to them; but He likened them to a niddah, with whom the Kohen remains in the house without concern. So the Shechinah dwells with Israel even when they are tamei, as it says, ‘Who dwells with them in the midst of their tumah’ (Vayikra 16:16).” Connection: On the same pasuk Rav Tzadok cites, the Midrash shows that the tumah of niddah is the kind from which return and purity remain possible.

1235.label: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Pesach
1235.rest: — “The mitzvah is to tell of the Exodus every day, for Israel were created only to tell and testify about the Creator, as it says, ‘This people I formed for Myself; they shall tell My praise’ (Yeshayahu 43:21). But before the redemption they could not tell and make clear the glory of His kingship in the world, because of the wicked who hide the light and the truth. Therefore after the redemption they are obligated to tell of the Exodus, for now the mouth of Israel was opened; for before, the power of speech was in exile.” Connection: Both make the telling itself the substance of the mitzvah; Sefas Emes roots it in speech released from exile, Rav Tzadok in the new understanding each person must bring to it.

1236.label: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Pesach
1236.rest: — “The Midrash says: ‘Circlets of gold’ — the spoil of the Sea; ‘points of silver’ — the spoil of Egypt. At the Exodus, all the dross of loves and desires that had spread into the mixture of good and evil was clarified. So too the evil fears had to be clarified out of that mixture, and this was done at the splitting of the Sea; and the salvation of the Sea was for all generations, as it is written, ‘The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever’ (Tehillim 19:10). Therefore it is alluded to as ‘circlets of gold,’ ordered and settled more permanently; while love is called ‘points of silver,’ for the fervor of love is not as permanent as fear.” Connection: The same Midrash read as inner wealth rather than material spoil; Sefas Emes identifies that wealth as the refined fear of Heaven gained at the Sea.

1237.label: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Sivan 1:2
1237.rest: — “In Sefer Yetzirah: ‘He made the letter zayin king over walking, bound a crown to it, combined them one with another, and formed with them Gemini in the world, Sivan in the year, and the left foot in the soul.’ According to this you will understand the precision of ‘on this day’ (Shemos 19:1): on this day He made the letter zayin king over walking; therefore on this very day they came, by walking, to the Torah, for this day is suited for it.” Connection: Bnei Yissaschar likewise joins the “walking” of Sivan in Sefer Yetzirah to the coming to Torah at Sinai.

1238.label: Rabbeinu Bachya, Shemos 10:9
1238.rest: — “It is the festival of Shavuos, the day of the giving of the Torah, of which He had already told him, ‘When you take the people out of Egypt, you will serve God on this mountain’ (Shemos 3:12). One cannot explain it as Pesach, for they made the Pesach in Egypt; nor Sukkos, which has no remembrance at the mountain of God. Rather it is Shavuos, in the month of Sivan, as it is written, ‘In the third month… on this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai’ (Shemos 19:1); and that day was Rosh Chodesh Sivan.” Connection: Like the Pesikta Rav Tzadok cites, Rabbeinu Bachya reads the promise at the burning bush as pointing to the month of Sivan and Matan Torah.

1239.label: Maharal, Derush al HaTorah
1239.rest: — “‘And they journeyed from Refidim’ — the Mechilta brought by Rashi: it already said they came to the wilderness of Sinai! Rather, it compares their journeying to their arrival: just as their arrival at Mount Sinai was in teshuvah, so their journeying from Refidim was in teshuvah. That is, this too was a preparation for receiving the Torah: when they came to the wilderness of Sinai they were returning to Hashem in teshuvah, the reverse of what they had sinned at Refidim, where they had been far from Him; now they came to draw near.” Connection: Maharal also reads the repeated verbs of arrival as stages of preparation, beginning with teshuvah for Refidim.

1240.label: R. Elimelech of Lizhensk, Noam Elimelech, Yisro
1240.rest: — “When a person overcomes himself, shakes himself from his dust, and exerts himself in service, he comes to the great level called ‘the wilderness of Sinai.’ This is ‘They journeyed from Refidim’ — from slackness (rifyon) in Torah and service — ‘and came to the wilderness of Sinai, and encamped (vayachanu) in the wilderness’: vayachanu from chen, grace, for there is great grace in his service and holiness. ‘And Israel encamped’ — they come to great unity, and through it they prevail ‘opposite the mountain,’ the evil inclination, which is called a mountain.” Connection: The same stages of arrival read as inner avodah, with the unity of “vayichan” as the culmination.

1241.label: R. Naftali Tzvi Yehudah Berlin, Haamek Davar, Bamidbar 28:26
1241.rest: — “Onkelos translates ‘in your Atzaros.’ From here the Mishnah regularly calls this festival Atzeres… In Scripture, Atzeres is said only of the seventh day of Pesach and of Shemini Atzeres; [the Mishnah's usage comes] from the Targum of this word. Yet it is still not explained how ‘b'Shavuoseichem’ is translated ‘b'Atzarteichon.’” Connection: The Netziv raises Rav Tzadok's very question, why the Oral tradition and Onkelos call Shavuos Atzeres when the Torah does not.

1242.label: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Sivan 3:1
1242.rest: — “[Israel then had] very great love and did not yet have many new mitzvos to occupy themselves with; so Hashem commanded them mitzvos of setting bounds and separation, which held (la'atzor) in their vessels the fear and the great love they had received; therefore the festival is called Atzeres. This reason suffices for the festival at the time of the giving of the Torah, but not for later times… and indeed in the Torah the festival is not called Atzeres; only Chazal in their days, after Matan Torah, called it Atzeres.” Connection: Bnei Yissaschar also derives “Atzeres” from holding in what was received, the same sense of retention (kelitah) Rav Tzadok brings from the Arizal.

1243.label: Ramban, Vayikra 23:11
1243.rest: — “A week is also called ‘Shabbos,’ as in ‘those coming in on the Shabbos with those going out on the Shabbos’ (Melachim II 11:9); for since every seven days contain one Shabbos, and the count of the days is from it, one week is called one ‘Shabbos’ — a usage familiar in the words of our Rabbis… It is possible that every ‘Shabbos’ in this passage means a week.” Connection: Ramban shows in the plain meaning that each week of the count is named for its Shabbos, the link Rav Tzadok develops between Shavuos and the holiness of Shabbos.

1244.label: R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushas Levi, Shavuos
1244.rest: — “Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, added one day on his own, and the Holy One agreed with him, so the receiving of the Torah was on the fifty-first day. But the great illumination of receiving the Torah was essentially on the sixth of Sivan, through Moshe Rabbeinu; for it was in the mind of the Holy One to give it on the sixth of Sivan, and only in deed was it on the seventh, because Moshe added on his own. It follows that on the sixth of Sivan they were ready to receive the Torah, their impurity had ceased, and the Holy One was ready to give it.” Connection: Kedushas Levi answers the Magen Avraham's question in the same direction: the sixth of Sivan is the time of the giving from Above, even though the Torah was received on the seventh.

1245.label: R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushas Levi, Shavuos
1245.rest: — “In Pesachim 68b we say: ‘All agree regarding Atzeres that we also require “for you.”’ That is, on Pesach a person rejoices because his body rejoices at going out from slavery, which is a bodily good. But on Shavuos the joy is over the giving of the Torah, and it would be hard for the body to rejoice, since Matan Torah is only a spiritual good. Therefore they said that on Atzeres we also require ‘for you’: that the body should rejoice, believing that the Torah is the life of the World to Come and of this world.” Connection: The same Gemara read, as Rav Tzadok reads it, as the inclusion of the body's enjoyment in the holiness of Matan Torah.

1246.label: R. Avraham Dov of Ovruch, Bas Ayin, Shavuos
1246.rest: — “[Rav Yosef had] true humility, as it says (Sotah 49b), ‘Do not teach “humility,” for I am here,’ and he felt no good trait in himself. Therefore he said: ‘Were it not for this day that brought it about’ — were it not for this day, which shows us that humility is a great virtue, through which the Torah was given to us as a gift and is called ‘the giving of our Torah’ — ‘how many Yosefs are there in the marketplace,’ for he did not regard himself as having any good trait.” Connection: Bas Ayin reads Rav Yosef's words as humility that credits everything to the gift of the day, the inner side of the plain reading Rav Tzadok starts from.

1247.label: R. Avraham Yehoshua Heschel of Apta, Ohev Yisrael, Vayakhel
1247.rest: — “[At Sinai each one of Israel received] two crowns; afterward, when they sinned with the Calf, this departed from them, as it says, ‘And the Children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Chorev’ (Shemos 33:6): all the illumination of holiness they had received at Chorev was lost. All the lights and crowns, the ornaments of Israel taken from them at Chorev, Moshe Rabbeinu took for himself. But Moshe is a faithful servant, and on holy Shabbos, when holiness rests upon Israel, he returns the crowns to each one of Israel, and each receives according to his holiness, as is known from the Arizal's kavanah on ‘Moshe rejoiced in the gift of his portion.’” Connection: The ornaments stripped at Chorev, which Rav Tzadok explains from the Zohar, are here shown returning each Shabbos through Moshe.

1248.label: R. Chanoch Zundel, Etz Yosef on Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2
1248.rest: — “‘When Israel heard “You shall have no other,” the evil inclination was uprooted from their heart.’ The evil inclination takes hold of the filth within a person; and since the filth of Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, ceased, there was no place for the evil inclination to take hold, and it was uprooted from their heart… But when they said to Moshe, ‘You be the messenger between us,’ they sinned in this, for they had seen that Hashem spoke with them and they lived; and the evil inclination returned to its place.” Connection: The commentator on the same Midrash explains how the uprooted inclination could return, which bears directly on Rav Tzadok's question of why words of Torah were still needed.

1249.label: Pri Tzaddik, Metzora 1
1249.rest: — “[It is written of the time of Matan Torah] ‘engraved upon the Tablets,’ and it says (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2): when Israel heard ‘I am,’ the Torah was implanted in their heart… when they heard ‘You shall have no other,’ the evil inclination was uprooted from their heart. That is: from the utterance ‘I am,’ the Torah was implanted in the heart — ‘a wise man's heart is at his right’ — and this is the sum of all the positive commandments; and from ‘You shall have no other,’ the evil inclination was uprooted in all the negative commandments. Therefore it was then permitted to offer leaven, for then it shows the nullification of the leaven in the dough.” Connection: Rav Tzadok elsewhere maps the two halves of the Midrash onto the positive and negative commandments, and ties them to the leavened Two Loaves of Shavuos.

1250.label: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Sivan 8:2
1250.rest: — “Malchus is the mouth, and we call it Torah she'b'al peh; therefore the secret of the kingship of the House of David, which is the secret of the Oral Torah, came forth from Rus. Therefore David, the secret of the Oral Torah, was born on Shavuos, the day of the giving of the Written Torah, to bind the Written Torah with the Oral Torah in complete unity; and therefore we read Megillas Rus [on Shavuos].” Connection: Bnei Yissaschar too ties David's birth on Atzeres and the reading of Rus to the Oral Torah, the Malchus that joins the Written Torah given that day.

1251.label: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Shabbos Chol HaMoed Sukkos
1251.rest: — “[The Shema] is called the acceptance of the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, and it is written, ‘And you shall love…’: the mitzvah is that the acceptance of the yoke be with love and joy, not like a worldly yoke that is hard on a person. So in Pesachim 68b: ‘All agree regarding Atzeres that we also require “for you.” Why? It is the day on which the Torah was given’; and Rashi explains, to show that this day on which the Torah was given is pleasing and welcome to Israel — even though the mitzvos were not given for enjoyment but as a yoke.” Connection: The same Rashi is read as the demand that the yoke of Torah itself be received with delight, which is Rav Tzadok's theme.

1252.label: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Tammuz and Av 1:1
1252.rest: — “The permutation of the Name for the month of Tammuz is entirely reversed, and it indicates judgment. From this permutation came the judgment upon wicked Haman, when he said, ‘All this is worth nothing to me’ (Esther 5:13). Therefore judgment rules in this month, even before the seventeenth of Tammuz, for those were the days of the spies' journey, and those days are not days of the strengthening of mercy. And the permutation of the month of Av begins reversed…” Connection: Both read Tammuz's reversed permutation of Havayah as the sign of judgment; Bnei Yissaschar links it to the spies and to Haman.

1253.label: R. Yosef Chaim of Baghdad, Ben Yehoyada, Shevuos 10a
1253.rest: — “‘Rosh Chodesh is also called mo'ed’ (Bamidbar 29:39). Besides the fact that in the future every Rosh Chodesh will be a full festival, after the rectification of the sin of the Calf is complete, as is known — even now there is a reason to call it mo'ed, because the fixing of the festivals depends on it.” Connection: Ben Yehoyada gives the hidden future festival of Rosh Chodesh that Rav Tzadok reads into “He proclaimed a mo'ed against me.”

1254.label: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Tammuz and Av 1:2
1254.rest: — “In Sefer Yetzirah: ‘He made the letter ches king over sight… and formed with them Cancer in the world, Tammuz in the year, and the right hand in the soul’; and afterward, ‘He made the letter tes king over hearing… and formed with them Leo in the world, Av in the year, and the left kidney in the soul.’ You see that the letters ches and tes rule these two months; and this is alluded to in ‘Yerushalayim has sinned greatly (chet chat'ah)’ (Eichah 1:8).” Connection: The same Sefer Yetzirah passage, read for the letters that govern Tammuz and Av.

1255.label: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Tammuz and Av 1:7
1255.rest: — “The breaking among the primordial kings was in the aspect of the eyes, and in the aspect of the ear there is repair and life, in the secret of ‘Listen, and your soul shall live’ (Yeshayahu 55:3). Therefore, when the month came that is in the aspect of hearing, as was said, repair came about for the aspect of sight; therefore in it the mountaintops were seen.” Connection: Bnei Yissaschar too makes the hearing of Av the repair of the failure of sight, the movement Rav Tzadok traces from Tammuz to Av.

1256.label: R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushas Levi, Shabbos Nachamu
1256.rest: — “The month of Av: Av is the initials of arur (‘cursed’) and baruch (‘blessed’) — at first, until the fifteenth of Av, arur, and from the fifteenth of Av, baruch. So too the permutation of this month, from ‘Haskes ushma Yisrael hayom’ (Devarim 27:9), indicates growth after absence and completeness after lack; and ‘haskes’ is as our Sages said (Berachos 63b): first ‘has,’ be silent, and afterward ‘kases,’ break apart [in study].” Connection: The same verse of the month's permutation, read as the turn from loss to rebuilding that Rav Tzadok finds in Av.

1257.label: Maharsha, Chidushei Aggados, Taanis 26b
1257.rest: — “‘And so it says, “Go forth and gaze… on the day of his wedding” — this is the giving of the Torah.’ Rashi: Yom Kippur, when the last Tablets were given. And the Bartenura added: ‘and on the day of the joy of his heart — this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash,’ which was dedicated on Yom Kippur. I do not know that it was dedicated on Yom Kippur; according to the context it appears to refer to the fifteenth of Av, for the reasons for its joy given in the Gemara all depend on the building of the Beis HaMikdash.” Connection: Maharsha assigns “the joy of his heart” to the fifteenth of Av, the pairing of the two days that Rav Tzadok explains.

1258.label: Pri Tzaddik, Bamidbar 18
1258.rest: — “The light is the aspect of the first light that was hidden… and the sun, whose body is fire, is as the first light was before it was hidden. The nations count by the sun as it is now, in its sheath; but of the future it is written, ‘The light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun’ (Yeshayahu 30:26). It follows that the sun in this world is truly only an aspect of light, like the moon that receives from the light of the sun.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the sun receives from the hidden light”; both read the moon's future light through the sun that itself receives.

1259.label: Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 7
1259.rest: — “‘The King said: My son has not yet regained his radiance (ziv)… so the Holy One said: the radiance of My children has not yet come, from the bondage of mortar and bricks; rather, let them be refreshed…’ Ziv is the attribute of Yosef the tzaddik… as the Zohar (III 117b) says, he is the radiance of the blessings, from whom radiance goes out to the world, and therefore it is called the month of Ziv. Surely it does not mean that they were to be healed of the blemishes from the bondage, for Hashem could heal them in a moment; rather, their radiance had not yet come, for they had not yet been refined in the attribute of Ziv, Yesod, through the counting of seven times seven.” Connection: Rav Tzadok reads the same Midrash there as the Sefirah's refinement leading to Matan Torah, tying it to the name Ziv as he does here.

1260.label: Pri Tzaddik, Shemini 7
1260.rest: — “‘Come, eat of My bread’ — this is the bread of the Written Torah, and the wine of the Oral Torah. This is the precision of the wording, ‘and drink of the wine I have mixed,’ and it does not say ‘of My wine,’ as it says ‘of My bread.’… And the Oral Torah comes to repair the great anger… and immediately after it is written, ‘Sustain me with ashishos, spread me with apples, for I am lovesick.’” Connection: The same reading of “the wine I have mixed” as the Oral Torah, joined to the same verse of Shir HaShirim.

1261.label: Pri Tzaddik, Balak 14
1261.rest: — “At the third meal we sing ‘Wondrous Counselor,’ as it says, ‘For You have done wonders, counsels from afar’ (Yeshayahu 25:1): counsel comes from afar, that is, from a supernal place. And they said, ‘The kidneys give counsel’ — from afar, from the root, as it says, ‘Behold, You desire truth in the inward parts, and in the hidden part You make me know wisdom’ (Tehillim 51:8); for the counsel of the kidneys is from the root. And the Torah says, ‘Counsel and wisdom are mine’ (Mishlei 8:14): through words of Torah one can also reach counsel from afar, from the root.” Connection: Both read “the kidneys give counsel” through “For You have done wonders, counsels from afar,” locating the kidneys' counsel in the hidden root.

1262.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Av 6
1262.rest: — “In Sefer Yetzirah: ‘He made the letter tes king over hearing… and Av in the year, and the left kidney in the soul.’ We must understand what connection the kidney has to hearing; the ear would seem more fitting… The essence of hearing is that it enter the heart, not only that it enter the ear like a funnel that takes in on one side and lets out on the other.” Connection: The same passage of Sefer Yetzirah for Av, asking, as here for Iyar, why the month's faculty is joined to a kidney.

1263.label: Pri Tzaddik, Kedoshim 12
1263.rest: — “This parashah is always read in the month of Iyar, for it says in Sefer Yetzirah, ‘He made the letter vav king over thought… and Iyar in the year’; all the days of the Sefirah are to rectify this blemish, as the Arizal wrote, and it is alluded in omer having the numerical value of keri. And the main part is in Iyar, created through the vav in thought; and the vav includes two vavs: the vav of truth, the attribute of Yaakov, who was like Adam before the corruption, and the filler vav of Yosef the tzaddik, who overcame his inclination… All the days of the Sefirah are to purify themselves from the impurity of Egypt, to be pure vessels ready to receive the Torah.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “omer equals keri”; both join Sefer Yetzirah's vav of Iyar, Yaakov and Yosef, and the Sefirah's repair of the covenant.

1264.label: Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 15
1264.rest: — “‘In the third month’: according to what is written in R. Chaim Vital's gloss on the Zohar (II 11b), that Moshe was not recognized in the supernal radiance until three months, R. Chaim Vital wrote that these are Nissan, Iyar and Sivan, corresponding to Chesed, Gevurah and Tiferes. And the festival of Shavuos is Tiferes, as it says (Berachos 58a), ‘and the Tiferes — this is Matan Torah,’ which includes all three middos, corresponding to the letter vav, which is called the letter of truth.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “Tiferes and the giving of the Torah”; both build on R. Chaim Vital's Nissan–Iyar–Sivan as Chesed, Gevurah and Tiferes.

1265.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Sivan 4
1265.rest: — “Iyar corresponds to Yitzchak Avinu, according to what is said in the Zohar (I 142a), ‘and the darkness He called night — this is Yitzchak, who is darkness’… Yitzchak was the first to be circumcised at eight days, and then the preparation was made for Knesses Yisrael, the seed of Yaakov, to shine out of the darkness. And the month of Sivan corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, who includes the attributes of Avraham and Yitzchak, Chesed and Gevurah.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “Nissan, Iyar and Sivan correspond to Chesed, Gevurah and Tiferes, and Iyar to Gevurah”; both assign Iyar to Yitzchak's Gevurah.

1266.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Nisan 3
1266.rest: — “In Sefer Yetzirah: ‘He made the letter hei king over speech (sichah)… and Nissan in the year and the right foot in the soul’ — so is the Arizal's version. The lower hei is the lower Shechinah, Malchus; and in Nissan began the building of the Jewish nation… and Israel's strength is only in their mouths… And it says ‘speech’ (sichah) rather than ‘word’ (dibbur), as it says (Eruvin 54b), ‘Sichu — these are the masters of the Talmud, all of whose speech is words of Torah.’” Connection: Rav Tzadok's treatment of the Sefer Yetzirah line for Nissan, the other half of the versions compared here.

1267.label: Pri Tzaddik, Devarim 8
1267.rest: — “‘The good lamp that shines upon the heads’: in the Gemara (Niddah 30b) the verse ‘When His lamp shone above my head’ is expounded of the fetus in its mother's womb, that a lamp is lit above its head and it gazes from one end of the world to the other — the same language as of the light created on the first day (Chagigah 12a)… In its mother's womb it does not yet have the evil inclination, which rules from the moment of birth, while the soul is given from conception (Sanhedrin 91b); so it too is in the aspect of a tzaddik, and therefore a lamp is lit above its head… And so on Shabbos.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the evil inclination has no power over a fetus in its mother's womb”; both read the lamp above the head as the hidden first light.

1268.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 23
1268.rest: — “In the time of Yoshiyahu, even though they had a Mikdash, because they had been wicked in the days of Menashe and Amon and did not take it to heart until the eighteenth year of Yoshiyahu's reign, when Chilkiyahu found the Sefer Torah… [the Pesach came] with great awakening and renewal; and in the Gemara (Shabbos 56b), ‘There is none greater among the baalei teshuvah than Yoshiyahu in his generation.’” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other account of a Pesach brought out of distance and return, carried by the newness of the baal teshuvah's longing.

1269.label: Pri Tzaddik, Lag BaOmer 8
1269.rest: — “So too the Sefirah of Hod begins on Pesach Sheni, and it says (Ra'aya Mehemna, Zohar III 152b): the first Pesach is from the right, where Chochmah is; the second Pesach is from the left, where Binah is… And Moshe said to them, ‘Stand, and I will hear’ — that is, that they pray and cry out to Hashem, ‘Why should we be diminished’; and through this they made it into words of Torah and merited Pesach Sheni.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “Pesach Sheni and Hod”; both set Pesach Sheni at the start of Hod and see its parashah as Torah born of the people's own cry.

1270.label: Pri Tzaddik, Lag BaOmer 1
1270.rest: — “This was on Lag BaOmer, in the Sefirah of Hod of Hod; and Hod is the attribute of Aharon the Kohen, for the seven shepherds correspond to the seven middos (as the Zohar Chadash, Toldos, counts them), and he too was a root of the Oral Torah. For Moshe Rabbeinu was the root of the Written Torah, and Aharon…” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “Hod is the Oral Torah”; both tie the Sefirah of Hod to the Oral Torah.

1271.label: Pri Tzaddik, Lag BaOmer 8
1271.rest: — “The first Pesach is from the right, where Chochmah is; the second Pesach is from the left, where Binah is. That is, the exile of Egypt was a preparation for Matan Torah, and on the first Pesach they merited being ready for Matan Torah, Chochmah, which is ‘Torah is light’… But Pesach Sheni, when it was no longer the time of the Exodus…” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “Pesach Sheni and Hod”; both read the Zohar's first and second Pesach as two different directions of holiness.

1272.label: Takanas HaShavin 10
1272.rest: — “The first: teshuvah out of love, and through it one repairs what came before, for through teshuvah out of love intentional sins become as merits (Yoma 86b)… Through teshuvah out of love it becomes clear that even the hour of sin before the teshuvah he did not do it from his heart at all, but only an act of youth and folly, as they said (Sotah 3a), a person does not sin unless a spirit of folly enters him… for in truth all Israel's heart is toward Heaven.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's fuller account of the repair at the root through which intentional sins become merits, the meaning he gives Pesach Sheni here.

1273.label: Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Parah 2
1273.rest: — “‘These things I have done’ — it does not say ‘I will do,’ but ‘I have done’: for R. Akiva and his companions; things not revealed to Moshe were revealed to R. Akiva and his companions… That is, through the Oral Torah, which is the much wisdom, one can repair the much anger even after the corruption; and this is the power of the Oral Torah, for R. Akiva was the root of the Oral Torah, as the Arizal wrote, and this is the fiftieth gate, revealed to the baal teshuvah.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the wisdom of R. Akiva and the attainment of the fiftieth gate”; both make R. Akiva the root of the Oral Torah.

1274.label: Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 3
1274.rest: — “This whole parashah speaks of the holiness of Aharon, and it begins with the oil, which is Aharon's power and dedication to make the light of the Oral Torah shine in Israel; and this was needed only after the corruption of the mixed multitude, as it says (Nedarim 22b), ‘Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah…’ for ‘in much wisdom is much anger’: to repair the much anger, much wisdom was needed.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the abundance of the light of the Oral Torah as a result of sins that need repair”; the same reading of Nedarim 22b.

1275.label: Pri Tzaddik, Tzav 2
1275.rest: — “Certainly all Israel live in the World to Come, only through Hashem, Who revives them, and they are like a new creation… but ‘that his dust be stirred’ means that death will be only like sleep and awakening, according to what it says (Sotah 21a), ‘When you lie down, it will watch over you — this is death; and when you awake, it will speak for you — in the World to Come.’ This one merits only who made himself a neighbor to the dust in his lifetime, lowly as dust in his own eyes.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “death for Israel is like sleep”; both read Sotah 21a this way.

1276.label: Pri Tzaddik, Balak 13
1276.rest: — “Yaakov Avinu, whose eating was in holiness and who did not know the pleasure of the body at all, being like Adam before the corruption, merited eternal life and did not die. And even though burial and embalming are written of him, it was only like sleep, as it says, ‘Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust’ (Yeshayahu 26:19). And so it is expounded (Sotah 21a), ‘When you walk, it will guide you — in this world; when you lie down, it will watch over you — this is death; and when you awake, it will speak for you — in the time to come.’” Connection: Rav Tzadok elsewhere applies the same verse and Gemara to Yaakov, whose death was only sleep.

1277.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 4
1277.rest: — “We have been precise in what it says (Berachos 9b) of Rav Bruna, who rejoiced in a mitzvah: once he joined geulah to tefillah, and laughter did not leave his mouth all that day — how was laughter permitted to him, if even the laughter of a mitzvah is forbidden? But in truth laughter and joy are one matter; only joy is in the heart, and laughter is…” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “joining geulah to tefillah”; both weigh what Rav Bruna's joining of geulah to tefillah truly achieved.

1278.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 1
1278.rest: — “After the corruption, much wisdom was needed to repair the much anger, and of this it says, ‘and you shall eat the grass of the field.’ And this is what is expounded in the Zohar: ‘And they embittered their lives with hard labor’ — with kushya; ‘with mortar’ — with kal vachomer; ‘and with bricks’ — with the clarification of halachah; ‘and with all labor in the field’ — this is the Baraisa.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “through rectifying the much anger they come to much wisdom”; both make the Oral Torah the repair of “much anger.”

1279.label: Pri Tzaddik, Shelach 6
1279.rest: — “There is the Tree of Life and there is the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil; and through teshuvah one can make the Tree of Knowledge very good, intentional sins becoming merits, and it too becomes the Tree of Life. And the mekoshesh thought that perhaps Hashem's will was that they first go astray and afterward repent, and that from this would come ‘very good,’ a still higher level, as they said (Berachos 34b), ‘In the place where baalei teshuvah stand, complete tzaddikim cannot stand.’” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “sin in Israel is not essential but arranged in advance by God”; both weigh the standing of the baal teshuvah through the same Gemara.

1280.label: R. Mordechai Yosef of Izhbitz, Mei HaShiloach, Mishlei 24:27
1280.rest: — “‘Prepare your work outside’: first a person must keep all the mitzvos in their plain sense, being very careful in all the negative commandments and turning from evil. ‘And make it ready in the field’: field means spreading out, that all the prohibitions spread out to him in fences and all the stringencies of the words of the Scribes… ‘And make it ready’ is an expression of permanence and strength, for the fences and safeguards sustain the body of the mitzvah. ‘Afterward you shall build your house’: after you have grown yourself in strength and are fenced on every side, you will be permitted to spread yourself in all your desire, and will need no fence.” Connection: The Izhbitzer reads the same verse as a sequence of stages in service, as Rav Tzadok does with the Gemara's sequence of Mikra, Mishnah and Gemara.

1281.label: Pri Tzaddik, Mishpatim 4
1281.rest: — “The essence of the first sin was in eating, as it says, ‘And the woman saw that the tree was good for food’; and from this followed also the desire for immorality, as it says (Shabbos 146a), that he injected filth into her; and also through lashon hara… And to this Chazal alluded (Sanhedrin 38b), ‘Adam HaRishon drew his foreskin’ — that is, the first blemish of the covenant; ‘and Adam HaRishon was a heretic’ — that he inclined to the serpent's view.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other reading of Sanhedrin 38b as the root blemish of the covenant, the subject of this siyum.

1282.label: Pri Tzaddik, Shelach 13
1282.rest: — “The expression ‘tying crowns’ is the power of the Oral Torah, as we find (Menachos 29b) in this very language: ‘There is a man who is destined to expound upon each and every crownlet heaps upon heaps of halachos.’ And so we find in the Gemara (Megillah 28b): ‘And one who makes use of the crown (taga)’ — of one who studies halachos, the crown of the Torah; for the crowns are halachos, the aspect of the Oral Torah.” Connection: The same reading of Megillah 28b: the “crown” of the Torah is the halachos of the Oral Torah.

1283.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, the First Night of Pesach 5
1283.rest: — “‘Whoever expands upon the telling of the Exodus is praiseworthy.’ We must understand why here it is not said of one who expands in the telling, ‘Have you finished all the praises of your Master?’ — as we find in the Gemara (Megillah 25a), of the one who went down before R. Chanina and added many praises, and he told him, ‘Have you finished the praises of your Master?… It is like a man who has thousands upon thousands of gold dinars, and they praise him for silver dinars; is it not a disgrace to him?’” Connection: The Radziner asks why expanding is praised in the Haggadah when expanding praise is elsewhere censured, the same question of what “expanding” must add that drives Rav Tzadok here.

1284.label: Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas HaShabbos 1
1284.rest: — “This is the treasury of the fear of Heaven, the only thing the Holy One has in His world, for it is not decreed but depends on man's choice, as it says, ‘Everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven’… And ‘man is born to toil’; even of Adam HaRishon before the sin it is said, ‘And He placed him in the Garden to work it and to guard it.’” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other use of “man is born to toil,” as the work for which man was made even before the sin.

1285.label: Kuntres Es HaOchel 10
1285.rest: — “In the Zohar matzah is called ‘the food of healing’ (II 40b), for it has the power to heal what came before; and so with every mitzvah, as stated above from the Midrash Rabbah… as it is written of words of Torah, ‘It shall be healing to your navel’ (Mishlei 3:8).” Connection: The same Zohar on matzah as the food of healing, which Rav Tzadok explains here as healing the root of desire.

1286.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 52
1286.rest: — “‘We will make you circlets of gold with points of silver.’ In the Midrash: ‘circlets of gold’ — the spoil of the Sea; ‘points of silver’ — the spoil of Egypt… We have already said that the meaning is not silver and gold, for that was not a tiding to Avraham Avinu… rather the intent is love and fear, for in the holy Zohar fear is called gold and silver is longing and love. Now everywhere love is greater than fear, and here it says the spoil of the Sea, gold, fear, is greater than the points of silver, love… But it is written, ‘What does Hashem your God ask of you but to fear.’” Connection: The same Midrash read the same way, gold as fear and silver as love.

1287.label: Pri Tzaddik, Shelach 7
1287.rest: — “‘The fear of Hashem is pure’ (Tehillim 19:10), and in the Yerushalmi (Demai 4:1): the awe of Shabbos is upon the unlearned, for even an unlearned person has the awe of Shabbos upon him. And this is what he said, that even its leaves, the unlearned, give off the fragrance of the World to Come; and this is at the entrance of Shabbos… And the Tree of Life refers to the Holy One, Who is called an apple tree, as it says, ‘Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my Beloved among the sons.’” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other reading of the fragrance of Gan Eden and the apple tree as the holiness that reaches every Jew at Shabbos.

1288.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Nisan 1
1288.rest: — “And the right foot in the soul, even though speech has no connection to the foot; whereas in the month of Sivan, where it says ‘He made the letter zayin king over walking… and the left foot in the soul,’ walking fits the foot, which is not so with speech. But in truth with Hashem we find walking in speech, as it says, ‘And they heard the voice of Hashem God walking in the Garden’… And in words of Torah we find, ‘Happy are those whose way is perfect, who walk in the Torah of Hashem’; and in the Gemara (Eruvin 54b), ‘and walkers — these are the masters of Scripture.’” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the Torah is called walking”; the same Sefer Yetzirah line for Sivan read as walking in Torah.

1289.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 3
1289.rest: — “Nissan is first of the months of the year of the moon, and Tishrei the new year for the years of the sun; and this is called shanah, from shoneh, for it returns and goes round as before and has no renewal. But Israel count by the moon, the aspect of the moon that receives from the sun, whose light is renewed every month.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “renewal in Israel”; both rest Israel's power on renewal, which Rav Tzadok here asks of words of Torah, “as if new.”

1290.label: Pri Tzaddik, Yisro 10
1290.rest: — “From here, that their coming to the wilderness of Sinai was with great longing and with abandonment and separation from all the desires of this world; for in Egypt they had been sunk in its impurity… and the husk of Egypt was evil longings and desires, and they distanced themselves from every desire, and their longing to receive the Torah was strong, as it says, ‘I remember for you the kindness of your youth, your going after Me in the wilderness’ (Yirmeyahu 2:2)… and it teaches us how to come to such longing, and of this it says, ‘And they journeyed from Refidim.’” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the longing for receiving the Torah that Israel had on entering the wilderness”; both read the journey from Refidim the same way.

1291.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5
1291.rest: — “At the time of creation the month was created with this letter, this power and this limb, that is, before the corruption, as ‘God made man upright’… And in this month it was fitting that Moshe bring down the first Tablets, and it would have been the true rectification, as it says, ‘I said: You are G-dly beings’ — for they would not have died (Avodah Zarah 5a).” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other reading of “I said: You are G-dly beings” as the state of the first Tablets, here tied to Sivan.

1292.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeira 2
1292.rest: — “It says (Bereishis Rabbah 8): When the Holy One came to create Adam HaRishon, the ministering angels formed groups; some said, ‘Let him not be created,’ and some said, ‘Let him be created’; this is what is written, ‘Kindness and truth met, righteousness and peace kissed’ (Tehillim 85:11)… the angels of peace are the attribute of Yosef the tzaddik. And we have already spoken of what it says there, ‘He took truth and cast it to the earth,’ — and did not peace also say, ‘Let him not be created, for he is all strife’? Yet it is not mentioned what was done with peace.” Connection: The same Midrash and the same question, what answered the objection of Peace, which Rav Tzadok takes up here.

1293.label: Yisrael Kedoshim 8
1293.rest: — “Then Parshas Parah: to purify the impure through an awakening of holiness from his own side and his own effort, for in this is the purification from the impurity of the dead, through the dew of Torah that revives him (Kesubos 111b), through killing oneself over words of Torah, for it is written, ‘A man, when he dies in a tent’ (Bamidbar 19:14) (Berachos 63b; Shabbos 83b).” Connection: The same Gemara, Torah endures only in one who kills himself over it in the tent of Torah, read as purification.

1294.label: Pri Tzaddik, Va'era 6
1294.rest: — “The Zohar (II 166b): this light the Holy One sowed in His Garden of Eden… and the first light is destined to bring forth offspring for the World to Come… even every day, for were it not for this light the world could not stand… The world was created through the Torah, as it says, ‘I was His instrument’; and afterward, in His goodness He renews each day the work of creation through the renewal of halachos that the Holy One renews each day, and after Matan Torah it was given over to the Sages.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the hidden light is revealed to those who toil in the Oral Torah.”

1295.label: Pri Tzaddik, Bechukosai 13
1295.rest: — “As it says in the holy Zohar on the difference between the Ten Commandments, said in the singular, and their repetition in Kedoshim in the plural: ‘From the day Israel were in the world, they were not found before the Holy One with one heart and one will as on the day they stood at Mount Sinai, and therefore everything was said in the singular.’ That is, at Matan Torah it is written, ‘And Israel encamped,’ like one man, as it says in the Mechilta, and then they merited Matan Torah and the Ten Commandments in the singular.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other reading of “like one man with one heart” as the condition for the Torah given in the singular.

1296.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 40
1296.rest: — “On Shemini Atzeres it is written, ‘It shall be an atzeres for you,’ and here, ‘an atzeres to Hashem your God’… In Tanchuma (Pinchas 15) on Shemini Atzeres: ‘It should have been fifty days after the festival, just as Atzeres is fifty days after the festival, but the Holy One said, it is winter…’ It appears from this that Shavuos is like Shemini Atzeres after Sukkos.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “only the Sages call Shavuos ‘Atzeres’”; both join Shavuos to Pesach as Shemini Atzeres to Sukkos.

1297.label: Pri Tzaddik, Sukkos 43
1297.rest: — “In this parashah nothing of Shemini Atzeres is mentioned, only ‘You shall make the festival of Sukkos seven days, and you shall rejoice in your festival’… but the expression ‘and you shall be only joyful’ is an expression of promise.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “Shavuos after Pesach, like Shemini Atzeres after Sukkos”; both read Atzeres as the absorption of the festival's holiness.

1298.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 54
1298.rest: — “After a Jew is careful the whole festival with the least chametz and leaven, which alludes to the yetzer hara, the leaven in the dough (Berachos 17a), and counts the days of the Sefirah to be refined sevenfold in each middah, they merit through this each year Matan Torah as it was then, ‘I said: You are G-dly beings,’ for the first blemish has already been repaired. And then it is permitted to offer leaven on high; that is, the leaven is only what is ‘nicely diminished’ (Berachos 34a), what will remain of the yetzer hara even in the future.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other account of the leavened offering of Shavuos as the evil inclination nullified and made holy.

1299.label: Pri Tzaddik, Behar 1
1299.rest: — “All the mitzvos were said, their generalities, particulars and details, at Sinai, in the aspect of ‘the word of Hashem,’ and were repeated afterward in the Tent of Meeting, where it is written ‘And Hashem spoke to Moshe,’ and they are in the category of prophecy… And they were repeated a third time in the plains of Moav, which Moshe said on his own, even though it was the word of Hashem; still it was in the category of Kesuvim, said with ruach hakodesh.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “ruach hakodesh and the Oral Torah”; both divide the Torah's transmission into Torah, prophecy and ruach hakodesh.

1300.label: Pri Tzaddik, Shemos 3
1300.rest: — “Then came the rest, as it is written, ‘And they were completed… for on it He rested from all His work,’ for all creation found favor in His eyes and He had rest from it. And this is what it says (Rosh Hashanah 18a): ‘He Who fashions their hearts together’ — if you say it means He created them all and unites…” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other reading of Rosh Hashanah 18a on “He Who fashions their hearts together.”

1301.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeitzei 7
1301.rest: — “Just as the three middos of the holy Avos are the root of eternal life, so, one opposite the other, are the three opposite middos, jealousy, desire and honor, which take a person out of the world. Desire is the opposite of love, the Chesed of holiness, and this is Yishmael, the dross of Avraham…” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “Yaakov counters the evil inclination of pride”; both set jealousy, desire and honor against the three Avos.

1302.label: Pri Tzaddik, Toldos 3
1302.rest: — “There is a meal from the level of the sage, as it says in the holy Zohar (II 61b): ‘Higher than all is the nourishment of the companions… the nourishment of spirit and soul’… This is eating in holiness far more than a mitzvah… and it is called ‘the table that is before Hashem,’ which is like an actual offering. As we find (Berachos 10b): whoever hosts a Torah scholar in his home is as if he offered the daily offerings; and it says (Yoma 71a): whoever wishes to pour a libation of wine on the altar should fill the throats of Torah scholars with wine.” Connection: The same Gemaras on eating that is like an offering, the theme Rav Tzadok draws from “for you” on Atzeres.

1303.label: Pri Tzaddik, Noach 2
1303.rest: — “It is brought in the writings of the Arizal that the souls of Israel who were in Egypt in the crushing labor and who received the Torah were the souls of the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion, among whom there were great souls, only that good and evil were mixed together; for from eating of the Tree of Knowledge the mixture came also into the souls… until Avraham Avinu came and merited to be father to the souls of Israel, and then the souls were set apart.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other account of the setting apart of Israel's souls from the mixture, which he places at Sinai here.

1304.label: Pri Tzaddik, Yisro 6
1304.rest: — “At Matan Torah it says in the Gemara (Shabbos 88a): to each one of Israel they tied two crowns, one corresponding to ‘we will do’ and one to ‘we will hear’… and Moshe merited and took them all; and it is brought from the holy Arizal that on Shabbos Moshe Rabbeinu returns the crowns to Israel, and these are the crowns of Shabbos. And it says in the holy Zohar (II 80b), ‘And Israel were crowned with seventy crowns on that night.’” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the crown given to Israel at Mount Sinai, its meaning”; both explain the two crowns of Shabbos 88a.

1305.label: Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 10
1305.rest: — “According to what is said in the holy Zohar (III 261a): ‘What is “and the image”?… this is the inner voice…’ therefore the upper Hei is ‘a great voice that did not cease.’ And at Matan Torah it is written, ‘And all the people saw the thunders (kolos).’” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other treatment of the seen voices at Sinai through the Zohar's inner voice.

1306.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 1
1306.rest: — “We also find, ‘the kindness of the nations,’ that there is in them the attribute of Chesed, and this is from Yishmael, the dross of Avraham's Chesed… and the wisdom of Esav is from the dross of Yitzchak's Gevurah… And I have already spoken on what is written, ‘He shone forth from Seir and appeared from Mount Paran.’” Connection: Both read Devarim 33:2 as Torah's light drawn out of Seir and Paran, the husks of Esav and Yishmael.

1307.label: Pri Tzaddik, Korach 11
1307.rest: — “And Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him, who said, ‘And I am prayer,’ is the root of prayer, and the aspect of prayer is as one standing before the King; and he was a chariot for the attribute of Malchus, and Malchus is the mouth, which we call the Oral Torah. And the Arizal wrote that Dovid HaMelech was the head of the masters of ruach hakodesh.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “Dovid is the master of those with ruach hakodesh”; both bind Dovid to Malchus and the Oral Torah.

1308.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Elul 2
1308.rest: — “For this reason we say this psalm in the month of Elul… for in Elul one must repair his deeds so that sin not cause; for from Rosh Chodesh on begin the days of favor, when Moshe Rabbeinu went up to receive the second Tablets.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other treatment of the first and second Tablets, here set in Elul.

1309.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 25
1309.rest: — “The completion of the fruit is on Shavuos, the time of Matan Torah, of which it is written, ‘I said: You are G-dly beings,’ for they would not have died (Avodah Zarah 5a); and this is that they merited then the upper Shabbos, and the evil inclination departed from there (Tikkunei Zohar 48)… but after the corruption, ‘you have corrupted your deeds’…” Connection: The same verses, “I said: You are G-dly beings… you have corrupted your deeds,” read of Matan Torah and its loss.

1310.label: Pri Tzaddik, Motza'ei Yom Kippur 6
1310.rest: — “So too on Shavuos, the time of Matan Torah: only on that day is there the resting of the giving of the Written Torah; and even though they said (Sifrei, Eikev), ‘Every day let them be new in your eyes,’ that is another matter, for this is the power of the renewal of the Oral Torah, which is renewed every day in the souls of Israel, each according to his aspect.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “every year on Shavuos the merit is awakened to attain words of Torah from the side of the Tree of Life”; both separate the day of the Written Torah from the Oral Torah's daily renewal.

1311.label: Resisei Layla 53
1311.rest: — “Certainly the intent is the joy of Israel in Hashem their strength, as it is written, ‘Rejoice in Hashem and be glad, you righteous, and sing, all you upright of heart’ (Tehillim 32:11); and it is the joy of mitzvos and Torah, as it is written, ‘The precepts of Hashem are upright, gladdening the heart’ (Tehillim 19:9), for uprightness gives birth to joy in the heart.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other reading of “The precepts of Hashem are upright, gladdening the heart” as the joy that the yoke of Torah itself brings.

1312.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 1
