1312.rest: — “‘You gave Roshei Chodashim to Your people… a remembrance for them all.’ Rosh Hashanah is the day of the creation of Adam HaRishon, and the year is the circuit of the sun… and the renewal of the moon each month is the birth of the moon anew. Therefore every Rosh Chodesh is a remembrance of the creation of Adam HaRishon… and for this reason they increase prayers on Erev Rosh Chodesh and call it a minor Yom Kippur.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “Rosh Chodesh as a time of atonement and rectification of the sin of Adam and the serpent's venom.”

1313.label: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 13
1313.rest: — “In the Yerushalmi (end of Shekalim 3): piety brings to ruach hakodesh, as it is written, ‘Then You spoke in a vision to Your pious ones’; ruach hakodesh brings to the resurrection of the dead, as it is written, ‘And I will put My spirit in you and you shall live.’ And the intent is according to what it says (Kesubos 111b): ‘For Your dew is a dew of lights’ — whoever makes use of the light of Torah, the light of Torah revives him; that is, the dew of the Oral Torah, of which it says, ‘My word shall distill like the dew.’” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “resurrection of the dead through the dew of Atika.”

1314.label: Pri Tzaddik, Behar 2
1314.rest: — “From this we learn that the whole Torah was said, its generalities and details, at Sinai; for as long as there is a reality of evil in the world, the 613 kinds of counsel are needed to be saved from it.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other use of the Zohar's “613 kinds of counsel,” joined, as here, to the Torah needed while evil is still in the world.

1315.label: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 25
1315.rest: — “It would seem that the holiness of Shabbos should come first, for it is from Hashem's side, as it says, ‘to know that I, Hashem, sanctify you,’ and it is a holiness fixed and enduring from the six days of creation, which is not so with the holiness of the month, which Israel fix. But in the Gemara (Zevachim 91a) the mussafin of Rosh Chodesh are reckoned as sanctified over the mussafin of Shabbos, and Rashi wrote the reason, that they are more sanctified than those of Shabbos because it is called a mo'ed — and this is not understood.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “why from Israel's side Rosh Chodesh is holier than Shabbos”; the same question on Zevachim 91a.

1316.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Elul 1
1316.rest: — “Against this comes the mitzvah of the head-tefillin, which corresponds to Kesser, ‘we will hear’: that words of Torah enter the heart, as it says, ‘Hear, and your soul shall live,’ and it is written, ‘Guard your heart, for from it are the issues of life.’ And through words of Torah entering, one is saved from improper pride.” Connection: The same verses, “Hear, and your soul shall live” and “Guard your heart,” read as hearing that enters the heart.

1317.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Shevat 4
1317.rest: — “And the Arizal's version: ‘He made the letter tzaddi king over swallowing (le'itah), and Shevat in the year, and the gizzard in the soul,’ according to what it says (Berachos 61b), ‘the gizzard grinds’; that is, to repair…” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other treatment of “swallowing” in Sefer Yetzirah, here for Shevat; the two versions give swallowing to Av and to Shevat.

1318.label: Pri Tzaddik, Balak 14
1318.rest: — “The kidneys give counsel from afar, that is, from the root, as it says, ‘Behold, You desire truth in the inward parts, and in the hidden part You make me know wisdom’; for the counsel of the kidneys is from the root. And the Torah says, ‘Mine are counsel and sound wisdom’: through words of Torah one can also reach counsel from afar, from the root.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “counsel and wisdom that are in the kidneys”; both join the kidneys' counsel to “Mine are counsel and sound wisdom.”

1319.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 53
1319.rest: — “‘And Miriam the prophetess took the drum’: Rashi explains that the righteous women of the generation were confident… and took drums out of Egypt; and in the Mechilta: the righteous were confident and knew that the Holy One would do miracles and mighty acts for them… they prepared drums and dances (mecholos).” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other reading of the women's dances as an expression of confident faith, the dances that mark the Fifteenth of Av.

1320.label: Tzidkas HaTzaddik 34
1320.rest: — “‘The night was created only for sleep’ (Eruvin 65a), according to one opinion; and see the Tosafos there, that this means the nights of the season of Tammuz. And see Taanis 31a, that from the Fifteenth of Av one must add, that is, from half the season of Tammuz… after which the nights begin to grow longer.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's halachic-chronological reading of the same Gemara on adding nights to Torah from the Fifteenth of Av.

1321.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi 10
1321.rest: — “The Written Torah is like rain, ‘My lesson shall drop as the rain,’ for it is seen to come from heaven. But the Oral Torah is what the Sages renew in their hearts, and they are truly the words of the living God, and it is like dew, whose descent is not seen, only afterward moisture is seen on the ground; and this is ‘My word’ (imrasi), for amirah is in a whisper.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the main Torah study is by day, but because of the damage study at night was added”; both tie the night's Torah to the Oral Torah.

1322.label: Pri Tzaddik, Chayei Sarah 1
1322.rest: — “It is expounded in Midrash Tanchuma: ‘She will not fear for her household because of the snow,’ why? ‘For all her household is clothed in scarlet (shanim)’ — two (shnayim): Shabbos and milah. And even though everywhere it brings the fire of Gehinnom, here it calls it snow… And there is the husk of Amalek, of whom it says ‘who chilled you,’ who cooled you down; that is, he throws coldness and laziness upon a person, and this is the first of the husk.” Connection: The same verse of Eishes Chayil read against the coldness of Amalek, as in this maamar's white garments and scarlet.
